explanations.C: This is a true statement. Discounted cash flow models are used to evaluate proposed capital investment projects. Using discounted cash flows, a proposed project is acceptable if it has a positive net present value. The poorly performing unit will have a difficult time generating the required return on investment, which might reflect poorly on the abilities of the manager. And yet, a business unit that is performing poorly needs the skills of a good manager if it is to have any chance of turning around.

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: A company uses return on investment (ROI) to evaluate year-end divisional performance. Which one of the following inventory practices would most reduce comparability between two similar divisions?

options.A: One division uses the net method to record purchases and the other division uses the gross method to record purchases.
options.B: One division uses LIFO and the other division uses FIFO.
options.C: One division uses a perpetual inventory system and the other division uses a periodic inventory system.
options.D: One division places goods for sale on consignment and the other division does not.

correctExplanation: Any of the accounting policies for inventory listed has the potential to reduce comparability of ROI between two similar divisions. However, the accounting policy difference that would reduce comparability the most is a difference in cost flow assumptions used. ROI is the income of the business unit divided by the assets of the business unit. The inventory cost flow assumption used affects both the income of the business unit and the assets of the business unit. Assuming increasing costs, the use of LIFO will increase cost of goods sold, thereby decreasing net income while also decreasing total assets, because the units on hand in inventory will be costed at lower prices. The use of FIFO will decrease cost of goods sold, thereby increasing net income while also increasing total assets, because the units on hand in inventory will be costed at higher prices. The two ROIs would not be comparable because the bases on which they would be calculated would be different.

explanations.A: This difference would not reduce comparability between two similar divisions the most.
explanations.C: This difference would not reduce comparability between two similar divisions the most.
explanations.D: The practice of placing goods for sale on consignment by one division would not be the inventory practice from among the answer choices given that would most reduce the comparability between two otherwise similar divisions. Goods that are out on consignment still belong in the inventory of the consignor company because the ownership never transfers to the consignee. So the division that places their inventory in the hands of a consignee for sale still owns the inventory, and the inventory is still an asset on that division's balance sheet. The goods will be carried on the consignor’s balance sheet at the cost the consignor paid for the goods plus any shipping costs the consignor paid to get the goods to the consignee company that will sell the goods. The shipping costs to the consignee are costs of making the goods available for sale to the customer and thus are “inventoriable” costs. Thus, the only difference between the inventory cost for a division that places goods for sale on consignment and one that does not is the shipping costs to get the inventory to the consignee's location. The inventory cost for the division that places their inventory for sale on consignment would be a little higher than the inventory cost for the division that does not, but it would be only by the amount of the shipping costs to the consignee's location.

studyUnit: Study Unit 11: C.3. Performance Measures, ROI, and RI

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: Which one of the following firms is likely to experience dysfunctional motivation on the part of its managers due to its allocation methods?

options.A: Manhattan Electronics uses the sales revenue of its various divisions to allocate costs connected with the upkeep of its headquarters building. It also uses ROI to evaluate the divisional performances.
options.B: To allocate depreciation of forklifts used by workers at its central warehouse, Shahlimar Electronics uses predetermined amounts calculated on the basis of the long-term average use of the services provided.
options.C: Rainier Industrial does not allow its service departments to pass on their cost overruns to the production departments.
options.D: Tashkent Auto's MIS is operated out of headquarters and serves its various divisions. Tashkent's allocation of the MIS-related costs to its divisions is limited to costs the divisions will incur if they were to outsource their MIS needs.

correctExplanation: The question asks which allocation method would lead to negative (dysfunctional) behavior on the part of managers. If costs are allocated on the basis of sales revenue, a division with increased sales will receive more allocated costs. This could serve as a demotivator for the manager of the division with increased sales. Also, using ROI to measure divisional performance is probably not the best choice of method. Use of ROI to evaluate divisional performance could lead to managers' rejecting profitable new investments if the new investments' ROIs are lower than the divisions' historical ROIs, since the new investments could bring down their future ROIs.

explanations.B: The question asks which allocation method would lead to negative (dysfunctional) behavior on the part of managers. The allocation of costs based on usage is a reasonable method for the allocation of these costs and should not lead to dysfunctional motivation on the part of managers.
explanations.C: The question asks which allocation method would lead to negative (dysfunctional) behavior on the part of managers. Not allowing cost overruns in the service departments to be passed on to other departments will motivate the service departments to control their costs.
explanations.D: The question asks which allocation method would lead to negative (dysfunctional) behavior on the part of managers. By allocating costs equal to the market value of the services provided, the management of the divisions will use the MIS services available internally rather than outsourcing their MIS needs. Utilizing services available internally normally is preferable to outsourcing.

studyUnit: Study Unit 11: C.3. Performance Measures, ROI, and RI

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: Which statement below best represents a benefit of residual income (RI) as a performance measure?

options.A: Managers maximize an absolute amount and invest as long as the required return is earned.
options.B: RI blends all ingredients of profitability into one percentage that is easily comparable.
options.C: RI is more likely to promote goal congruence in a low profit location versus return on investment.
options.D: Managers can increase their RI by decreasing the internal rate of return.

correctExplanation: Residual income is an absolute amount. It is the amount of annual monetary return in the form of operating income that is in excess of a required monetary amount of return on the unit’s assets. The formula for residual income is: Annual operating income of business unit − (Assets of business unit x required rate of return = Resudual income of business unit When RI is used to evaluate manager and segment performance, a project that would be beneficial to the company is more likely to be selected, because as long as the RI for a project under consideration is positive, managers will invest in the project, even if its ROI is lower than the unit’s current ROI.

explanations.B: Residual income is not expressed as a percentage. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.C: Residual income is an absolute amount. It is the amount of annual monetary return in the form of operating income that is in excess of a required monetary amount of return on the unit’s assets. RI is more likely than ROI to promote goal congruence, but not specifically in a low profit location or situation. RI is more likely than ROI to promote goal congruence because as long as the RI for a project under consideration is positive, managers will invest in the project, even if its ROI is lower than the unit’s current ROI; and the investment will benefit the company. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.D: The internal rate of return is a discounted cash flow method of evaluating capital investment projects, and it is covered in the HOCK study materials CMA Part 2 exam. Decreasing the internal rate of return for a project is not a means of increasing the project’s RI.

studyUnit: Study Unit 11: C.3. Performance Measures, ROI, and RI

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: The segment margin of an investment center after deducting the imputed interest on the assets used by the investment center is known as

options.A: Return on investment.
options.B: Residual income.
options.C: Return on assets.
options.D: Operating income.

correctExplanation: Residual income is the amount of return after a certain required return on the assets in use by the division. The calculation of the required return is based on an imputed interest rate for the cost of funds represented by the assets in use. This describes the situation in the question.

explanations.A: Return on investment is calculated as income divided by the invested amount. There is no deduction of an imputed interest rate in the calculation of return on investment.
explanations.C: Return on assets does not take into account the imputed interest rate on the assets of the investment center. See the correct answer for a complete explanation.
explanations.D: Operating income does not take into account the imputed interest rate on the assets of the investment center. See the correct answer for a complete explanation.

studyUnit: Study Unit 11: C.3. Performance Measures, ROI, and RI

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: A company is considering the addition of a new product line. The new product line is expected to generate a return higher than the cost of capital, but lower than the current overall return on investment (ROI). If the company decides to add the potential new product line, residual income will

options.A: increase.
options.B: decrease.
options.C: become higher than the firm’s return on investment.
options.D: remain unchanged.

correctExplanation: If the expected rate of return on a new investment is greater than the required rate of return (usually the cost of capital), residual income will increase, even if the expected return on the new investment is lower than the current return on investment.

explanations.B: If the expected rate of return on a new investment is greater than the required rate of return (usually the cost of capital), residual income will increase, even if the expected return on the new investment is lower than the current return on investment.
explanations.C: If the expected rate of return on a new investment is greater than the required rate of return (usually the cost of capital), residual income will increase, even if the expected return on the new investment is lower than the current return on investment.
explanations.D: If the expected rate of return on a new investment is greater than the required rate of return (usually the cost of capital), residual income will increase, even if the expected return on the new investment is lower than the current return on investment.

studyUnit: Study Unit 11: C.3. Performance Measures, ROI, and RI

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: Residual income is a better measure for performance evaluation of an investment center manager than return on investment because

options.A: The problems associated with measuring the asset base are eliminated.
options.B: Returns do not increase as assets are depreciated.
options.C: Desirable investment decisions will not be neglected by high return divisions.
options.D: Only the gross book value of assets needs to be calculated.

correctExplanation: Residual income (RI) is calculated as the amount of return (operating income of a business unit) that is in excess of a targeted amount of return on the investments that are employed by that business unit (calculated as assets of the business unit multiplied by the required rate of return). RI is focused on the monetary amount of income that is in excess of a targeted amount. It is not focused on a percentage of return as ROI is. When using RI to evaluate investment opportunities, any project that has a positive RI will be accepted even if it will reduce the overall company's or business unit's ROI. Thus, desirable investment decisions will not be neglected by high return business units.

explanations.A: The asset base is total assets for both return on investment and residual income, and measuring it is usually not a problem.
explanations.B: The asset base is total assets for both return on investment and residual income. As fixed assets are depreciated, both methods will be affected.
explanations.D: The asset base is total assets for both return on investment and residual income. Furthermore, total assets includes the net book value of fixed assets, not the gross book value of fixed assets.

studyUnit: Study Unit 11: C.3. Performance Measures, ROI, and RI

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: A company uses return on investment (ROI) to measure the performance of its business units. The company manufactures and distributes consumer goods. Last year management identified a possible upcoming shortage of raw materials in its supply chain. To mitigate this risk, a large amount of raw material was bought in advance and stored in the manufacturing plant inventory. As a result of this decision ROI will

options.A: have an unpredictable change.
options.B: decrease.
options.C: not change.
options.D: increase.

correctExplanation: The large amount of raw material in inventory will cause assets to increase. ROI is annual income divided by assets. When assets increase, annual income is divided by a greater amount of assets in the denominator, which causes ROI to decrease.

explanations.A: The change in ROI is predictable. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.C: ROI will change as a result of the large amount of raw material in inventory. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.D: ROI will not increase as a result of the large amount of raw material in inventory. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

studyUnit: Study Unit 11: C.3. Performance Measures, ROI, and RI

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: A firm earning a profit can increase its return on investment by

options.A: Increasing sales revenue and operating expenses by the same dollar amount.
options.B: Increasing investment and operating expenses by the same dollar amount.
options.C: Decreasing sales revenues and operating expenses by the same percentage.
options.D: Increasing sales revenues and operating expenses by the same percentage.

correctExplanation: Since the firm is profitable, revenue is greater than expenses, so increasing both revenue and expenses by the same percentage will cause the increase in revenue to be larger than the increase in expenses. As a result, net income will increase and, since investment would not change, ROI will increase.

explanations.A: Increasing sales revenue and operating expenses by the same dollar amount will cause net income to remain unchanged and so will not change the ROI of the company.
explanations.B: One way to solve this problem is to simply set up a basic ROI of, for example, $100,000 of profit / $400,000 total assets giving a ROI of 0.25 and then go through the choices changing these figures as outlined in each option. In this choice we should increase the investment (the denominator) and expenses (which will decrease income) by the same amount. Let us assume that this amount is $50,000. That would make the ROI calculation $50,000 ÷ $450,000, which is 0.111, or a decrease in the ROI.
explanations.C: Decreasing sales will decrease income and decreasing expenses will increase income. Since the firm is profitable, income is greater than expenses, so decreasing both income and expenses by the same percentage will cause the decrease in income to be larger than the decrease in expenses. As a result, net income will decline and, since investment would not change, ROI will decrease.

studyUnit: Study Unit 11: C.3. Performance Measures, ROI, and RI

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: For several years, Northern Division of Marino Company has maintained a positive residual income. Northern is currently considering investing in a new project that will lower the division’s overall return on investment (ROI) but increase its residual income. What is the relationship between the expected rate of return on the new project, the firm’s cost of capital, and the division’s current ROI?

options.A: The expected rate of return on the new project is higher than the division's current ROI but lower than the firm's cost of capital.
options.B: The expected rate of return on the new project is higher than the firm's cost of capital but lower than the division's current ROI.
options.C: The firm's cost of capital is higher than the expected rate of return on the new project but lower than the division's current ROI.
options.D: The division's current ROI is higher than the expected rate of return on the new project but lower than the firm's cost of capital.

correctExplanation: Since the required rate of return on the project is not given, the cost of capital is used as the required rate of return. The expected rate of return on the new project must be higher than the firm’s cost of capital/required rate of return, because the project will increase the division’s residual income, which is positive. If the expected rate of return were lower than the firm’s cost of capital, residual income would decrease and the firm would lose money on the project because the financing for the project (the cost of capital) would cost more than the project would earn. The expected rate of return on the new project is lower than the division’s overall ROI, because the new project will lower the division’s overall ROI.

explanations.A: Since the required rate of return on the project is not given, the cost of capital is used as the required rate of return. The new project will lower the division’s overall return on investment, so the expected rate of return on the new project must be lower than the division's current ROI, not higher. Because the proposed project will increase residual income, which is positive, the expected rate of return on the new project cannot be lower than the firm’s cost of capital/required rate of return. If it were, residual income would decrease, not increase, and the firm would lose money on the project because the financing for the project (the cost of capital) would cost more than the project would earn.
explanations.C: Since the required rate of return on the project is not given, the cost of capital is used as the required rate of return. Because the proposed project will increase the firm's residual income, which is positive, the firm's cost of capital/required rate of return cannot be higher than the expected rate of return on the project. If it were, residual income would decrease, not increase, and the firm would lose money on the project because the financing for the project (the cost of capital) would cost more than the project could earn.
explanations.D: Since the required rate of return on the project is not given, the cost of capital is used as the required rate of return. The division’s current ROI is higher than the expected rate of return on the new project, because the investment in the new project will lower the division’s overall ROI. However, the division's ROI cannot be lower than the firm's cost of capital/required rate of return. Since the division is maintaining a positive residual income, its ROI must be higher than the firm's cost of capital, not lower.

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: Performance results for four geographic divisions of a manufacturing company are shown below. Division Target Return on Investment Actual Return on Investment Return on Sales A 18% 18.1% 8% B 16% 20.0% 8% C 14% 15.8% 6% D 12% 11.0% 9% The division with the best performance is

tail: The division with the best performance is

options.A: Division C.
options.B: Division A.
options.C: Division D.

In addition, among the divisions that exceeded their targets, Division B had one of the highest returns on sales. (Division D had a higher return on sales, but Division D did not exceed its target return on investment.) Therefore, Division B is the division with the best overall performance.

However, it did not exceed its target return on investment by as much as some other divisions did. Therefore, it cannot qualify as the division with the best performance.

studyUnit: Study Unit 11: C.3. Performance Measures, ROI, and RI

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: Listed below is selected financial information for the Western Division of the Hinzel Company for last year. Account Amount (thousands) Current assets $ 625 General and administrative expenses 75 Net sales 4,000 Property, plant, and equipment 1,775 Cost of goods sold 3,525 If Hinzel treats the Western Division as an investment center for performance measurement purposes, what is the division's return on investment (ROI) for last year?
intro: Listed below is selected financial information for the Western Division of the Hinzel Company for last year. Account Amount (thousands)
tail: If Hinzel treats the Western Division as an investment center for performance measurement purposes, what is the division's return on investment (ROI) for last year?
correctExplanation: ROI is calculated as operating income of the business unit divided by total assets (or investments) of the business unit. Operating income equals net sales minus COGS and G&A expenses, or $400,000 ($4,000,000 − $3,525,000 − $75,000). Total assets are equal to the sum of current assets and property, plant, and equipment, or $2,400,000 ($625,000 + $1,775,000). ROI thus equals $400,000 ÷ $2,400,000 = 16.67%. Note that usually average total assets would be used to calculate ROI. Assuming the information on assets given in the question is year-end balances and not average balances, information on average total assets is not available and cannot be calculated from the information given, so the information that is available is used.

explanations.A: ROI is calculated as operating income of the business unit divided by total assets (or investments) of the business unit. This answer results from failing to deduct the general and administrative costs in calculating operating income.
explanations.B: ROI is calculated as operating income of the business unit divided by total assets (or investments) of the business unit. This answer results from dividing operating income by property, plant, and equipment. Current assets should be included in total assets.
explanations.D: ROI is calculated as operating income of the business unit divided by average total assets (or investments) of the business unit. This answer results from dividing operating income by property, plant, and equipment less current assets. The denominator should be current assets plus property, plant, and equipment, not property, plant, and equipment minus current assets.

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: Teen Styles, a merchandising company, is considering a $1,000,000 upgrade to its retail and warehousing facilities that will allow the company to handle more products and attract more customers. Teen Styles anticipates that sales will increase by $500,000, and operating income will increase by $200,000 per year. If Teen Styles has a minimum required return on investment of 15%, what would be the residual income resulting from the upgrade?
correctExplanation: Residual income is Operating Income minus (Assets × Required rate of return). When evaluating a project, the incremental amounts of operating income and assets attributable to the project should be used. Projected incremental annual operating income is $200,000. The $1,000,000 investment multiplied by the 15% required rate of return is $150,000. Annual operating income of $200,000 minus $150,000 equals $50,000.

explanations.A: $500,000 is the amount by which sales are expected to increase, not the residual income resulting from the upgrade. Residual income is Operating Income minus (Assets × Required rate of return). Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.B: $75,000 is the $500,000 by which sales are expected to increase multiplied by the 15% required rate of return. Residual income is Operating Income minus (Assets × Required rate of return). Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.C: $800,000 is the $1,000,000 investment minus the anticipated increase of $200,000 in operating income as a result of the project. Residual income is Operating Income minus (Assets × Required rate of return). Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: A company’s management is planning on making an investment of $800,000 to launch a new product. In the first year, the new product is expected to generate sales of $200,000 and a contribution margin of $175,000. Incremental fixed costs are $50,000. The company’s expected return on investment in the first year is closest to
correctExplanation: Return on investment for a specific investment is income expected to be generated by the investment divided by the investment. Income expected to be generated by the planned investment is the $175,000 increased contribution margin expected less the incremental fixed costs of $50,000, or $125,000. The amount invested is $800,000. Thus, return on investment is $125,000 divided by $800,000, which equals 0.15625 and is closest to 16%.

explanations.A: Return on investment for a specific investment is income expected to be generated by the investment divided by the investment. 22% is the sales expected to be generated by the investment divided by the investment.
explanations.C: Return on investment for a specific investment is income expected to be generated by the investment divided by the investment. 25% is the contribution margin expected to be generated by the investment divided by the investment.
explanations.D: Return on investment for a specific investment is income expected to be generated by the investment divided by the investment. 6% is the incremental fixed costs divided by the investment.

studyUnit: Study Unit 11: C.3. Performance Measures, ROI, and RI

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: The management team of a company is evaluating the use of either return on investment or residual income as a measure of the performance of the company’s lines of business. In a presentation about the two measures, which of the following statements are correct? I. Both measures include key elements such as revenues, costs, and level of investments, which are critical for top management decision making. II. Both measures avoid all potential goal-congruency problems within the organization. III. The only disadvantage of the measures is that they both have a long-term focus, rather than a short-term focus. IV. Both measures can be manipulated to suit the user’s purposes as the calculation is based on accounting numbers.

options.A: II and III only.
options.B: I and II only.
options.C: III and IV only.
options.D: I and IV only.

correctExplanation: Statements I and IV are correct. Both ROI and RI utilize revenues, costs, and level of investments and are critical for decision-making (I). Both can be manipulated because they are both based on accounting numbers, and accounting numbers can be manipulated (IV). Nowever, II and III are not correct: Neither ROI nor RI avoids all of the goal congruency issues in a company (II). ROI and RI both have a short-term, rather than a long-term focus (III).

explanations.A: Neither II nor III is correct: Neither ROI nor RI avoids all of the goal congruency issues in a company (II). ROI and RI both have a short-term, rather than a long-term focus (III). Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.B: II is not correct because neither ROI nor RI avoids all of the goal congruency issues in a company. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.C: III is not correct because ROI and RI both have a short-term, rather than a long-term focus. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

studyUnit: Study Unit 11: C.3. Performance Measures, ROI, and RI

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: KHD Industries is a multidivisional firm that evaluates its managers based on the return on investment (ROI) earned by their divisions. The evaluation and compensation plans use a targeted ROI of 15% (equal to the cost of capital) and managers receive a bonus of 5% of basic compensation for every one-percentage point that the division's ROI exceeds 15%. David Evans, manager of the Consumer Products Division, has made a forecast of the division's operations and finances for next year that indicates the ROI would be 24%. In addition, new short-term programs were identified by the Consumer Products Division and evaluated by the finance staff as follows. Program Projected ROI A 13% B 19% C 22% D 31% Assuming no restrictions on expenditures, what is the optimal mix of new programs that would add value to KHD Industries?

options.A: C and D only.
options.B: D only.
options.C: A, B, C, and D.
options.D: B, C, and D only.

correctExplanation: Programs B, C and D have projected ROIs that are higher than the firm's 15% cost of capital. Therefore, assuming no restrictions on expenditures, all three of those programs would add value to KHD Industries. Note that the problem asks for which programs would add value to the company, not which programs would maximize the manager's bonus. If, as the manager projects, the company does earn an ROI equal to 24% on operations other than these new programs next year, then the addition of B and C would cause the division's ROI to decrease because their individual projected ROIs are below 24%. That would, in turn, cause the manager's bonus to be lower than it would be with a 24% or higher ROI. However, since the projected ROIs for B and C are higher than the company's cost of capital, those programs should be undertaken since they will add value to the company.

explanations.A: C and D are not the only programs that would add value to KHD Industries. All programs with projected ROIs that are higher than the firm's cost of capital will add value.
explanations.B: D is the only program with a projected ROI that is higher than the manager's projection of the division's ROI excluding the new programs. Thus, it is the only program that would increase overall ROI for the division above 24% and thus increase the manager's bonus. Due to the way the manager's bonus is determined, the manager may be tempted to undertake program D only. However, the question does not ask which program(s) would increase the manager's bonus. It asks which programs would add value to the company as a whole. There are other programs that would add value to the company as a whole although they would not increase the manager's bonus.
explanations.C: Not all of the programs will add value to KHD Industries. Only the programs with projected ROIs that are higher than the firm's cost of capital will add value.

studyUnit: Study Unit 11: C.3. Performance Measures, ROI, and RI

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: Fabro Inc. produced 1,500 units of Product RX-6 last week. The inputs to the production process for Product RX-6 were as follows: 450 pounds of Material A at a cost of $1.50 per pound 300 pounds of Material Z at a cost of $2.75 per pound 300 labor hours at a cost of $15.00 per hour What is the best productivity measure for the first-line supervisor in Fabro Inc.'s production plant?

options.A: 5.00 units per labor hour.
options.B: 0.33 units per dollar input.
options.C: $15.00 per labor hour.
options.D: $2.00 per pound.

correctExplanation: The first-line supervisor is usually responsible for productivity in terms of the number of units produced during the period. He or she cannot control the price of inputs (materials, labor). Thus, the best productivity measure for the first-line supervisor is the units produced per labor hour, which is 5.00 units per labor hour (1,500 units ÷ 300 labor hours).

explanations.B: This is the units produced per dollar of labor used. This is not the best productivity measure for the first-line supervisor because the first-line supervisor does not control the labor rates and his or her performance should not be measured on that basis.
explanations.C: This is the labor rate. This is not the best productivity measure for the first-line supervisor because the first-line supervisor does not control the labor rates and his or her performance should not be measured on that basis.
explanations.D: This is the weighted average price per pound of the two materials used in the production of Product RX-6. This is not the best productivity measure for the first-line supervisor because the first-line supervisor does not control the price and his or her performance should not be measured on that basis.

studyUnit: Study Unit 11: C.3. Performance Measures, ROI, and RI

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: Oakmont Company has two divisions: Household Appliances and Construction Equipment. The manager of the Household Appliances Division is evaluated on the basis of return on investment (ROI). The manager of the Construction Equipment Division is evaluated on the basis of residual income. The cost of capital has been 12% and the ROI has been 16% for the two divisions. Each manager is currently considering a project with a 14% rate of return. According to the current evaluation system for managers, which manager(s) would have an incentive to undertake the project?

options.A: Both managers would have an incentive to undertake the project.
options.B: Neither manager would have an incentive to undertake the project.
options.C: The manager of the Household Appliances Division would have an incentive to undertake the project while the manager of the Construction Equipment Division would not have an incentive to undertake the project.
options.D: The manager of the Construction Equipment Division would have an incentive to undertake the project while the manager of the Household Appliances Division would not have an incentive to undertake the project.

correctExplanation: The manager of the Construction Equipment Division would have an incentive to undertake the project because the manager is evaluated on the basis of residual income, and a project with a 14% rate of return would increase residual income. The manager of the Household Appliances Division would not have an incentive to undertake the project because the manager is evaluated on the basis of return on investment, and a project with a 14% rate of return would decrease the 16% return on investment the division is currently achieving. However, since both projects have rates of return that are greater than the company's cost of capital, both projects will increase the value of the company, so both should be accepted by their respective managers.

explanations.C: The manager of the Household Appliances Division would not have an incentive to undertake the project because the manager is evaluated on the basis of return on investment, and a project with a 14% rate of return would decrease the 16% return on investment the division is currently achieving. question: James Webb is the general manager of the Industrial Product Division, and his performance is measured using the residual income method. intro: James Webb is the general manager of the Industrial Product Division, and his performance is measured using the residual income method. Webb is reviewing the following forecasted information for his division for next year: Category Amount (thousands)
tail: If the imputed interest charge is 15% and Webb wants to achieve a residual income target of $2,000,000, what will operating expenses need to be in order to achieve the target residual income?
correctExplanation: Residual income is equal to operating income of the business unit minus an imputed interest charge equal to the assets of the business unit multiplied by the required rate of return. The formula for Residual Income is: Operating income of business unit − (Assets of business unit × required rate of return) = Residual Income Since operating income is not given, it must be "backed into" by starting with the required residual income. Once the target operating income has been calculated, then operating expense can be "backed into" by using the revenue given and the target operating income that results in residual income of $2,000,000. Total assets of the business unit are equal to the sum of current assets and noncurrent assets. Noncurrent assets are represented in this question as property, plant, and equipment. Thus, total assets equal $19,000,000 ($1,800,000 + $17,200,000). Hence, the imputed interest charge is $2,850,000 ($19,000,000 × 15%). In order to achieve the target residual income of $2,000,000, operating income needs to be equal to the sum of the imputed interest charge and the target amount of residual income, or $4,850,000 ($2,850,000 + $2,000,000). Thus, operating expense will need to be equal to the revenue minus the target operating income, or $25,150,000 ($30,000,000 − $4,850,000).

The formula for Residual Income is: Operating income of business unit − (Assets of business unit × required rate of return) = Residual Income Since operating income is not given, it must be "backed into" by starting with the required residual income of $2,000,000 and using the imputed interest charge, calculated as the assets of the business unit multiplied by the required rate of return. After the target operating income has been calculated, then operating expense can be "backed into" by using the revenue given and the target operating income that results in residual income of $2,000,000. topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: The most likely reason a company would switch its performance measurement tool from ROI to RI is because

options.A: ROI favors large units.
options.B: RI provides a basis to evaluate units with different sizes.
options.C: goal-congruency will be better achieved.
options.D: RI incorporates nonfinancial factors.

correctExplanation: Goal-congruency refers to the aligning of goals of the individual managers with the goals of the whole organization. An individual division manager may reject a capital investment that would improve the company’s total profits because the proposed project’s return on investment would cause his own division’s return on investment to decrease. But since the investment would improve the company’s overall profit, the proposed project should be accepted. If the expected rate of return on a new investment is greater than the required rate of return (usually the cost of capital), residual income (RI) will increase due to the new investment, even if the expected return on investment (ROI) for the new project is lower than the current return on investment. An investment that may have been rejected on the basis that its ROI was lower than the unit’s existing ROI would instead be accepted, and the company would benefit from the new investment. Therefore, when RI is used in preference to ROI, a project that would be beneficial to the company is more likely to be selected, even if its ROI is lower than the unit’s existing ROI, and goal-congruency will be better achieved.

explanations.A: ROI does not favor large units. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.B: RI does not provide a basis to evaluate units with different sizes. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.D: RI does not incorporate nonfinancial factors. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

question: After investing in a new project, Lee Company discovered that its residual income remained unchanged. Which one of the following must be true about the new project?

options.B: The net present value of the new project must have been positive.
options.C: The net present value of the new project must have been negative.
options.D: The return on investment of the new project must have been less than the firm’s cost of capital.

correctExplanation: If the overall company’s residual income remains unchanged after the company has invested in a new project, the residual income of the new project must be zero. Residual income of zero for a project can occur only when the return on investment of the new addition is equal to the company’s cost of capital.

explanations.B: If the overall company’s residual income remains unchanged after the company has invested in a new project, it does not mean that the net present value of the new project must have been positive. The net present value of a project is not relevant to the calculation of residual income. The net present value (NPV) method of capital investment analysis is covered on the CMA Part 2 exam. It is based on the present value of the future expected after-tax net cash flows from a project. All expected future cash inflows and outflows are discounted to the beginning of the project using the required rate of return. The NPV of an investment or project is the difference between the present value of all future expected after-tax net cash inflows and the present value of all (initial and future) expected net after-tax cash outflows, using the required rate of return. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

question: A company has recently implemented responsibility accounting in all 7 segments of the company. The following information is available for Segment W for the last quarter. intro: A company has recently implemented responsibility accounting in all 7 segments of the company. The following information is available for Segment W for the last quarter.
tail: Based on the information provided, if the company treats Segment W as an investment center, what is the annual return on investment for Segment W?
correctExplanation: Annual return on investment is calculated as the annual return, or income, of the segment, divided by the assets invested in the segment. When the income and the assets are for one quarter, the income is annualized before dividing it by the quarter's invested assets. The income of the segment for the quarter is calculated as the revenues ($8,000,000) minus cost of sales ($6,350,000) minus general and administrative expenses ($180,000) for a quarterly return of $1,470,000. The annualized return is $1,470,000 × 4 = $5,880,000. The total of assets invested in the segment is not provided. The only way to derive it from the information that is provided is to sum net working capital ($12,000,000) and net property, plant and equipment ($31,750,000), and use the sum as total invested assets even though net working capital is not the same thing as current assets. (Net working capital is current assets minus current liabilities.) The sum of net working capital and PP&E is $43,750,000. Annual ROI is thus calculated as $5,880,000 ÷ $43,750,000 = 13.44%.

explanations.A: Annual return on investment is calculated as the annual return, or income, of the segment, divided by the assets invested in the segment. When the income and the assets are for one quarter, the income is annualized before dividing it by the quarter's invested assets. This answer does not include the general and administrative expenses in the calculation of the annual return of the segment. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.B: Annual return on investment is calculated as the annual return, or income, of the segment, divided by the assets invested in the segment. When the income and the assets are for one quarter, the income is annualized before dividing it by the quarter's invested assets. This answer does not include the net working capital in the calculation of the amount invested in the segment. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.C: Annual return on investment is calculated as the annual return, or income, of the segment, divided by the assets invested in the segment. When the income and the assets are for one quarter, the income should be annualized before dividing it by the quarter's invested assets. This answer results from not annualizing the segment's quarterly income before dividing it by the assets invested in the segment. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

studyUnit: Study Unit 11: C.3. Performance Measures, ROI, and RI

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: A company is concerned that its divisional managers are not making decisions that are in the best interests of the overall corporation. In order to prevent this, the company should use a performance evaluation system that focuses on

options.A: operating income.
options.B: residual income.
options.C: flexible budget variances.
options.D: controllable costs.

correctExplanation: When division managers are evaluated on the basis of residual income, they are more likely to embark upon projects that will be in the best interests of the overall corporation. Residual income is not a rate, but instead, it is an amount of income. As long as the expected net income before taxes from the project is greater than the target monetary return in (calculated as a percentage of invested capital), the project will be in the best interests of the overall corporation and it will also have positive residual income. Using residual income overcomes a weakness inherent in using return on investment for manager evaluation. If return on investment is used, a project that would have a higher return than the company's cost of capital and thus would be good for the company may be rejected by the division manager because its return on investment is lower than the division's current return on investment and thus it would bring the division's return on investment down.

explanations.A: A performance evaluation system that focuses on operating income would not necessarily encourage divisional managers to make decisions that are in the best interests of the company.
explanations.C: A performance evaluation system that focuses on flexible budget variances would not necessarily encourage divisional managers to make decisions that are in the best interests of the company.
explanations.D: A performance evaluation system that focuses on controllable costs would not necessarily encourage divisional managers to make decisions that are in the best interests of the company.

question: A corporation has set a goal to increase its return on investment (ROI). To facilitate this goal the corporation has set up an incentive program that rewards each division for increasing their ROI. One possible downfall of this incentive program is that it will

options.B: cause the corporation to pay out incentives if goals are achieved.
options.C: result in managers rejecting profitable projects.
options.D: cause the corporation to select high-risk investments.

correctExplanation: Any project with a return higher than the company’s required rate of return will increase the company’s net profit. However, a project with a return higher than the company’s required rate of return may reduce the division’s ROI if the division’s current ROI is higher than the expected ROI of the new project. The outcome may be that a division manager will reject a project that would have been beneficial to the overall company because it would have lowered that division’s ROI.

explanations.A: There is no reason why incentives to increase ROI should cause division managers to compete for the corporation’s investment funds. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.B: If the corporation promises incentives and then keeps that promise, that is not a downfall of the incentive program. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.D: Although potentially higher returns normally are associated with higher risk, there is no reason to expect incentives for increasing ROI to cause the corporation to select high-risk investments, because along with potentially higher returns, there would be the potential for higher losses, as well. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

The required rate of return may be determined based prior experience, the cost of capital, or any other estimation depending on management's decision. The formula for Residual Income is: Operating income of business unit − (Assets of business unit × required rate of return) = Residual Income

studyUnit: Study Unit 11: C.3. Performance Measures, ROI, and RI

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: A company expects to have assets of $825,000 and net operating income of $230,000 next year. In addition, the company is evaluating an investment opportunity that requires an initial investment of $160,000 and is expected to generate $180,000 of sales annually. The investment will have a 70% contribution margin ratio and $42,000 fixed costs. The company’s minimum required rate of return is 14%. What would be the residual income next year if the company proceeds with the investment opportunity?
correctExplanation: Residual income is: Operating income of business unit − Assets of business unit × required rate of return = Residual income Operating income next year is expected to be $230,000. If the company proceeds with the investment opportunity, the new investment is expected to add $84,000 to operating income, as follows: Sales - new investment $180,000 − Variable cost of sales - new investment $180,000 × (1 − 0.70) 54,000 − Fixed costs - new investment 42,000 = Operating income - new investment $ 84,000 Therefore, operating income next year with the new investment is expected to be $230,000 + $84,000, or $314,000. Assets next year are expected to be $825,000. If the company proceeds with the investment opportunity, new assets of $160,000 will be added, for total assets of $985,000. $985,000 multiplied by the required rate of return of 14% equals $137,900. Residual income next year if the company proceeds with the investment opportunity is thus expected to be $314,000 − $137,900 = $176,100.

explanations.A: This is the residual income related to the new investment only. Residual income next year if the company proceeds with the investment opportunity should include both the expected income and assets without the new investment and the expected income and assets if the company proceeds with the new investment. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.C: This is the expected operating income next year if the company proceeds with the investment opportunity, but it is not residual income. Residual income is: Operating income of business unit − Assets of business unit × required rate of return = Residual income Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.D: This is residual income expected next year if the company does not proceed with the investment opportunity. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: Return on investment focuses on income as a percentage of investment, while residual income focuses on

options.A: management decisions.
options.B: operating income less a capital charge.
options.C: cost of capital times the amount of investment.
options.D: the capital charge.

correctExplanation: A business unit's residual income is the business unit’s actual operating income minus its target operating income (target return), or capital charge. The target return is the assets of the business unit multiplied by the unit's required rate of return. Residual income is Operating income of the business unit − (Assets of business unit × required rate of return) = Residual Income

explanations.A: Residual income does not focus on management decisions. Residual Income is a business unit’s actual operating income minus its target operating income (target return). Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.C: The cost of capital (or the required rate of return) times the amount of investment is a component of the calculation of residual income, but residual income does not focus on that. Residual Income is a business unit’s actual operating income minus its target operating income (target return). Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.D: The capital charge is a component of the calculation of residual income, but residual income does not focus on the capital charge. Residual Income is a business unit’s actual operating income minus its target operating income (target return). Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: An industrial conglomerate acquires minority holdings in companies that operate in capital-intensive industries. The company evaluates its holdings by comparing its annual return on investment against the average of its respective industries. These comparisons will be valid as long as the companies being compared apply similar revenue and expense recognition policies because the use of different acceptable policies might

options.A: cause timing differences in income recognition.
options.B: overstate overall income and therefore impair the comparability.
options.C: distort the comparability of ratios due to changes in cash flows.
options.D: result in higher overall income if aggressive policies are used.

correctExplanation: Accounting profit depends on assumptions and estimates made, as well as principles applied. A company’s management may be either aggressive or conservative in its selection of generally accepted accounting principles. The use of aggressive rather than conservative accounting policies causes net income to be recognized earlier, leading to higher earnings and higher book values in the short run. However, all costs eventually flow through the income statement, and the choice of accounting policies merely creates differences in timing. For the company using aggressive policies, later periods' earnings will be lower than they would have been for the same company using conservative accounting policy choices.

explanations.B: The use of different acceptable accounting policies would not overstate overall income. Accounting profit depends on assumptions and estimates made, as well as principles applied. A company’s management may be either aggressive or conservative in its selection of generally accepted accounting principles. The use of aggressive rather than conservative accounting policies causes net income to be recognized earlier, leading to higher earnings and higher book values in the short run. However, all costs eventually flow through the income statement, and the choice of accounting policies merely creates differences in timing. For the company using aggressive policies, later periods' earnings will be lower than they would have been for the same company using conservative accounting policy choices.
explanations.C: The use of different acceptable accounting policies does not cause changes in cash flows. The amount of cash that comes in and the amount of cash that goes out are not affected by the revenue and expense recognition policies chosen by management. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.D: The use of aggressive accounting policy choices does not result in higher overall income, but rather earlier recognition of income. For the company using aggressive policies, later periods' earnings will be lower than they would have been for the same company using conservative accounting policy choices.

studyUnit: Study Unit 11: C.3. Performance Measures, ROI, and RI

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: The required rate of return used in the residual income approach to performance evaluation can best be described as the:

options.A: Average return-on-investments for the company over the last several years.
options.B: Target return-on-investment set by the company’s management.
options.C: Historical weighted-average cost of capital for the company.
options.D: Average lending rate for the year being evaluated.

correctExplanation: The required rate of return used in calculating Residual Income is an interest rate assigned by management. It is the rate of return that management desires. It is not a cash interest charge but rather it is an interest charge that is assigned for the purpose of analysis. The required rate of return may be the company’s weighted average cost of capital, or it may be another rate.

explanations.A: Though the required rate of return may be the average return-on-investments for the company over the last several years, this is not the best description of the required rate of return.
explanations.C: Though the required rate of return may be the historical weighted-average cost of capital for the company, this is not the best description of the required rate of return.
explanations.D: Though the required rate of return may be the average lending rate for the year being evaluated, this is not the best description of the required rate of return.

studyUnit: Study Unit 11: C.3. Performance Measures, ROI, and RI

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: A company’s management is planning on making an investment of UAE Dirham (AED) 1,000,000 to establish a new division in the United Arab Emirates. The new division is expected to generate sales of AED 720,000 and net income of AED 250,000 in Year 1. If the company’s required rate of return is 10%, what is the division’s residual income in Year 1?
correctExplanation: Residual income is the amount by which income exceeds a certain target level of income, which is the company's required rate of return on the invested capital. In this question, the target level is 10% of AED 1,000,000, or AED 100,000. RI = 250,000 − (1,000,000 × 0.10) = 150,000 A net income of AED 250,000 provides a residual income of AED 150,000.

explanations.B: This is the amount of target income for the company. It is used to calculate residual income, but it is not the amount of residual income. Residual income is the amount by which income exceeds the target level of income. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.C: This is the expected sales revenue of AED 720,000 minus the target level of income, which is the required rate of return on the amount invested. Residual income is the amount by which income exceeds the target level of income. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.D: This is the expected operating income of AED 250,000 less 10% of the expected operating income (25,000). Residual income is the amount by which income exceeds the target level of income, which is the company's required rate of return on the invested capital. Here, the target level is 10% of the AED 1,000,000 invested, or AED 100,000. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

studyUnit: Study Unit 11: C.3. Performance Measures, ROI, and RI

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: One approach to measuring divisional performance is return on investment. Return on investment is expressed as operating income:

options.A: Divided by fixed assets.
options.B: Divided by the current year's capital expenditures plus cost of capital.
options.C: Minus imputed interest charged for invested capital.
options.D: Divided by total assets.

correctExplanation: The formula for an individual division's return on investment is its operating income divided by its total assets.

explanations.A: The formula for an individual division's return on investment is not its operating income divided by its fixed assets. The divisor in the ROI calculation needs to include more than just fixed assets.
explanations.B: The formula for an individual division's return on investment is not its operating income divided by the current year's capital expenditures plus cost of capital. The divisor in the ROI calculation needs to include more than just the current year's capital expenditures, and the cost of capital is not used in the calculation of return on investment.
explanations.C: The formula for an individual division's return on investment is not its operating income minus imputed interest charged for invested capital. Operating income minus imputed interest charged for invested capital describes residual income.

studyUnit: Study Unit 11: C.3. Performance Measures, ROI, and RI

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: Residual income is often preferred over return on investment (ROI) as a performance evaluation measure because

options.A: residual income is a measure over time while ROI represents the results for a single time period.
options.B: residual income concentrates on maximizing the amount of income rather than a percentage return as with ROI.
options.C: the imputed interest rate used in calculating residual income is more easily derived than the target rate that is compared to the calculated ROI.
options.D: average investment is employed with residual income while year-end investment is employed with ROI.

correctExplanation: Residual income is the operating income earned after the the required charge for the funds invested by the company in its operations (usually the cost of capital) has been covered. If the expected rate of return on a new investment is greater than the required rate of return, residual income will increase as a result of the new investment even if the expected return on investment (ROI) for the new project is lower than the division's current return on investment. When evaluating a potential project for investment, any project that has a positive RI will be accepted, even if it will reduce the overall company’s or unit’s ROI. Therefore, an investment that may have been rejected on the basis that its ROI was lower than the existing ROI would instead be accepted, and the company would benefit from the new investment.

explanations.A: Both residual income and return on investment are related to a single time period, but residual income is a monetary amount whereas return on investment is a percentage return amount. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.C: The imputed interest rate used in calculating residual income is the organization's required rate of return, and the same required rate of return is used to evaluate return on investment. The required rate of return is determined by senior management. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.D: Either average investment or year-end investment may be used to evaluate both residual income and return on investment. In practice, accountants use the average of the beginning and ending balances of the year for total assets in calculating ROI and residual income. However, HOCK has been informed by the ICMA that the CMA Part 1 exam questions will not require candidates to use an average of the employed assets of the business unit. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

studyUnit: Study Unit 11: C.3. Performance Measures, ROI, and RI

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: Ramirez Inc. opens a new retail store every two years and currently operates in 24 different locations. Ramirez uses return on investment (ROI) to evaluate store performance. The best comparison among stores will be achieved if Ramirez values long-term assets at their

options.A: historical cost.
options.B: book values.
options.C: historical cost adjusted for inflation.
options.D: fair values.

correctExplanation: ROI is annual income of a business unit divided by assets of the business unit. Different methods of depreciating fixed assets among business units lead to differing net asset values and ROIs that are not comparable. Furthermore, business units with older fixed assets will have lower net asset values than business units with newer fixed assets, even if the same depreciation method is being used by all business units. Therefore, the best comparison among stores will be achieved if Ramirez values its fixed assets at their fair values for the purposes of calculating ROI.

explanations.A: Business units with older fixed assets will have lower historical cost values than business units with newer fixed assets because of inflation, causing the business units’ ROI’s to be not comparable. Furthermore, historical cost unadjusted for accumulated depreciation—even if the assets were purchased at the sae time—is not meaningful for any purpose. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.B: Business units with older fixed assets will have lower net asset book values than business units with newer fixed assets, causing the business units’ ROI’s to be not comparable. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.C: Historical cost adjusted for inflation during the assets’ holding periods might make the historical cost values for the business units used in calculating ROI reasonably comparable. However, historical cost unadjusted for accumulated depreciation is not meaningful for any purpose.

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: A company uses return on investment (ROI) to compare its divisions, using this evaluation to determine division manager bonuses. Which method of asset measurement would provide the best method of comparison?

options.A: Historical cost.
options.B: Depreciated cost.
options.C: Current cost.

studyUnit: Study Unit 11: C.3. Performance Measures, ROI, and RI

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: Edith Carolina, president of the Deed Corporation, requires a minimum return on investment of 8% for any project to be undertaken by her company. The company is decentralized and leaves investment decisions up to the discretion of the division managers as long as the 8% return is expected to be realized. Michael Sanders, manager of the Cosmetics Division, has had a return on investment of 14% for his division for the past 3 years and expects the division to have the same return in the coming year. Sanders has the opportunity to invest in a new line of cosmetics that is expected to have a return on investment of 12%. If the Deed Corporation evaluates managerial performance using return on investment, what will be the preference for taking on the proposed cosmetics line by Edith Carolina and Michael Sanders?

options.A: Carolina will reject / Sanders will accept
options.B: Carolina will reject / Sanders will reject
options.C: Carolina will accept / Sanders will reject
options.D: Carolina will accept / Sanders will accept

correctExplanation: Since return on investment uses a percentage of return as the measurement, Sanders would not accept this proposal. That is because the expected return on this investment (12%) is less than the return that Sanders' division has earned in the past (14%). Therefore, accepting this investment would decrease Sanders' return on investment so he would reject it. On the other hand, Carolina would accept the project because the return of this project is greater than the 8% required by the company.

explanations.A: Carolina would accept the project because the expected return on this project's investment is greater than the 8% required by the company. Sanders will not accept the project, because accepting this investment would decrease Sanders' return on investment.
explanations.B: Carolina would accept the project because the expected return on this project is greater than the 8% required by the company.
explanations.D: Sanders will not accept the project, because accepting this investment would decrease Sanders' return on investment.

studyUnit: Study Unit 11: C.3. Performance Measures, ROI, and RI

topic: Return on Investment and Residual Income
question: Business unit A has a return on investment of 10%, with a net profit for the year of $40,000. The opportunity cost for the business unit investments has been calculated at 8%. The company plans to purchase a new machine worth $100,000 and expects the net profit to rise by an additional $15,000. The new purchase decision will increase the return on investment

options.A: to 11% and increase the residual income by $7,000.
options.B: by 1% and increase the residual income by $8,000.
options.C: by 1% and increase the residual income by $15,000.
options.D: to 11% and increase the residual income by $15,000.

correctExplanation: Return on investment is income (operating income unless otherwise stated) of the business unit divided by total assets of the business unit (investment). Before the investment, Business Unit A had a return on investment of 10% and income for the year of $40,000. Thus, the total assets of Business Unit A must have been $400,000 ($40,000 ÷ $400,000 = 10%). After making a new investment of $100,000, the assets of the business unit will increase to $500,000 and its income is expected to increase by $15,000 to $55,000. After the investment, ROI is expected to become $55,000 ÷ $500,000, or 11%, an increase of 1%. Residual income is income of the business unit less the product of assets of the business unit multiplied by the required rate of return, which may be the opportunity cost of investments. The opportunity cost is 8%. Before the investment, the residual income of Business Unit A was $40,000 − ($400,000 × 0.08), or $8,000. After making the new $100,000 investment, when income is expected to increase to $55,000, residual income is expected to become $55,000 − ($500,000 × 0.08), or $15,000. Thus RI is expected to increase by the difference between $15,000 and $8,000, or by $7,000.

explanations.B: The new purchase decision is expected to increase Business Unit A's return on investment by 1%, but it will not increase residual income by $8,000. The amount by which residual income will increase is the new residual income minus the former residual income amount.
explanations.C: The new purchase decision is expected to increase Business Unit A's return on investment by 1% and increase its residual income to $15,000, but not to increase residual income by $15,000. The amount by which residual income will increase is the new residual income minus the former residual income amount.
explanations.D: The new purchase decision is expected to increase Business Unit A's return on investment to 11% and increase its residual income to $15,000, but not to increase residual income by $15,000. The amount by which residual income will increase is the new residual income minus the former residual income amount.

question: A company is considering three independent projects. Projected financial information is shown below. options.A: Joker and Penguin only.

studyUnit: Study Unit 11: C.3. Performance Measures, ROI, and RI

question: To insure that a divisional vice president places appropriate focus on both the short-term and the long-term objectives of the division, the best approach would be to evaluate the vice president’s performance by using

options.A: residual income since it will eliminate the rejection of capital investments that have a return less than ROI but greater than the cost of capital.
options.B: financial and nonfinancial measures, including the evaluation of quality, customer satisfaction, and market performance.
options.C: return on investment (ROI) which permits easy and quick comparisons to other similar divisions.
options.D: division segment margin or profit margin.

correctExplanation: Financial measures such as return on investment, residual income, and profit margins focus on the achievement of short-term objectives. Nonfinancial measures such as evaluation of quality, customer satisfaction and market performance focus on the achievement of long-term objectives. Evaluation of both financial and nonfinancial measures is called a balanced scorecard method of evaluation. The balanced scorecard includes both financial and nonfinancial measures in evaluating the overall contribution made by each unit to the achievement of company goals.

explanations.A: Residual income focuses on the achievement of short-term objectives.
explanations.C: Return on investment focuses on the achievement of short-term objectives.
explanations.D: Segment margin and profit margin focus on the achievement of short-term objectives.

intro: A company has divided its customers into two groups. Group 1 consists of 20% of the company’s most loyal and reliable customers. Group 2 consists of 80% of the company’s customers who are either small customers or larger customers who order small quantities to test the product before placing larger orders. tail: The best way for the company to improve profitability is to

options.A: raise the selling price of the product.
options.B: discontinue sales to Group 2 customers.
options.C: eliminate discounts for Group 1 customers.
options.D: charge a separate fee for the delivery of small quantities.

correctExplanation: Delivery charges were $500,000 for the Group 2 orders. If even a portion of those costs were reimbursed by the customers, the sales to the Group 2 customers would become profitable. Thus charging a separate delivery fee for small orders is the best way for the company to improve its profitability.

explanations.A: Depending upon the elasticity of demand for the product, raising the selling price of the product might result in fewer sales and thus reduced profitability. Since only the Group 2 customers are unprofitable, efforts to improve profitability should focus on those customers.
explanations.B: The sales to the Group 2 customers could become profitable if a change were made to the terms of small sales. Furthermore, small quantities ordered by customers who are testing the product before placing larger orders can lead to future, more profitable, business. Therefore, discontinuing sales to Group 2 customers would not be a good decision.
explanations.C: The sales to the Group 1 customers are profitable even with the sales discounts. Eliminating discounts for Group 1 customers would not be a good move because it could lead to fewer of those profitable sales. Since only the Group 2 customers are unprofitable, efforts to improve profitability should focus on those customers.

studyUnit: Study Unit 12: C.3. Multiple Performance Measures

question: All of the following are considered appropriate goals for measuring a division manager's efficiency for a budgeting period except

options.A: a targeted share of the market.
options.B: earnings per share projections.
options.C: a reduction in the organizational structure (fewer employees doing a given amount of work).
options.D: budgeted operating income.

correctExplanation: Earnings per share projections and actual earnings per share are calculated for the company as a whole by dividing earnings by the weighted average number of shares outstanding. There is no such thing as earnings per share for an individual division, because shareholders are not shareholders of one division only but are shareholders of the whole company. Therefore, earnings per share projections are not considered an appropriate goal for measuring a division manager's efficiency for a budgeting period.

explanations.A: A targeted share of the market for a division is considered an appropriate goal for measuring a division manager's efficiency for a budgeting period because the division's actual share of the market can be compared with the targeted share of the market to measure the division manager's performance.
explanations.C: A targeted reduction in the organizational structure for a division is considered an appropriate goal for measuring a division manager's efficiency for a budgeting period because the division's actual reduction accomplished can be compared with the targeted reduction to measure the manager's performance.
explanations.D: Budgeted operating income for a division is considered an appropriate goal for measuring a division manager's efficiency for a budgeting period because actual operating income can be compared with budgeted operating income to measure the division manager's performance.

correctExplanation: Customer profitability involves more than just the gross profit or gross profit margin for each customer. Other customer-level, or customer-specific, costs that would not exist if each customer's orders had not been received and fulfilled need to be considered, as well. Customer-specific expenses include the variable selling expense related to each individual customer's orders, and that amount should be deducted from each customer's gross profit margin to determine that customer's profitability. The customer-specific selling expense used should not include costs that would be incurred whether or not sales are made to that customer. It should include only costs incurred as a result of making sales to that specific customer, that is, costs that would not be incurred if that customer's orders were not received and fulfilled. Examples of customer-specific selling expenses are sales commissions paid and shipping-out expenses paid.
