studyUnit: Study Unit 3: F.1. Databases

question: Schema, subschemas, and record structures are defined in which of the following functions for which a database management system is used?

options.A: Database development.
options.B: Application development.
options.C: Database maintenance.
options.D: Database interrogation.

correctExplanation: The structure of a database is defined during the process of database development. The structure of a database includes the schema, subschemas, and record structure. The schema is a map or plan of the entire database. It is the database’s logical structure. The schema specifies the names of the data elements contained in the database and their relationships to the other data elements. The subset of information in a database that a given application or user is permitted to access is called a subschema. For example, read-only access to data may be granted to many users for queries, but only certain users have authority to update it. In defining the record structure for each table, the database administrator gives each field a name and a description, determines how many characters the field will have, and what type of data each field will contain (for example, text, integer, decimal, date), and may specify other requirements such as how much disk space is needed.

explanations.B: Schema, subschemas, and record structures are not defined in the process of application development. Application development involves developing custom applications including the queries, forms, reports, and labels for the custom applications and allowing many different custom applications to easily access a single database.
explanations.C: Schema, subschemas, and record structures are not defined in the process of database maintenance. Database maintenance involves record deletion, alteration, and reorganization.
explanations.D: Schema, subschemas, and record structures are not defined in the process of database interrogation. Database interrogation is done by users to retrieve data from a database by using a query language and the database management system to select subsets of records in order to extract information.

question: Data in a database is structured in various levels from the lowest level to the highest level. Arrange the following data elements according to their hierarchical levels, from the lowest level to the highest level: File Field Record Database

options.A: Field, record, database, file.
options.B: Field, file, record, database.
options.C: Field, record, file, database.
options.D: Database, field, record, file.

correctExplanation: A data field is the first level in the data hierarchy. A field is information that describes one attribute of an item, or entity, in the database such as a person or an object. A record is the second level in the data hierarchy. A database record contains all the information about one item, or entity, in the database. A file, also called a table, is the third level of the data hierarchy. A table is a set of common records. A complete database is the highest level. Several related files or tables make up a database.

explanations.A: The database is the highest level in the data hierarchy.
explanations.B: A file is a higher level than a record in the data hierarchy.
explanations.D: The database is the highest level in the data hierarchy, not the lowest.

question: Smart Backpacks, Inc. specializes in making backpacks that cater to tech-savvy individuals with features like built-in batteries and GPS trackers. While 80% of the sales are for standard backpacks, the company also offers customizable backpacks. Because building a custom backpack can take up to a week, the customer is not charged until their backpack ships. In the past year, the company has experienced tremendous growth, with sales tripling over the previous year. The company has experienced a variety of growing pains leading to some customer satisfaction issues. However, the management accountant has suggested that an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system might help and could solve all of the following issues except:

options.A: Longer production times due to the number of customizable backpack options.
options.B: Sales staff not being able to tell customers if their desired backpack is currently in stock.
options.C: Delays in production due to shortages of raw materials.
options.D: Customers being charged the incorrect price when their custom backpack ships.

correctExplanation: An ERP system by itself would not be able to improve the process of physically manufacturing the backpacks.

explanations.B: Sales staff using the ERP system would have access to current inventory and would be able to tell customers if a particular backpack is in stock.
explanations.C: The ERP system would integrate the raw materials inventory and supply chain functions, allowing the company to more accurately track their raw materials and re-order before they run out.
explanations.D: With an ERP system, after production of each custom backpack it would be marked in the ERP system as ready to ship and transferred to the shipping department. The ERP system would create the packing slip for the shipping department to access and would charge the customer. The price charged would be the price on the customer's order.

studyUnit: Study Unit 4: F.1. Enterprise Resource Management

question: An ERP (Enterprise Resource Planning) system enables the same information to be available across all departments such as purchasing, production, delivery, and sales. This can help in

options.A: Reducing wasted time.
options.B: Minimizing duplication of effort.
options.C: Lowering production costs.
options.D: All of the above.

correctExplanation: All of the above may be improved with an ERP system. An Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system is usually a suite of integrated applications that is used to collect, store, manage, and interpret data across the organization. Often the information is available in real time. The applications share data, facilitating information flow among business functions. Communication and coordination are improved across departments, leading to greater efficiencies in production, planning, and decision-making that can lead to lower production costs, lower marketing expenses, and other efficiencies such as reducing redundancies and wasted time. Data duplication is reduced and labor required to create inputs and distribute and use system outputs is reduced. Potential errors caused by inputting the same data multiple times are reduced.

explanations.A: Wasted time can be reduced with an ERP system because communication and coordination are improved across departments, leading to efficiencies.
explanations.B: Duplication of effort is minimized with an ERP system. However, that is not the only thing that can be improved by an ERP system.
explanations.C: Production costs can be lowered with an ERP system because the improvement in communication and coordination across departments can lead to greater efficiencies in production. However, production costs are not the only thing that can be improved by an ERP system.

explanations.B: Accounting and finance is a component of an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system.
explanations.D: Human resources is a component of an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system.

studyUnit: Study Unit 4: F.1. Enterprise Resource Management

question: Which of the following is not true of an Enterprise Resource Planning system?

options.A: Business process reengineering is usually required in order to use it.
options.B: Extension is available to customers, suppliers, and other business partners.
options.C: It features integration.
options.D: It utilizes a decentralized database.

correctExplanation: An Enterprise Resource Planning system does not utilize a decentralized database. An Enterprise Resource Planning system utilizes a centralized database. The data from the separate areas of the organization flow into a secure and centralized database rather than several separate databases in different locations. All users use the same data derived through common processes.

explanations.A: This is a true statement. An ERP system usually forces organizations to reengineer or redesign their business processes in order to use the system. Because ERP software is “off-the-shelf” software, customization is usually either impossible or prohibitively expensive. Thus, business processes used must accommodate the needs of the system and many may need to be redesigned.
explanations.B: This is a true statement. Extended enterprise resource planning systems include customers, suppliers, and other business partners. The systems interface with customers and suppliers through supply chain management applications that give partners along the supply chain access to internal information of their suppliers and customers. Suppliers can access the company’s internal information such as inventory levels and sales orders, enabling the company to reduce its cycle time for procuring raw materials for manufacturing or goods for sale. Customers can also view their supplier’s information about their pending orders.
explanations.C: This is a true statement. ERP software integrates accounting, customer relations management, business services, human resources, and supply chain management so that the data needed by all areas of the organization will be available for planning, manufacturing, order fulfillment, and other uses. The system tracks all of a firm’s resources, including cash, raw materials, inventory, fixed assets, and human resources, forecasts their requirements, and tracks shipping, invoicing, and the status of commitments such as orders, purchase orders, and payroll.

question: Which of the following are disadvantages of converting existing separate IT systems to an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system? I. Re-engineering business processes for the new ERP system is usually required, which is time-consuming. II. Converting data from existing systems to the new ERP system is costly. III. Information technology staff costs increase. IV. An ERP transition can lead to system failures and cause disruptions in various departments of the organization. V. An unsuccessful ERP transition can result in system-wide failures that disrupt production, inventory management, and sales, leading to huge financial losses. Customers who are inconvenienced by the implementation may leave. Because the entire business relies on the new ERP system, it is critical that it be completely functional and completely understood by all employees before it “goes live.” No opportunities are available to “work out the bugs” or “learn the ropes” when the entire business relies on the one system. (IV) Ongoing costs after implementation include hardware costs, system maintenance costs, and upgrade costs (V).

question: A single location in which a copy of all historical data for an entire organization is located is known as a

correctExplanation: A data warehouse is a single location where a copy of all of the historical data for the entire organization is stored so it can be accessed for data mining to discover patterns in the data for use in making decisions. A data warehouse is also called an enterprise data warehouse.

explanations.A: A data mart is not a single location in which a copy of all historical data for an entire organization is located. A data mart is a subsection of a data warehouse that provides users with analytical capabilities for a restricted set of data.
explanations.B: A data lake is not a single location in which a copy of all historical data for an entire organization is located. A data lake is a massive body of information fed by multiple sources for which the content has not been processed. It can include unstructured data such as social media data, videos, emails, chat logs, and images of invoices, checks, and other items. Data lakes have important capabilities for data mining and generating insights, but usually only a data scientist is able to access their capabilities because of the analytical skills needed to make sense of the raw information.
explanations.C: A data field is not a single location in which a copy of all historical data for an entire organization is located. A data field is the first level in the data hierarchy of a database. A data field describes one attribute of an item or entity in the database, such as a person or object.

question: Enterprise Performance Management (EPM) software is

studyUnit: Study Unit 5: F.1. Data Warehouse, Data Mart, Data Lake, and EPM

topic: Data Warehouse, Data Mart, Data Lake, and EPM
question: Which of the following is not a type of data mart?

options.A: Dependent.
options.B: Semi-dependent.
options.C: Hybrid.
options.D: Independent.

correctExplanation: Semi-dependent is not a type of data mart. A data mart—a subsection of a data warehouse that provides users with analytical capabilities for a restricted set of data—can be one of three different types: Dependent. A dependent data mart draws on an existing data warehouse. It is constructed using a top-down approach and withdraws a defined portion of the data in the data warehouse when it is needed for analysis. Several dependent data marts, used by different areas of the organization, can draw on a single data warehouse. Independent. An independent data mart is created without the use of a data warehouse through a bottom-up approach. The data for just one data mart for a single business function is uploaded, transformed, and then loaded directly into the data mart. If an organization needs several data marts for different areas of the organization, each one would need to be created and updated separately, which is not optimal. Furthermore, the idea of independent data marts is antithetical to the motivation for developing a data warehouse. Hybrid. A hybrid data mart combines elements of dependent and independent data marts, drawing some data from an existing data warehouse and some data from transactional systems.

explanations.A: A dependent data mart is a type of data mart. A dependent data mart draws on an existing data warehouse. It withdraws a defined portion of the data from the data warehouse when it is needed for analysis.
explanations.C: A hybrid data mart is a type of data mart. A hybrid data mart combines elements of dependent and independent data marts, drawing some data from an existing data warehouse and some other sources. Only a hybrid data mart allows analysis of data from a data warehouse with data from other sources.
explanations.D: An independent data mart is a type of data mart. An independent data mart is created without the use of a data warehouse. The data for just a single business function is uploaded, transformed, and then loaded directly into the data mart for use by that business function. If an organization needs several data marts for different areas of the organization, each one would need to be created and updated separately, which is not optimal. Furthermore, the idea of independent data marts is antithetical to the motivation for developing a data warehouse.

The data for just one data mart for a single business function is uploaded, transformed, and then loaded directly into the data mart. question: Which one of the following is not a function of an accounting information system that is integrated with an Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system and an Enterprise Performance Management (EPM) system?

options.A: Provide an electronic purchase order form with pre-filled columns.
options.B: Allow vendors to access and select requisition forms.
options.C: Deliver data to management for performance evaluation.
options.D: Automatically send documentation to appropriate parties for approval.

correctExplanation: An accounting information system, even one integrated with an ERP system, does not allow vendors to access and select requisition forms. A Supply Chain Management (SCM) application can be used with an ERP system to provide suppliers with access to the company’s inventory levels and sales orders so they can ship product to the company automatically whenever its inventory of an item gets low. However, vendors cannot access internal requisition forms or select internal requisition forms.

explanations.A: In an accounting information system, preformatted input screens are used to assist in the data entry process. For example, a date field to be filled in would be presented onscreen as __/__/____. However, preformatted input screens can also be automatically populated in certain fields with data such as the current date, default shipping method, sales tax to be charged and collected based on the shipping address, and other terms.
explanations.C: An Enterprise Performance Management (EPM) system monitors and manages performance of an organization in reaching its performance goals. It can be integrated with the organization’s accounting information system, ERP system, customer relations management system, data warehouse, and other systems. It automates the gathering of data from multiple sources and consolidates it to support performance management. And an EPM system can be used to generate dashboards that automatically present current information that is customized to the needs of each user. A dashboard is a screen in a software application, a browser-based application, or a desktop application. It organizes and displays in one place information relevant to a given objective or process, or for senior management, it may show patterns and trends in data across the organization. A dashboard is typically connected to an underlying data source so it can be updated continuously. It frequently has an interactive element that enables a user to view the data in different ways, drill down to learn more about a particular data point, sort the data, or filter the data to exclude portions of it.
explanations.D: An accounting information system that is integrated with an ERP system can automatically send documentation to appropriate parties for approval, for example if credit approval is required for an order received. The sales order department would release the order electronically through the ERP system, and the document would be automatically routed electronically to the credit department for their approval. The credit department’s response would be entered into the ERP system and automatically routed electronically back to the sales order department.

question: For the data stored in a data warehouse to be useful, the data should

question: Which of the following best describes the primary purpose of data governance within an organization?

options.A: Enabling the availability of reliable and consistent data for better decision-making and risk management.
options.B: Ensuring data is stored in the cloud for easy access.
options.C: Implementing advanced data analytics to derive business insights.
options.D: Managing data flows both internal and external to the organization.

correctExplanation: Data governance involves ensuring that data is reliable, consistent, and available so that management can assess performance, make informed decisions, and manage associated risks. This includes setting policies and procedures to ensure data quality and integrity.

explanations.B: While storing data in the cloud can be a part of data management strategies, data governance encompasses a broader range of practices, including data quality, integrity, security, and privacy, not just storage solutions.
explanations.C: Advanced data analytics is a use of data management and data governance, but it is not the primary purpose for data governance. Data governance ensures the data used in analytics is accurate, reliable, and secure, thus supporting analytics activities but not defining them.
explanations.D: Although managing data flows is a component of data governance, it is not the primary purpose. Data flows pertain to how data moves within and outside the organization, but data governance focuses more on the overall management and control of data assets.

question: Which of the following is not one of the five interrelated components of the internal control system according to COSO?

explanations.D: Monitoring is part of the internal control system according to COSO. Monitoring is overseeing the entire internal control system to assess the operation of existing internal controls to ensure that the internal control system continues to operate effectively.

studyUnit: Study Unit 6: F.2. Data Governance

question: Which of the following is a core aspect of data management that focuses specifically on the protection and lifecycle of data within an organization?

options.B: Data integration techniques

explanations.C: Data governance policies are overarching rules and procedures that guide how data is managed and controlled within an organization. While crucial, they are part of the governance framework rather than a specific aspect of the hands-on management of data security and lifecycle.

question: Data governance encompasses the practices, procedures, processes, methods, technologies, and activities that deal with the overall management of the data assets and data flows within an organization. Data governance is a process that helps the organization better manage and control its data assets and it includes several aspects. Management of the completeness, consistency, reliability, and accuracy of data describes what aspect of data governance?

options.A: Data integrity.
options.B: Data usability.
options.C: Data availability.
options.D: System availability.

correctExplanation: The completeness, consistency, reliability, and accuracy of data describes data integrity. The management of data integrity is an aspect of data governance.

explanations.B: The completeness, consistency, reliability, and accuracy of data does not describe data usability. Data usability is the accessibility of data to users and applications, its quality, and its accuracy. The management of data usability is a different aspect of data governance.
explanations.C: The completeness, consistency, reliability, and accuracy of data does not describe data availability. Data availability is the process of making the data available to users and applications when it is needed and where it is needed. The management of data availability is a different aspect of data governance.
explanations.D: The completeness, consistency, reliability, and accuracy of data does not describe system availability. System availability is the process of maximizing the probability that the system will function as required and when required. The management of system availability is a different aspect of data governance.

question: Data governance encompasses the practices, procedures, processes, methods, technologies, and activities that deal with the overall management of the data assets and data flows within an organization. explanations.B: Determination of who is authorized to access data and which items of data each authorized person can access does not describe data security. explanations.C: Determination of who is authorized to access data and which items of data each authorized person can access does not describe compliance with regulations. studyUnit: Study Unit 6: F.2. Data Governance

question: Data governance encompasses the practices, procedures, processes, methods, technologies, and activities that deal with the overall management of the data assets and data flows within an organization. Data governance is a process that helps the organization better manage and control its data assets and it includes several aspects. Management of the process of combining data from different sources, both internal and external, and providing users with a unified view of all the data describes what aspect of data governance?

options.A: System maintenance.
options.B: Data usability.
options.C: Data integration.
options.D: Data mining.

correctExplanation: The process of combining data from different sources, both internal and external, and providing users with a unified view of all the data describes data integration. The management of data integration is an aspect of data governance.

explanations.A: The process of combining data from different sources, both internal and external, and providing users with a unified view of all the data does not describe system maintenance. System maintenance involves making modifications to the system to correct a problem, to improve the system’s performance, to update it, or to adapt it to changed requirements or a changed environment. The management of system maintenance is a different aspect of data governance.
explanations.B: The process of combining data from different sources, both internal and external, and providing users with a unified view of all the data does not describe data usability. Data usability is accessibility of the data to users and applications, its quality, and its accuracy. The management of data usability is a different aspect of data governance.
explanations.D: The process of combining data from different sources, both internal and external, and providing users with a unified view of all the data does not describe data mining. Data mining is the use of algorithms in complex data sets to find patterns in the data that can be used to extract usable data from the data set. Data mining uses specialized computational methods derived from the fields of statistics, machine learning, and artificial intelligence to search large data sets to extract and analyze data in order to discover previously unknown, useful patterns, trends, and relationships within the data that go beyond simple analysis and that can be used to make decisions. Data mining is not an aspect of data governance.

topic: Data Life Cycle and Records Management
question: Which of the following is not one of the stages of the data life cycle?

options.A: Data maintenance
options.B: Data synthesis
options.C: Data purging
options.D: Data monitoring

correctExplanation: Data monitoring is not a part of the data life cycle.

explanations.A: Data maintenance is the processing of data before deriving any value from it, such as performing data integration. A governance issue is determining how best to supply the data to the stages at which data synthesis and data usage occur.
explanations.B: Data synthesis is the creation of new data values using other data as input. To “synthesize” something means to combine different things to make something new. Data synthesis is therefore combining data from different sources to create new data. Governance issues include concerns about data ownership and the need for citation, the quality and adequacy of the input data used, and the validity of the synthesized data.
explanations.C: Data purging occurs at the end of the data’s life cycle. Data purging is the removal of every copy of a data item from all locations within the organization. Purging should generally be done only of data that has been previously archived. Data governance considerations include development and maintenance of data retention and destruction policies that comply with all laws and regulations regarding record retention; conformance with established policies; confirmation that purging has been done properly; and documentation of data purged.

studyUnit: Study Unit 7: F.2. Data Life Cycle and Records Management

topic: Data Life Cycle and Records Management
question: The data life cycle encompasses the period from creation of data and its initial storage through the time the data becomes out of date or no longer needed and is purged. Which of the following statements is correct about the data life cycle?

Furthermore, data does not need to pass through all of the stages, and it may pass through various stages several times during its life cycle.

explanations.B: This is not a correct statement. The stages of the data life cycle do not describe a sequential flow of data.
explanations.C: This is not a correct statement. Data is not limited to passing through each stage of the data life cycle only once. Data may pass through various stages several times during its life cycle.
explanations.D: This is not a correct statement. Data does not need to pass through all of the states of the data life cycle.

question: A data breach is an example of a stage in the life cycle of data, even though it would be unplanned and certainly unwanted. Which stage of the data life cycle does a data breach constitute?

studyUnit: Study Unit 7: F.2. Data Life Cycle and Records Management

topic: Data Life Cycle and Records Management
question: Which of the following is a stage of the data life cycle?

options.A: Data records management.
options.B: Data cleansing.
options.C: Data maintenance.
options.D: Data mining.

correctExplanation: Data maintenance is a stage in the data life cycle. Data maintenance is the processing of data before deriving any value from it, such as performing data integration. Other stages are: data capture, data synthesis, data usage, data analytics, data publication, data archival, and data purging.

explanations.A: Data records management is not a stage in the data life cycle. Records management involves developing a policy that establishes how records are to be maintained, identified, retrieved, preserved, and when and how they are to be destroyed. The policy then must be followed consistently. However, if a lawsuit is pending or anticipated, all document and data destruction should cease. All documents and data should be preserved, even if they would otherwise be purged under the policy. The stages in the data life cycle are: data capture, data maintenance, data synthesis, data usage, data analytics, data publication, data archival, and data purging.
explanations.B: Data cleansing is not a stage in the data life cycle. Data cleansing is part of preprocessing data to be used in data mining. It includes determining whether the values in the data are in a reasonable range and whether there are obvious outliers, determining how missing data (blank fields) should be handled, and altering the data as necessary to make it usable. The stages in the data life cycle are: data capture, data maintenance, data synthesis, data usage, data analytics, data publication, data archival, and data purging.
explanations.D: Data mining is not a stage in the data life cycle. Data mining is the use of statistical techniques to search large data sets to extract and analyze data in order to discover previously unknown, useful patterns, trends, and relationships within the data that go beyond simple analysis and that can be used to make decisions. The stages in the data life cycle are: data capture, data maintenance, data synthesis, data usage, data analytics, data publication, data archival, and data purging.

topic: Data Life Cycle and Records Management
question: In which data life cycle stage do legal, regulatory, or contractual constraints on whether the data can legally be used in the ways the users want to use it constitute a governance challenge?

options.A: Data maintenance.
options.B: Data synthesis.
options.C: Data usage.
options.D: Data analytics.

correctExplanation: Legal, regulatory, or contractual constraints on whether the data can legally be used in the ways the users want to use it constitute a governance challenge in the data usage stage of the data life cycle. Data usage is the application of the data to tasks, whether used in support of the organization or used by others as part of a product or service the organization offers. Organizations must ensure that the data is used only for purposes that align with contractual limitations, that the usage complies with privacy laws, and does not violate any confidentiality agreements or intellectual property rights. For example, customer data collected for one purpose cannot be repurposed without the consent of the data owners.

explanations.A: Legal, regulatory, or contractual constraints on whether the data can legally be used in the ways the users want to use it would not constitute a governance challenge in the data maintenance stage of the data life cycle. Data maintenance is the processing of data before deriving any value from it, such as performing data integration. Regulations frequently mandate specific retention periods and right-to-erasure requirements such the GDPR's "right to be forgotten." Contracts may specify how long data must be kept or when it must be destroyed. Data security during storage is also heavily regulated.
explanations.B: Legal, regulatory, or contractual constraints on whether the data can legally be used in the ways the users want to use it would not constitute a governance challenge in the data synthesis stage of the data life cycle. Data synthesis is the creation of new data values using other data as input. Creating new datasets by combining or transforming data raises issues about the ownership of the derived data, about whether the synthesized data inherits the regulatory constraints of the source data, and whether new data products trigger additional compliance obligations. If synthesis creates personally identifiable information from data that was previously anonymized, it may violate privacy regulations. These constraints need to be tracked throughout each stage.
explanations.D: Legal, regulatory, or contractual constraints on whether the data can legally be used in the ways the users want to use it would not constitute a governance challenge in the data analytics stage of the data life cycle. Data analytics is the process of gathering and analyzing data in a way that produces meaningful information to aid in decision-making. The organization must ensure that its analytical methods do not violate laws such as fair lending or anti-discrimination; that audit trails are maintained for regulatory compliance; and that contractual restrictions on what types of analysis can be performed are complied with. Data analytics may also reveal sensitive information that triggers additional legal obligations.

topic: Data Life Cycle and Records Management
question: The management accountant at Wolfe's Widgets is working on creating a records management policy after one of the database servers crashed and the IT staff discovered that most of the backups were also corrupted. In the end, Wolfe's Widgets lost over three years of personnel and tax records. Which of the following would likely not be included in Wolfe's Widgets' new records management policy?

options.A: The statute of limitations for how long records legally must be maintained.
options.B: A comprehensive list of what records need to be maintained.
options.C: A strategy for preserving all records indefinitely.
options.D: Creation of an index for the location of all of the company's records.

correctExplanation: All records do not need to be preserved indefinitely. Records that are no longer needed should be destroyed at the appropriate time.

explanations.A: A statute of limitations is the time period during which an organization may sue or be sued or the time period within which a government agency can conduct an examination.
explanations.B: The records management policy should identify the information that is considered records and the information that is not considered records but that nevertheless should be subject to the guidance in the policy.
explanations.D: The records management policy should establish the practice of maintaining an index of active and inactive records and their locations and of maintaining logs containing records of all purged data.

question: Which form of cybersecurity attack is a form of extortion?

options.A: Copyright infringement.
options.B: Social engineering.
options.C: Ransomware.
options.D: Pay-per-click abuse.

correctExplanation: Extortion is the act of using actual or threatened force, violence, or intimidation to force a person or entity to turn over money or property. Extortion is a criminal offense. Ransomware is a form of extortion. It is particularly dangerous malware that encrypts data on a system and then demands a ransom (a payment) for decryption. If the ransom is not paid, the data is lost forever. The most common way that ransomware is installed is through a malicious attachment or a download that appears to come from a trusted source. The primary defenses against ransomware are to avoid installing it in the first place and having data backups.

explanations.A: Copyright infringement is not a form of extortion. Extortion is the act of using actual or threatened force, violence, or intimidation to force a person or entity to turn over money or property. Copyright infringement is the theft and replication of copyrighted material, for example intellectual property such as computer programs or textbooks or entertainment property such as music and movies.
explanations.B: Social engineering is not a form of extortion. Extortion is the act of using actual or threatened force, violence, or intimidation to force a person or entity to turn over money or property. Social engineering involves deceiving company employees into divulging information such as passwords, usually through a fraudulent email but it may be through something as simple as a telephone call. An individual may pose as a trustworthy coworker, perhaps someone from the company’s IT support division, and politely ask for passwords or other confidential information.
explanations.D: Pay-per-click abuse is not a form of extortion. Extortion is the act of using actual or threatened force, violence, or intimidation to force a person or entity to turn over money or property. Pay-per-click abuse refers to fraudulent clicks on paid online search ads (for example, on Google or Bing) that drive up the target company’s advertising costs. Furthermore, if there is a set limit on daily spending, the ads are pushed off the search engine site after the maximum-clicks threshold is reached, resulting in lost business as well as inflated advertising costs. Such scams are usually run by one company against a competitor.

explanations.C: Social engineering refers to using social tactics to gain information. Social skills, rather than technical skills, would be the most essential when attempting to gain information through social engineering.
explanations.D: Dumpster diving requires no computer knowledge.

question: Which of the following would mitigate password attacks?

options.A: Two-factor authentication using a verification code sent separately within a few minutes in order to complete a login.
options.B: Two-factor authentication using complex passwords linked to biometrics.
options.C: An intrusion detection system.
options.D: All of the above.

correctExplanation: Password attacks are attempts to break into a system by guessing passwords. All of the answer choices would mitigate password attacks. An intrusion detection system is a system that monitors network traffic in order to detect suspicious activities. It sends an alert to security teams when it detects a security risk or threat. Two-factor authentication requires two independent, simultaneous actions before access to a system is granted. A complex password would be difficult to break. Linking a password to biometrics would add two-factor authentication, creating additional security.

explanations.A: Two-factor authentication requires two independent, simultaneous actions before access to a system is granted. An example of two-factor authentication is requiring the input of a verification code sent separately within a few minutes of attempted login to complete the login. Two-factor authentication using a verification code sent separately within a few minutes in order to complete a login would mitigate password attacks. However, it is not the only answer choice that would do so.
explanations.B: Two-factor authentication requires two independent, simultaneous actions before access to a system is granted. A complex password would be difficult to break. Linking a complex password to biometrics would add two-factor authentication, creating additional security, which would mitigate password attacks. However, it is not the only answer choice that would do so.
explanations.C: An intrusion detection system is a system that monitors network traffic in order to detect suspicious activities. It sends an alert to security teams when it detects a security risk or threat. An intrusion detection system would mitigate password attacks. However, it is not the only answer choice that would do so.

question: Cyberattacks are usually intended to access, change, or destroy data, interrupt normal business operations, or they may involve extortion. A type of cyberattack that involves sending more data than expected to a computer system, causing the system to crash is

options.A: a Denial of Service (DOS) attack.
options.B: malware.
options.C: a buffer overflow attack.
options.D: a Distributed Denial of Service (DDOS) attack.

correctExplanation: Buffer overflow attacks are designed to send more data than expected to a computer system, causing the system to crash, permitting the attacker to run malicious code, or even allowing for a complete takeover of the system. Buffer overflow attacks can be easily prevented by the software programs adequately checking the amount of data received, but this common preventative measure is often overlooked during software development, leaving a system vulnerable to a buffer overflow attack.

explanations.A: A Denial of Service attack does not involve sending more data than expected to a computer system. Denial of Service (DOS) attacks occur when a website or server is accessed so frequently that legitimate users cannot connect to it.
explanations.B: Malware does not involve sending more data than expected to a computer system. Malware broadly refers to malicious software, including viruses.
explanations.D: A Distributed Denial of Service attack does not involve sending more data than expected to a computer system. Distributed Denial of Service attacks are a subset of Denial of Service attacks. Distributed Denial of Service (DDOS) attacks use multiple systems in multiple locations to attack one site or server by accessing it so frequently that legitimate users cannot connect to it.

question: During an audit of logins to computers on the plant floor, the auditor notices that one of the employee's accounts is being used to access a computer remotely via the Internet during work hours, when the employee is at work. There are no unsuccessful login attempts using an incorrect password in the computer's log. The auditor asks the employee if they gave their password to anyone, and the employee says, "No, of course not, only to the IT department when they called and said they needed to check something on my account. options.A: Brute Force Attack.
options.B: Dumpster diving.
options.C: Social Engineering.
options.D: Phishing.

correctExplanation: Social engineering uses personal interactions and social skills to trick people into divulging information. The most likely explanation is that the call was not from the IT department, but from someone outside the organization pretending to be an IT staff member.

explanations.B: This is not a likely explanation. For a password to be obtained through dumpster diving, the employee would have to write down the password, through that paper away, and then someone would have to find the paper in the trash.

This is not the most likely explanation given the employee's statement that the "IT department" had called and asked for his password. The fact that the employee added "I would never give my password out over email!" is not relevant, because the employee gave the password out over a telephone call, not over email.

question: A company that needs to filter incoming packets of electronic information being sent over the Internet will most likely implement a special-purpose hardware device or software called a(n)

options.A: intrusion prevention system to block unauthorized incoming packages of data.
options.B: firewall to permit certain authorized packages to enter the company network.
options.C: router to direct the package to the approved destination in the company network.
options.D: border router to control the link between the company network and the Internet.

correctExplanation: A firewall serves as a barrier between two networks and is designed to provide data filtering. Traditional firewalls use packet filtering to control network access by monitoring outgoing and incoming packets. Packets are used in networking to carry data during transmission from its source to its destination. They have a header that contains information that is used to help them find their way and to reassemble the data after transmission. Traditional firewalls permit or deny access based on the information in the header about the source and the destination Internet Protocol (IP) addresses, protocols, and ports.

explanations.A: An intrusion prevention system would filter some traffic, but is primarily designed to detect attacks and would not provide general-purpose data filtering.
explanations.C: A router is used to connect two different networks and would not be used to filter incoming packets.
explanations.D: A border router is a specific type of router that is used to connect enterprise networks to the Internet and would not be used to filter incoming packets.

An example of “something you have” is a physical object that can be used to certify an authorized user’s identity, such as a fob. options.D: Encryption.

correctExplanation: Social engineering is a form of cyberattack and is not a defense against cyberattack. Social engineering involves deceiving company employees into divulging information such as passwords, usually through a fraudulent email but it may be through something as simple as a telephone call. An individual may pose as a trustworthy coworker, perhaps someone from the company’s IT support division, and politely ask for passwords or other confidential information.

explanations.B: Penetration testing is a defense against cyberattack. Penetration testing is performed by ethical hackers. Ethical hackers are network and computer experts with hacking skills who attempt to attack a secured system. They use the same methods as are used by malicious hackers, but if they find vulnerabilities that could be exploited by a malicious hacker, they report them to the owner or manager so they can be remedied. Ethical hacking is also called intrusion testing and vulnerability testing.
explanations.C: A firewall is a defense against cyberattack. A firewall serves as a barrier between the internal and the external networks and prevents unauthorized access to the internal network. Most firewalls will prepare a report of Internet usage, including any abnormal or excessive usage and attempts to gain unauthorized entry to the network. A firewall can be in the form of software directly installed on a computer, or it can be a piece of hardware installed between the computer and its connection to the Internet.
explanations.D: Encryption is a defense against cyberattack. Encryption converts data into a code and then a key is required to convert the code back to data. Unauthorized people can receive the coded information, but without the proper key they cannot read it. Encryption protects both stored data and data that could be intercepted during transmission. If a hacker gains access to encrypted files, the hacker may be able to see where the traffic came from and where it went but not the content.

question: Three months ago, I.A.N. Manufacturing used an outside IT contractor to install some complex software updates on their ERP system. I.A.N.’s IT manager created an administrator account for the contractor with full access to the system. After the contractor completed the project about a week later, the system was inspected and tested, and everything worked as expected. During the current routine IT audit, spyware was found on the ERP system, and it had been installed just one week previously by someone accessing the system using the contractor’s login. While interviewing the IT staff, the IT manager confessed that he had neglected to disable the contractor’s login. Which of the following user authentication controls would have best been able to prevent someone from accessing the system and installing the spyware using the contractor’s account? Accounts that automatically expire. Logs of all login attempts. Automatic account logoff policies. Two factor authentication. Requiring users to change their password every month. An intrusion detection system.

options.A: II and III
options.B: IV, V, and VI
options.C: I, V, and VI
options.D: I only

correctExplanation: Automatically expiring accounts are the only one of these choices that would have been likely to prevent access after three months. For example, if there was a policy that any contractor account was automatically closed after two weeks, then the contractor’s account would have been locked and unusable three months later.

explanations.A: Because the account was never disabled, logs would not show any unusual activity. Even if the logs were regularly reviewed, they would only be a detective control (not a preventive control). Automatic logoff policies only log out an account after a short period of inactivity but would not prevent accessing the account again in the future.
explanations.B: While two-factor authentication might have been able to prevent access depending on the two factors used, the other options would not be effective. Because the account was still active, whoever accessed the account could simply change the password, and an intrusion detection system would not flag access to an authorized account in the system.
explanations.C: While choice I is correct, choices V and VI are not. Because the account was still active, whoever accessed the account could simply change the password, and an intrusion detection system would not be likely to flag access to an authorized account in the system.

question: Companies need to have strict controls over access to their proprietary data. Poor data oversight can leave a company vulnerable to accidents, fraud, and malicious parties who manipulate equipment and assets. options.A: Something you are.
options.B: Something you want.
options.C: Something you know.
options.D: Something you have.

correctExplanation: Access controls are methods of restricting data access to authorized users. Logical access controls identify authorized users and control the actions they can perform. One or more of the following logical access controls can be adopted: Something you know, for example, user IDs and passwords. Something you are, for example, biometrics such as fingerprints, facial recognition, and voice recognition. Something you have, for example, a physical object such as an electronic device that generates a unique code to enable access. "Something you want" is not a strategy used to restrict data access to authorized users.

explanations.A: “Something you are” refers to biometrics, or the recognition of physical characteristics such as fingerprints, facial recognition, or voice recognition, and it is a strategy used to restrict data access only to authorized users.
explanations.C: “Something you know” authentication such as user IDs and passwords is a strategy used to restrict data access only to authorized users.
explanations.D: “Something you have,” which can be a fob, a tiny electronic device that generates a unique code to enable access, is a strategy used to restrict data access only to authorized users. The code changes at regular intervals for increased security.

question: In which stage of the systems development life cycle (SDLC) is a cost-benefit analysis done?

options.A: System analysis.
options.B: Operations and maintenance.
options.C: Statement of objectives.
options.D: Investigation and feasibility study of alternative solutions.

correctExplanation: A cost-benefit analysis is done as part of the investigation and feasibility study stage of the SDLC. Needs are identified and feasibility of alternative solutions are assessed, including the availability of required technology and resources; and then a cost-benefit analysis is done.

explanations.A: In the system analysis stage of the SDLC, the current system is analyzed to identify its strong and weak points, and the information needs from the new system, such as reports to be generated, database needs, and the characteristics of its operation are determined.
explanations.B: In the operations and maintenance stage of the SDLC, the system is put into a production environment and used to conduct business. Continuous monitoring and evaluation take place to determine what is working and what needs improvement. Maintenance includes modifying the system as necessary to adapt to changing needs, replacing outdated hardware as necessary, upgrading software, and making needed security upgrades.
explanations.C: In the statement of objectives stage of the SDLC, a written proposal is prepared, including the need for the new system, the nature and scope of the project and timing issues. A risk assessment is done to document security threats, potential vulnerabilities, and the feasible security and internal control safeguards needed to mitigate the identified risks.

question: Which one of the following statements about robotic process automation (RPA) is incorrect?

options.A: RPA can be used to provide customer service.
options.B: RPA makes use of common sense.
options.C: RPA helps process tasks more rapidly.
options.D: RPA can lead to cost savings.

correctExplanation: Robots in RPA have no “common sense.” If a flaw in the instructions creates an error that would be obvious to a human, the robot will continue to follow the instructions provided without deviation and the error may be replicated hundreds or thousands of times before it is recognized by a human. Then, correcting all the incidents of the error could be very difficult (unless the errors could be corrected using the same automated tools).

explanations.A: Robotic process automation can be used to automate some customer service tasks, including conversing with customers.
explanations.C: Once an RPA process has been set up, the process can be completed much more rapidly.
explanations.D: RPA can provide cost savings along with greater accuracy, faster cycle times, and improved scalability if volumes increase or decrease.

question: An analyst prepared a forecast using newly developed system features. question: Business process analysis (BPA) is used to analyze a business process to determine the way it is currently being done in order to monitor efficiency and productivity, locate weaknesses in the process, determine potential improvements, and determine whether those improvements should be implemented. Which of the following is not a task that is part of a business process analysis?

options.A: Look for ways to streamline the process so it uses fewer resources.
options.B: Implement improvements to the process.
options.C: Determine the beginning and ending points of the process to be analyzed.
options.D: Model potential changes to the process.

correctExplanation: Implementing improvements to the process is not a task in business process analysis. The steps in business process analysis and the tasks associated with each step are the following: Determine the process to be analyzed, including critical functions such as revenue, expenses, and the end product; processes that appear to be underperforming; or a new process just implemented to determine whether it is working as intended. Determine the beginning and ending points of the process to be analyzed. Collect information about the process that will be needed to analyze it, performing interviews and research as necessary. Map the process using a flowchart or a software solution for business process mapping. Analyze the process by determining its most important components and whether they could be improved. Look for ways to streamline the process so it uses fewer resources. Determine potential improvements by modeling potential changes to the process and make recommendations for ways to improve the process.

explanations.A: Looking for ways to streamline the process so it uses fewer resources is a task included in the step of analyzing the process.
explanations.C: Determining the beginning and ending points of the process to be analyzed is a task included in the step of determining the process to be analyzed, the first step in business process analysis.

question: Which of the following are applications of artificial intelligence? I. Robotic process automation. II. Machine learning. III. Digital assistants. IV. Machine vision.

question: A company is preparing to implement artificial intelligence to automate several accounting processes. During planning, management proposes several actions. Which of the following actions would be the most appropriate when implementing artificial intelligence?

studyUnit: Study Unit 12: F.3. Cloud Computing

question: Which of the following is not a type of cloud computing resource?

options.A: Hardware as a Service.
options.B: Software as a Service.
options.C: Platform as a Service.
options.D: Infrastructure as a Service.

correctExplanation: There is no type of cloud computing resource called "Hardware as a Service." Cloud computing is a method of essentially outsourcing the IT function. It is a way to increase IT capacity or add capabilities without having to invest in new infrastructure or license new software. Cloud service providers offer three types of resources: Software as a Service Platform as a Service Infrastructure as a Service

explanations.B: Software as a Service is a type of cloud computing resource. Cloud computing is a method of increasing IT capacity or adding capabilities without having to invest in new infrastructure or license new software. Software as a Service is software provided by the cloud provider that is used by all business customers, for example enterprise resource planning; accounting, tax and payroll processing and tax filing; and online word processing. The user does not manage or control the application other than certain limited user-specific application configuration settings.
explanations.C: Platform as a Service is a type of cloud computing resource. Cloud computing is a method of increasing IT capacity or adding capabilities without having to invest in new infrastructure or license new software. When a company uses Platform as a Service, it deploys its own applications to the cloud using the cloud provider’s operating systems, programming languages, libraries, services, and tools. PaaS services include operating systems, database solutions, Web servers, and application development tools.
explanations.D: Infrastructure as a Service is a type of resource of cloud computing. Cloud computing is a method of increasing IT capacity or adding capabilities without having to invest in new infrastructure or license new software. Infrastructure as a Service includes both the hardware resources that support the cloud services being provided (for example server, storage, and network components) and the software deployed by the user. The user has control over operating systems, storage, and deployed applications and possibly limited control over selected networking components but does not manage or control the underlying cloud infrastructure.

question: Applications such as enterprise resource planning (ERP), customer relationship management (CRM), accounting, tax and payroll processing and tax filing, human resource management, document management, service desk management, online word processing and spreadsheet applications, and email are part of which cloud computing resource?

options.A: Infrastructure as a Service
options.B: Software as a Service.

correctExplanation: Software as a Service is the capability provided to the user to use the provider’s applications running on a cloud infrastructure. The applications are accessible from various client devices through either a thin client interface, such as a web browser (e.g., web-based email), or a program interface. The user does not manage or control the underlying cloud infrastructure including network, servers, operating systems, storage, or even individual application capabilities, with the possible exception of limited user-specific application configuration settings. Applications available as Software as a Service applications include enterprise resource planning (ERP), customer relationship management (CRM), accounting, tax and payroll processing and tax filing, human resource management, document management, service desk management, online word processing and spreadsheet applications, email, and many others.

explanations.A: Infrastructure as a Service does not provide applications such as enterprise resource planning (ERP), customer relationship management (CRM), accounting, tax and payroll processing and tax filing, human resource management, document management, service desk management, online word processing and spreadsheet applications, and email to users. Infrastructure as a Service is both the hardware resources that support the cloud services being provided, including server, storage, and network components, and the software deployed.
explanations.C: Platform as a Service does not provide applications such as enterprise resource planning (ERP), customer relationship management (CRM), accounting, tax and payroll processing and tax filing, human resource management, document management, service desk management, online word processing and spreadsheet applications, and email to users. Platform as a Service is the capability provided to the user to deploy onto the cloud infrastructure user-created or acquired applications created using programming languages, libraries, services, and tools supported by the provider.
explanations.D: There is no cloud service called “Technology as a Service.”

question: What is cloud computing?

question: In blockchain terminology, a _________________ is the consensus algorithm used on the Bitcoin blockchain.

options.A: Nonce.
options.B: Block.
options.C: Hash.
options.D: Proof of Work.

correctExplanation: “Proof of Work” is the consensus algorithm, also called the consensus protocol or consensus mechanism, used on a Proof of Work blockchain such as the Bitcoin network. Proof of Work is a decentralized mechanism for arriving at a consensus among members of the blockchain network. It requires mining nodes on the network to do work to solve a mathematical puzzle—the calculation of a hash value for the block that meets the requirements for the hash. The generation of a hash value that fulfills the target hash value by adding a nonce to the block header to alter the input to the hash and cycling through potential nonces until one is found that creates the target hash value is called Proof of Work. The Proof of Work is costly and time-consuming to produce but easy for others on the blockchain network to verify. A consensus algorithm is a set of rules and number of steps for accomplishing a generally accepted decision among a group. A consensus algorithm is used on a blockchain to ensure that a majority (at least 51%) of the nodes on the network agree that all transactions are validated and authentic. The Proof of Work (PoW) consensus algorithm is the most widely used consensus algorithm on blockchains, although other consensus algorithms are used as well.

explanations.A: A nonce is not the consensus algorithm used on the Bitcoin blockchain. The nonce (number used once) in a block on a blockchain is a number that miners include in the block header and repeatedly adjust while attempting to create a valid block. The nonce is included in the block header along with other metadata such as the previous block's hash, the timestamp, and the merkle root (a hash representing all the transactions in the block). During the mining process, a miner takes all the data in the block header, including the current nonce value, and runs it through a hash function. The goal is to find a nonce that produces a hash meeting the network's difficulty requirements—typically a hash that falls below a specific target value or contains a certain number of leading zeroes. If the resulting hash does not meet these requirements, the miner adjusts the nonce incrementally, usually by adding 1 to the nonce value, and hashes the block header again. This process repeats millions or billions of times until a miner finds a nonce that produces a valid hash. Once found, this valid hash proves the miner performed the computational work required (the source of the name "Proof of Work"), and other nodes can quickly verify the block by hashing the block header once with that nonce to confirm it meets the difficulty target.
explanations.B: A block is nor the consensus algorithm used on the Bitcoin blockchain. A block is a record in a blockchain that contains and confirms a group of transactions that have been encrypted and aggregated into the block by a miner.
explanations.C: A hash is not the consensus algorithm used on the Bitcoin blockchain. Hashing is taking an input string of any length and giving it an output of a fixed length using a hashing algorithm.

question: What is the purpose of a "Proof of Work" on the Bitcoin blockchain?

options.A: As a hash function.
options.B: To prevent double spending.
options.C: It follows the nonce.
options.D: It sends information to the blockchain network.

correctExplanation: A consensus algorithm like Proof of Work serves as the mechanism that allows a decentralized network to agree on the current state of the blockchain without requiring a central authority. The primary purposes of a consensus algorithm on a blockchain such as proof of work include: Preventing double-spending: ensuring that the same digital asset can’t be spent twice. Without consensus, different nodes might have conflicting records of who owns what Establishing transaction order: determining which transactions happened first when there are competing versions, creating a single authoritative history that all participants accept. Securing the network against attacks: proof of work specifically makes it computationally expensive to alter the blockchain’s history. An attacker would need to control more computing power than the rest of the network combined (a 51% attack), which becomes prohibitively costly as the network grows Enabling trustless operation: participants do not need to trust each other or any central entity. The algorithm itself, through mathematical and economic incentives, ensures that honest behavior is more profitable than dishonest behavior. In proof of work, miners compete to solve complex mathematical puzzles to add the next block. The difficulty of these puzzles creates the “work” that protects the chain. Rewriting history to eliminate a transaction, thus making it possible for a user to spend the same cryptocurrency more than once, would require redoing all that work, which becomes increasingly impractical as more blocks are added.

explanations.A: The purpose of a "Proof of Work" on the Bitcoin blockchain is not a hash function. Hashing is taking an input string of any length and giving it an output of a fixed length using a hashing algorithm.
explanations.C: This is a nonsense statement.
explanations.D: The purpose of a "Proof of Work" on the Bitcoin blockchain is not to send information to the blockchain network.

question: A number that miners adjust in the block header to find a valid hash that meets the blockchain network's difficulty requirements on a blockchain that uses Proof of Work as its consensus protocol is known as

options.A: a node.
options.B: a miner.
options.C: a nonce.
options.D: a hash.

correctExplanation: The nonce (meaning "number used once") in a block on a blockchain is a number that miners include in the block header and repeatedly adjust while attempting to create a valid block. The nonce is included in the block header along with other metadata such as the previous block's hash, the timestamp, and the merkle root (a hash representing all the transactions in the block). During the mining process, a miner takes all the data in the block header, including the current nonce value, and runs it through a hash function. The goal is to find a nonce that produces a hash meeting the network's difficulty requirements, typically a hash that falls below a specific target value or contains a certain number of leading zeroes. If the resulting hash does not meet these requirements, the miner adjusts the nonce incrementally, usually by adding 1 to the nonce value, and hashes the block header again. This process repeats millions or billions of times until a miner finds a nonce that produces a valid hash. Once found, this valid hash proves the miner performed the computational work required (the source of the name "Proof of Work"), and other nodes can quickly verify the block by hashing the block header once with that nonce to confirm it meets the difficulty target.

explanations.A: A number that miners adjust in the block header to find a valid hash that meets the blockchain network's difficulty requirements is not known as a node. A node is a computer on a peer-to-peer blockchain network. Nodes keep the network running by participating in the relay of information. A node sends information to a few other nodes, which in turn relay the information to additional nodes, and so forth. Every participant in a network is a node, but there are different types of nodes that have different types of tasks. On the Bitcoin network, there are two basic types of nodes: full nodes and lightweight, or light, nodes. Full nodes are where the blockchain resides, and they each store a complete copy of the blockchain, validate transactions, and maintain consensus. Light or lightweight nodes connect to full nodes in order to participate in the blockchain and do not store a complete copy of the blockchain.
explanations.B: A number that miners adjust in the block header to find a valid hash that meets the blockchain network's difficulty requirements is not known as a miner. Miners, or mining nodes, are full nodes on a blockchain that uses Proof of Work as its consensus protocol. The miners validate transactions, group them into blocks, find valid nonces through repeated hashing to solve the computational puzzle, and add completed blocks to the blockchain. The miner is the blockchain participant performing the work, not the number being adjusted.
explanations.D: A number that miners adjust in the block header to find a valid hash that meets the blockchain network's difficulty requirements is not known as a hash. A hash is the fixed-length string of characters produced by running data through a hashing algorithm. The hash is the result of the hashing process. Hashing is a mathematical process that takes an input of any length and produces an output of a fixed length. For example, a hash function might convert any amount of data into a 64-character string. The hash serves as a unique digital fingerprint of the input data. The same input always produces the same hash, but even a tiny change in the input produces a completely different hash.

question: Which of the following characteristics of smart contracts is incorrect?

options.A: Smart contracts can perform prompt regulatory reporting.
options.B: Smart contracts are not subject to fraud and manipulation.
options.C: Smart contracts can access outside information or data to trigger actions.
options.D: Smart contracts can enhance market activity and efficiency by facilitating trade execution.

correctExplanation: A smart contract may be subject to fraud and manipulation, such as hacking and loss of digital assets. For example, an attacker might cause the smart contract to improperly transfer assets to themself or others, and the sender and the intended receiver would have limited or no recourse. Smart contracts can include deliberately damaging code that does not behave as promised or that may be manipulated. An oracle, the third party source used by the smart contract to authorize payments, may be subject to manipulation or may itself be fraudulent and may disperse fraudulent information that results in fraudulent outcomes.

explanations.A: This is a true statement. Smart contracts can perform prompt regulatory reporting. For example, financial institutions could input maximum interest rates into smart loan contracts to comply with usury laws, and regulators could have real-time access to the transactions.
explanations.C: This is a true statement. Smart contracts can access outside information or data such as commodity prices, weather data, interest rates, or an occurrence of an event, to trigger actions. For example, an orchard owner may be concerned about a freeze that could destroy the year’s fruit crop. An insurance company offers insurance against a freeze through a self-executing smart contract. The orchard owner and the insurance company agree to the contract terms and digitally sign a smart contract that is uploaded to a blockchain. The orchard owner’s periodic premium payments are automated, and the blockchain checks a third-party source such as the National Weather Service daily for a possible freeze event. If a freeze event occurs, payment is sent automatically from the insurance company to the orchard owner.
explanations.D: This is a true statement. Smart contracts can enhance market activity and efficiency by facilitating trade execution. Smart contracts provide for simultaneous execution of obligations by all parties. In a simple securities transaction, for example, a smart contract can effect payment by the buyer to the seller and delivery of the securities by the seller to the buyer at the same time. Thus, the mutual exchange occurs simultaneously with finality and certainty. All parties can see when the cash and securities become available in the smart contract record. The transaction doesn’t occur until the necessary settlement conditions are met, so there is no partial fulfillment risk and settlement failure is avoided.

studyUnit: Study Unit 13: F.3. Blockchain and Smart Contracts

question: A set of promises, specified in digital form, including protocols within which the parties perform on these promises is known as:

options.A: A blockchain.
options.B: A smart contract.
options.C: A distributed ledger.
options.D: A bitcoin.

correctExplanation: In blockchain terminology, a contract that has been digitized and uploaded to a blockchain is called a smart contract. According to Nick Szabo, a computer scientist who envisioned smart contracts in 1996, “A smart contract is a set of promises, specified in digital form, including protocols within which the parties perform on these promises.”

explanations.A: A blockchain is not a set of promises, specified in digital form, including protocols within which the parties perform on these promises. A blockchain is a decentralized and distributed platform. It is a record of transactions in chronological order that is used to store and share information among network participants. A blockchain is “a way for one Internet user to transfer a unique piece of digital property to another Internet user, such that the transfer is guaranteed to be safe and secure, everyone knows that the transfer has taken place, and nobody can challenge the legitimacy of the transfer."
explanations.C: A distributed ledger is not a set of promises, specified in digital form, including protocols within which the parties perform on these promises. In blockchain terminology, a distributed ledger is a database held by each full node in a network, and each full node updates the database independently. Records are independently constructed and passed around the network by the various full nodes—they are not held by any central authority.
explanations.D: A bitcoin is not a set of promises, specified in digital form, including protocols within which the parties perform on these promises. A bitcoin is a virtual currency that is secured by strong cryptography. It is a digital asset, also called a cryptoasset. It is used on the Bitcoin network, which is the distributed ledger of balances held in bitcoin tokens by users on the network. A virtual currency such as bitcoin is decentralized, which means it does not use a central bank or administrator as an intermediary. It can be transferred from one user to another on the Bitcoin network, a peer-to-peer network.

question: In practice, which one of the following is true with respect to transactions in a blockchain?

options.A: They are permanent, but only if they are time-stamped.
options.B: They can be changed if they are time-stamped.
options.C: They can be deleted, but only if all parties agree.
options.D: They cannot be changed, but they can be reversed and re-entered.

correctExplanation: This is a true statement. Transactions on a blockchain are considered immutable, which means “not subject to or susceptible to change." Note that although transactions on a blockchain are not susceptible to change, blockchains have been hacked and transactions have been changed by hackers, diverting payments and stealing a significant amount of the currency. But the legitimate parties to a transaction cannot go into the blockchain and change the original transaction even if they all agree. If all the parties to the transaction agree that a change to a confirmed transaction is needed, a new transaction must be created to reverse the original transaction, and then another new transaction can be created with the changed information.

explanations.A: When a transaction is entered onto the blockchain, it is time-stamped and broadcast, and the community of users controls how the reord of information is updated to include the new transaction. But time-stamping or the lack of time-stamping does not control whether a transaction is permanent. Once a transaction has been added to the blockchain, it is not susceptible to change, although it is not impossible to change it if a hacker is determined. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.B: When a transaction is entered onto the blockchain, it is time-stamped and broadcast, and the community of users controls how the record of information is updated to include the new transaction. Once a transaction has been added to the blockchain, it is not susceptible to change, although it is not impossible to change it if a hacker is determined. Time-stamping or the lack of time-stamping does not control the potential for a transaction to be changed by a determined hacker. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.C: Once a transaction has been added to the blockchain, it cannot be changed or deleted from the blockchain by the parties to the transaction, even if they all agree. If all parties to a transaction want to change the transaction, a new transaction must be created that reverses the original transaction, and then a new, revised, transaction can be created with the new information. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

Senior management used the information to create a new strategic plan, including new planned marketing programs. The company experienced a turnaround and sales increased by 30%. Sensitivity analysis can be used to determine how much the prediction of a model will change if one input to the model is changed.
