question: Which of the following is not a challenge inherent in data mining?

options.A: Poor quality data.
options.B: A growing volume of unstructured data.
options.C: A growing volume of structured data.
options.D: Data security.

correctExplanation: A growing volume of structured data is not a challenge inherent in data mining. Structured data that conforms to relational database management systems is not difficult to capture and analyze. Some of the challenges inherent in data mining include the following: Poor data quality: incomplete, out of date, or inconsistent data. Information exists in multiple locations in the organization and is not centrally located. Biases are amplified because data is interpreted by human beings, and human beings have biases, or preferences that can get in the way of impartial judgment. For example, people tend to trust data that supports their pre-existing opinions and to not trust data that does not. Correlation does not prove causation. If a causal relationship is assumed where none exists, despite correlations in the data, decisions made on the basis of the data will be flawed. Ethical issues such as profiling according to demographics or other characteristics can result from the collection of personal information on millions of people. Data security, for example personal information on individuals may be stolen by hackers or employees. A growing volume of unstructured data such as social media posts, videos, emails, chat logs, and images is difficult to capture and analyze.

explanations.A: Poor quality data is a challenge inherent in data mining. Data stored in relational databases may be incomplete, out of date, or inconsistent. For example, mailing lists can contain duplicate records, leading to duplicate mailings and excess costs. Poor quality data can lead to poor decisions.
explanations.B: A growing volume of unstructured data is a challenge inherent in data mining. Data items that are unstructured do not conform to relational database management systems, making capturing and analyzing unstructured data more complex. Unstructured data includes items such as social media posts, videos, chat logs, and images, for example images of invoices or checks received.
explanations.D: Data security is a challenge inherent in data mining because personal information on individuals is frequently stolen by hackers or even employees.

question: When used to determine what specific online advertisement to present to a person browsing the Internet based on the fact that other people who browsed the same things purchased a particular item, data mining involves ______________________ of patterns from a data set.

options.A: Classification.
options.B: Generalization.
options.C: Prediction.
options.D: Clustering.

correctExplanation: Data mining involves generalization of patterns from a data set. Generalization is used in data mining to determine, for example, what specific online advertisement to present to a person based on their browsing patterns and on purchases made by other people after having browsed the same topics. “Generalization” is the ability to predict or assign a label to a “new” observation based on a model built from past experience. In other words, the generalizations developed in data mining should be valid not just for the data set used in observing the pattern but should also be valid for new, unknown data.

explanations.A: Data mining involves classification, which is used to make a prediction about data with an unknown classification based on similar data where the classification is known. The similar data where the classification is known is used to develop rules that are applied to the data with the unknown classification to make a prediction about it, such as predicted purchasers or predicted non-purchasers. However, classification is not used in data mining to determine what specific online advertisement to present to a person based on their browsing patterns and on purchases made by other people after having browsed the same topics.
explanations.C: Data mining involves prediction. Prediction is used when the goal is to predict the numerical value of a variable. When a prediction such as the monetary amount of a purchase that a customer will make is needed, similar data where the purchase amounts are known is used to develop rules that are applied to the data where the purchase amounts are unknown to make a prediction. However, prediction is not used in data mining to determine what specific online advertisement to present to a person based on their browsing patterns and on purchases made by other people after having browsed the same topics.
explanations.D: Clustering is discovering groups in data sets that have similar characteristics without using known structures in the data. It can be used to reduce the number of groups to be included in the data mining algorithm. However, clustering is not used to determine what specific online advertisement to present to a person based on their browsing patterns and on purchases made by other people after having browsed the same topics.

question: Simple linear regression is an example of

options.A: A simple supervised learning algorithm.
options.B: An unsupervised learning algorithm.
options.C: Reinforcement learning.
options.D: A Monte Carlo simulation.

correctExplanation: Simple linear regression is an example of a basic supervised learning algorithm. Linear regression is a statistical approach that can be used to model the relationship between one or more independent variables and a dependent variable, based on historical data points. The x-variable, the independent variable, serves as the predictor variable. The y-variable, the dependent variable, is the outcome variable in the training and test data where the y-variable for each x-variable is known. The regression line is drawn so that it minimizes the sum of the squared deviations between the actual y-variables and the y-variables as predicted by the regression line. Then, the regression line is used to predict the y-variables that will result for new values of x for which the y-variables are unknown.

explanations.B: Simple linear regression is not an example of an unsupervised learning algorithm. Linear regression is a statistical approach that can be used to model the relationship between one or more independent variables and a dependent variable, based on historical data points. Unsupervised learning algorithms are used when there is no outcome variable to predict or classify. Association rules, dimension reduction, and clustering are unsupervised learning methods.
explanations.C: Simple linear regression is not an example of reinforcement learning. Linear regression is a statistical approach that can be used to model the relationship between one or more independent variables and a dependent variable, based on historical data points. Reinforcement learning is a feedback-based machine learning technique in which an intelligent agent (a machine) learns to determine the proper step based on the results of the previous steps in similar circumstances. The system reinforces itself.
explanations.D: Simple liner regression is not an example of a Monte Carlo simulation. Linear regression is a statistical approach that can be used to model the relationship between one or more independent variables and a dependent variable, based on historical data points. A Monte Carlo simulation analysis can be used to find solutions to mathematical problems that involve changes to multiple variables at the same time. Monte Carlo simulation uses repeated random sampling and can develop probabilities of various scenarios coming to pass that can be used to compute a predicted result.

studyUnit: Study Unit 15: F.4. Data Mining

question: Data mining is a large, multi-step project. In which step of a data mining project would the data scientist visualize the data by reviewing the information in a chart form?

options.A: Partition the data.
options.B: Interpret the results of the algorithm.
options.C: Reduce the data dimension if needed.
options.D: Explore, clean, and preprocess the data.

correctExplanation: Visualizing the data by reviewing the information in a chart form is a part of exploring, cleaning, and preprocessing the data for a data mining project. Exploring, cleaning, and preprocessing the data is the third step in a typical data mining project. It involves Verifying that the data is in usable condition (whether the values are in a reasonable range and whether there are obvious outliers); Determining how missing data (blank fields) should be handled; Visualizing the data by reviewing the information in chart form. If using structured data, ensuring consistency in the definitions of fields, units of measurement, time periods covered, and so forth. New variables may be created in this step, for example using the start and end dates to calculate the duration of a time period.

explanations.A: Partitioning the data is the sixth step in a typical data mining project, and it is performed if supervised learning (classification or prediction) will be used. Partitioning the data involves partitioning the dataset randomly into three parts: one part for training, one for validation, and one for testing. Visualizing the data by reviewing the information in a chart form is not a part of portioning the data.
explanations.B: Interpreting the results of the algorithm is the ninth step in a typical data mining project. It involves choosing the best algorithm and testing the final choice on the test data to learn how well it will perform. Visualizing the data by reviewing the information in a chart form is not a part of interpreting the results of the algorithm.
explanations.C: Reducing the data dimension if needed is the fourth step in a typical data mining project. It involves Eliminating unneeded variables, Transforming variables as necessary and creating new variables. Visualizing the data by reviewing the information in a chart form is not a part of reducing the data dimension.

studyUnit: Study Unit 15: F.4. Data Mining

question: Data mining is a large, multi-step project. In which step of a data mining project would the data scientist take samples from a large database or databases or from other sources?

options.A: Explore, clean, and preprocess the data.
options.B: Understand the purpose of the project.
options.C: Partition the data.
options.D: Select the dataset to be used.

correctExplanation: Taking samples from a large database, databases, or from other sources is done in selecting the dataset to be used for a data mining project. Selecting the dataset to be used is the second step in a typical data mining project. The samples should reflect the characteristics of the records of interest so the data mining results can be generalized to records outside of the sample. The data may be internal or external.

explanations.A: Exploring, cleaning, and preprocessing the data is the third step in a typical data mining project. It involves Verifying that the data is in usable condition (whether the values are in a reasonable range and whether there are obvious outliers). Determining how missing data (blank fields) should be handled. Visualizing the data by reviewing the information in chart form. If using structured data, ensuring consistency in the definitions of fields, units of measurement, time periods covered, and so forth. Taking samples from a large database, databases, or from other sources is not a part of exploring, cleaning, and preprocessing the data.
explanations.B: Understanding the purpose of the project is the first step in a typical data mining project. It involves understanding the user’s needs and what the user will do with the results. Also, the data scientist needs to know whether the project will be a one-time effort or will be ongoing. Taking samples from a large database, databases, or from other sources is not a part of understanding the purpose of the project.
explanations.C: Partitioning the data is the sixth step in a typical data mining project, and it is performed if supervised learning (classification or prediction) will be used. Partitioning the data involves partitioning the dataset randomly into three parts: one part for training, one for validation, and one for testing. Taking samples from a large database, databases, or from other sources is not a part of partitioning the data.

studyUnit: Study Unit 15: F.4. Data Mining

question: Data mining is a large, multi-step project. In which data mining step would regression analysis, neural networks and hierarchical clustering be considered as data mining techniques to use?

options.A: Partition the data.
options.B: Use algorithms to perform the task.
options.C: Reduce the data dimension if needed.
options.D: Select the data mining techniques to use.

correctExplanation: Regression analysis, neural networks and hierarchical clustering would be considered in the process of selecting the data mining techniques to use, the seventh step in a typical data mining project.

explanations.A: Consideration of regression analysis, neural networks, hierarchical clustering, and so forth is not a part of partitioning the data. Partitioning the data is the sixth step in a typical data mining project, and it is performed if supervised learning (classification or prediction) will be used. Partitioning the data involves partitioning the dataset randomly into three parts: one part for training, one for validation, and one for testing. Partitioning the data does not involve consideration of what data mining techniques to use.
explanations.B: Consideration of regression analysis, neural networks, hierarchical clustering, and so forth would not be a part of using algorithms to perform the task, the eighth step in a typical data mining project. The use of algorithms is an iterative process. The data scientist tries multiple algorithms, often using multiple variants of the same algorithm by choosing different variables or settings. The data scientist uses feedback from an algorithm’s performance on validation data to refine the settings. Use of algorithms to perform the task does not include consideration of the data mining techniques to use. Consideration of the data mining techniques to use needs to take place before algorithms can be used.
explanations.C: Consideration of regression analysis, neural networks, hierarchical clustering, and so forth is not a part of reducing the data dimension if needed. Reducing the data dimension is the fourth step in a typical data mining project, and it involves eliminating unneeded variables, transforming variables as necessary, and creating new variables. In reducing the data dimension, the data scientist needs to be sure to understand what each variable means and whether it makes sense to include it in the model. Reducing the data dimension does not involve consideration of what data mining techniques to use.

studyUnit: Study Unit 15: F.4. Data Mining

question: Data mining is a large, multi-step project. The following represent four of the steps that would typically be included in a data mining project. In what order would these steps be performed? Select the data mining techniques to use Determine the data mining task Explore, clean, and preprocess the data Reduce the data dimension
correctExplanation: The typical steps in data mining are: Understand the purpose of the project Select the dataset to be used Explore, clean, and preprocess the data Reduce the data dimension if needed Determine the data mining task Partition the data Select the data mining techniques to use Use algorithms to perform the task Interpret the results of the algorithm Deploy the model.

explanations.A: This arrangement is completely out of order.
explanations.B: Reducing the data dimension happens after exploring, cleaning, and preprocessing the data.
explanations.D: The data mining task should be determined before selecting which techniques to use.

studyUnit: Study Unit 15: F.4. Data Mining

question: Which of the basic concepts of predictive data analytics involves discovering groups in data sets that have similar characteristics without using known structures in the data for the purpose of reducing the number of groups to be included in the data mining algorithm?

options.A: Classification.
options.B: Association rules.
options.C: Clustering.
options.D: Prediction.

correctExplanation: Clustering, one of the basic concepts of predictive data analytics, is discovering groups in data sets that have similar characteristics without using known structures in the data. Clustering can be used in data reduction to reduce the number of groups to be included in the data mining algorithm.

explanations.A: Classification, one of the basic concepts of predictive data analytics, would be part of any data analysis, such as customers being classified as predicted purchasers or predicted non-purchasers. Classification does not involve discovering groups in data sets that have similar characteristics without using known structures in the data.
explanations.B: Association rules, also called affinity analysis, are one of the basic concepts of predictive data analytics and are used to find patterns of association between items in large databases, such as associations among items purchased from a retail store, or “what goes with what.” Association rules do not involve discovering groups in data sets that have similar characteristics without using known structures in the data.
explanations.D: The goal of prediction in predictive data analytics is to predict the numerical value of a variable such as the amount of a purchase. Prediction does not involve discovering groups in data sets that have similar characteristics without using known structures in the data.

studyUnit: Study Unit 15: F.4. Data Mining

question: Which of the basic concepts of predictive data analytics uses collaborative filtering?

options.A: Data reduction.
options.B: Association rules.
options.C: Online recommendation systems.
options.D: Dimension reduction.

correctExplanation: Online recommendation systems use collaborative filtering to deliver personalized recommendations to users. Collaborative filtering generates rules for “what goes with what” at the individual user level. It makes recommendations to individuals based on their historical purchases, online browsing history, or other measurable behaviors that indicate their preferences, as well as other users’ historical purchases, browsing, or other behaviors.

explanations.A: Data reduction does not use collaborative filtering. Collaborative filtering generates rules for “what goes with what” at the individual user level. Data reduction is the process of consolidating a large number of records into a smaller set by grouping the records into homogeneous groups.
explanations.B: Association rules does not use collaborative filtering. Collaborative filtering generates rules for “what goes with what” at the individual user level. Association rules, also called affinity analysis, are used to find patterns of association between items in large databases, such as associations among items purchased from a retail store, or “what goes with what," but at the entity level, not the individual level.
explanations.D: Dimension reduction does not use collaborative filtering. Collaborative filtering generates rules for “what goes with what” at the individual user level. Dimension reduction involves reducing the number of variables in the data before using it for data mining in order to improve its manageability, interpretability, and predictive ability.

studyUnit: Study Unit 15: F.4. Data Mining

question: Aaron's Auto Sales is reviewing last year's sales data to determine how to create more targeted advertisements based on the demographics of the individuals who purchase electric vehicles. Aaron's wants to analyze key market segmentation variables such as age, marital status, family size, gender, income, occupation, education, past vehicle purchases, accident history, and whether they own or rent their home to determine what characteristics buyers of electric vehicles have in common. However, to make the data simpler for analysis, Aaron's is limiting the number of factors to just family size, income, and past vehicle purchases so that their ad campaign can be more targeted based on only a few specific factors. Which predictive analysis tool did Aaron's use?

options.A: Clustering
options.B: Data reduction
options.C: Dimension reduction
options.D: Association rules

correctExplanation: Dimension reduction entails reducing the number of variables in the data before using it for data mining, in order to improve its manageability, interpretability, and predictive ability. This is exactly what Aaron's is doing by removing some of the vehicle options from the analysis.

explanations.A: Clustering is discovering groups in data sets that have similar characteristics without using known structures in the data. Aaron's did use known structures.
explanations.B: Data reduction is the process of consolidating a large number of records into a smaller set by grouping the records into homogeneous groups. Aaron's did not consolidate the sales into groups.
explanations.D: Association rules are used to find patterns between items, which is not what Aaron's was doing in this example.

studyUnit: Study Unit 15: F.4. Data Mining

question: Which of the following is not an example of the use of a neural network?

options.A: Performing fuzzy logic.
options.B: Self-driving vehicles with cameras on the vehicle.
options.C: Detecting fraud in credit card and other monetary transactions by recognizing that a given transaction is outside the ordinary pattern of behavior for that customer.
options.D: Identifying a digital image, for example identifying it as a cat or a dog.

correctExplanation: Neural networks are systems that can recognize patterns in data and use the patterns to make predictions using new data. A neural network is not used to perform fuzzy logic. Fuzzy logic helps to perform pattern recognition and classification tasks, but it does not perform prediction as a neural network does. A fuzzy logic system is simpler than a neural network. A fuzzy logic system can process incomplete and ambiguous data and make inferences in order to solve unstructured problems that may have multiple solutions with incomplete knowledge. Some examples of uses of neural networks include the following: Picking stocks for investment by performing technical analysis of financial markets and individual investment holdings. Making bankruptcy predictions. A neural network can be given data on firms that have gone bankrupt and firms that have not gone bankrupt. The neural network will use that information to learn to recognize early warning signs of impending bankruptcy, and it can thus predict whether a particular firm will go bankrupt. Detecting fraud in credit card and other monetary transactions by recognizing that a given transaction is outside the ordinary pattern of behavior for that customer. Identifying a digital image as, for example, a cat or a dog. Self-driving vehicles use neural networks with cameras on the vehicle as the inputs.

explanations.B: Neural networks are systems that can recognize patterns in data and use the patterns to make predictions using new data. Self-driving vehicles use neural networks with cameras on the vehicle as the inputs.
explanations.C: Neural networks are systems that can recognize patterns in data and use the patterns to make predictions using new data. A neural network can detect fraud in credit card and other monetary transactions by recognizing that a given transaction is outside the ordinary pattern of behavior for that customer.
explanations.D: Neural networks are systems that can recognize patterns in data and use the patterns to make predictions using new data. A neural network can identify a digital image, for example identifying it as a cat or a dog.

studyUnit: Study Unit 15: F.4. Data Mining

question: Data mining is frequently referred to as both an art and a science. Which of the following statements most accurately describes the art and science facets of data mining?

options.A: Data mining is a science, meaning that it results in definite conclusions.
options.B: Data mining is art, meaning that the output is often visual.
options.C: Data mining is an art because it involves making thoughtful choices.
options.D: Data mining is more science than art.

correctExplanation: In data mining, decisions must be made regarding what data to use, what tools to use, and what algorithms to use. For example, one word can have many different meanings. In mining text, the context of words must be considered. Therefore, instead of just looking for words in relation to other words, the data scientist looks for whole phrases in relation to other phrases. The data scientist must make thoughtful choices in order to get usable results.

explanations.A: Data mining does not necessarily result in definite conclusions; often the results of data mining require analysis and may not provide clear-cut answers.
explanations.B: While the output from data mining can be visual, this is not what is meant by saying that data mining is an art.
explanations.D: This statement is simply not true.

studyUnit: Study Unit 15: F.4. Data Mining

question: The repetition and refining of a process is known as

options.A: an iterative process.
options.B: an objective process.
options.C: the development process.
options.D: a descriptive process.

correctExplanation: The repetition and refining of a process is known as an iterative process. Data mining is an example of an iterative process because it involves trying different hypotheses repeatedly and making inferences from the results that can be applied to new data. Each repetition of the process is a single iteration, and the outcome of each iteration is the starting point of the next iteration.

explanations.B: The repetition and refining of a process is not known as an objective process.
explanations.C: The repetition and refining of a process is not known as the development process. Repetition and refining may be used in the process of development, but the repetition and refining of a process is not known by the name "development process."
explanations.D: The repetition and refining of a process is not known as a descriptive process.

studyUnit: Study Unit 15: F.4. Data Mining

question: A company could use data mining to help achieve all of the following except

options.A: forecasting demand at different locations.
options.B: identifying the most profitable customers.
options.C: predicting machinery failures.
options.D: improving customer privacy.

correctExplanation: Data mining involves using algorithms in complex data sets to find patterns in the data that can be used to extract usable data from the data set. Data mining is not used to improve customer privacy. In fact, data mining in raises concerns about customer privacy. Data mining might be used to classify potential customers into different groups to receive different marketing approaches based on some characteristic common to each group that is yet to be discovered. It may be used to answer questions such as what specific online advertisement should be presented to a particular person browsing on the Internet based on their previous browsing habits and the fact that other people who browsed the same topics purchased a particular item. Furthermore, data security is an issue in data mining because personal information on individuals is frequently stolen by hackers or even employees.

explanations.A: Data mining involves using algorithms in complex data sets to find patterns in the data that can be used to extract usable data from the data set. Data mining could be used to forecast demand at different locations based on past experience.
explanations.B: Data mining involves using algorithms in complex data sets to find patterns in the data that can be used to extract usable data from the data set. Data mining could be used to identify the most profitable customers based on their past purchases.
explanations.C: Data mining involves using algorithms in complex data sets to find patterns in the data that can be used to extract usable data from the data set. Data mining could be used to predict machinery failures based on past experience.

studyUnit: Study Unit 15: F.4. Data Mining

question: Reducing the number of variables in data before using it for data mining in order to improve its manageability, interpretability, and predictive ability in predictive data analytics is called

options.A: Clustering.
options.B: Data exploration.
options.C: Dimension reduction.
options.D: Data reduction.

correctExplanation: Dimension reduction, a basic concept of predictive data analytics, involves reducing the number of variables in the data before using it for data mining in order to improve its manageability, interpretability, and predictive ability.

explanations.A: Clustering, a basic concept of predictive data analytics, is discovering groups in data sets that have similar characteristics without using known structures in the data. It does not involve reducing the number of variables in the data before using it for data mining in order to improve its manageability, interpretability, and predictive ability.
explanations.B: Data exploration, a basic concept of predictive data analytics, is used to understand the data and detect unusual values. It does not involve reducing the number of variables in the data before using it for data mining in order to improve its manageability, interpretability, and predictive ability.
explanations.D: Data reduction, a basic concept of predictive data analytics, is the process of consolidating a large number of records into a smaller set by grouping the records into homogeneous groups. It does not involve reducing the number of variables in the data before using it for data mining in order to improve its manageability, interpretability, and predictive ability.

studyUnit: Study Unit 15: F.4. Data Mining

question: Comfortable Clothing Company, a retailer of casual clothes for men and women, launched a new collection of summer skirts and blouses in April for the upcoming summer season, immediately followed by a huge advertising campaign targeting television, radio, newspapers, and magazines. Because trends in men's clothing had not changed significantly since the previous year, Comfortable Clothing decided not to spend money revamping their men's lineup for the summer. In August, the management accountants started to work through several months of sales data with data mining tools to determine the success of their new women's clothing line and advertising campaign. Because they were already combing through the data, they also looked at men's summer clothing sales as part of their analysis. Through their analysis, the senior accountant noticed that sale of men's summer clothes also went up significantly over the same time period as women's and concluded that advertising for women's clothing also increases sales of men's clothing. Which of the following errors did the accountant make in their analysis?

options.A: Confirmation bias.
options.B: Gender discrimination.
options.C: Generalization.
options.D: Confusing correlation with causation.

correctExplanation: Analyzed data often displays correlations. However, correlation does not prove causation. Establishing a causal relationship is necessary before using correlated data in decision-making. It is reasonable that sales of men's summer clothing would increase beginning in April regardless of any advertising, simply because those clothes are now in season. The increase in men's summer clothing sales is likely coincidental with the advertising campaign for women's clothing.

explanations.A: There was no pre-determined result that the accountant was looking to confirm.
explanations.B: There is no evidence of discrimination based on the facts given.
explanations.C: Generalization is the ability to predict or assign a label to a “new” observation based on a model built from past experience. The accountant did not make any predictions.

studyUnit: Study Unit 15: F.4. Data Mining

question: A company seeks to tailor its marketing campaign targeting different customer groups. After establishing a data warehouse with relevant data, the company must now apply an appropriate analytical model to enable this targeting. The best model to use would be

options.A: classification analysis to find variables that predict customer categories.
options.B: cluster analysis to group similar observations about customers into natural groups.
options.C: regression analysis to find variables that enable predictions about customer behavior.
options.D: forecasting analysis to find variables to predict the future sales to a customer.

correctExplanation: Clustering is discovering groups in data sets that have similar characteristics without using known structures in the data or fixed groups. Clustering can be used in data reduction to reduce the number of groups to be included in the data mining algorithm. Customer segmentation is a form of clustering. Customers can be segmented according to geographic region, demographics such as age or gender, behavior such as usage level of a product or service, or lifestyle such as outdoor enthusiast or sports fan.

explanations.A: Any data analysis involves classification, such as whether a customer will purchase or not purchase. However, classification analysis to find variables that predict customer categories is not the best model to use to tailor a marketing campaign to target different customer groups.
explanations.C: Linear regression analysis is a statistical technique that is used to develop a mathematical equation that models the extent to which one variable (called the dependent or response variable) has historically been affected by one or more other variables (called the independent or predictor variables). If the historical relationship between the cause (or causes) and the effect has been sufficiently strong, regression analysis using the historical data can be used to make decisions and predictions about the dependent variable. Regression analysis to find variables that enable predictions about customer behavior is not the best model to use to tailor a marketing campaign to target different customer groups. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.D: Forecasting analysis to find variables to predict the future sales to a customer is not the best model to use to tailor a marketing campaign to target different customer groups. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

studyUnit: Study Unit 15: F.4. Data Mining

question: In which type of data analytics is data mining used?

options.A: Descriptive.
options.B: Diagnostic.
options.C: Predictive.
options.D: Prescriptive.

correctExplanation: Data mining is used in predictive analytics. Predictive analytics focus on the future using correlative analysis. Predictive analytics answer the question, “What is likely to happen”? by combining historical data with other data using rules and algorithms. Large quantities of data are processed to identify patterns and relationships between and among known random variables or data sets in order to make predictions about what is likely to occur in the future. The basic concepts of predictive analytics where data mining is used include: Classification of data. Data mining is used when the classification of the data is not known. Similar data where the classification is known is used to develop rules, and then those rules are applied to the data with the unknown classification to predict what the classification is or will be. Prediction, that is predicting the numerical value of a variable such as the amount of a purchase. Association rules or affinity analysis, used to find patterns of association between items in large databases, such as what products are frequently purchased along with what other products. Online recommendation systems, used to deliver personalized recommendations to online users by making predictions based on their historical purchases, online browsing history, or other behaviors that indicate their preferences, and on other users’ historical purchases, browsing, or other behaviors. Data reduction, or the process of consolidating a large number of records into a smaller set by grouping the records into homogeneous groups. Clustering, including discovering groups in data sets that have similar characteristics and using that information in data reduction to reduce the number of groups to be included in the data mining algorithm. Dimension reduction, or reducing the number of variables in the data before using it for data mining to improve its manageability, interpretability, and predictive ability. Data exploration, which is used to understand the data and detect unusual values by looking at each variable individually and looking at relationships between and among the variables to discover patterns in the data. Data visualization, a type of data exploration, consists of creating graphics for numerical data in order to visualize the distribution of the variables and to detect outliers.

explanations.A: Data mining is not used in descriptive data analytics.
explanations.B: Data mining is not used in diagnostic data analytics.
explanations.D: Data mining is not used in prescriptive data analytics.

studyUnit: Study Unit 15: F.4. Data Mining

question: Rachel's company has recently set up a new system that offers data mining capabilities and is training the management accountants how to use the various tools and processes. In the training, Rachel and her colleagues learned about the process of testing different hypotheses and then applying the results of one hypothesis as the data for another hypothesis. Which of the following terms best identifies this process?

options.A: Generalization
options.B: Prediction
options.C: Clustering
options.D: Iteration

correctExplanation: Iteration is the repetition of a process in order to generate a sequence of outcomes. Each repetition of the process is a single iteration, and the outcome of each iteration is the starting point of the next iteration.

explanations.A: Generalization is the ability to predict or assign a label to a “new” observation based on a model built from past experience. In other words, the generalizations developed in data mining should be valid not just for the data set used in observing the pattern but should also be valid for new, unknown data.
explanations.B: In prediction, the goal is to predict the numerical value of a variable such as the amount of a purchase rather than (for example) simply classifying customers as predicted purchasers or predicted non-purchasers.
explanations.C: Clustering is discovering groups in data sets that have similar characteristics without using known structures in the data. Clustering can be used in data reduction to reduce the number of groups to be included in the data mining algorithm.

studyUnit: Study Unit 15: F.4. Data Mining

question: Affinity analysis, a basic concept of predictive data analytics, is another name for

options.A: Data analysis.
options.B: Association rules.
options.C: Data reduction.
options.D: Data exploration.

correctExplanation: Association rules are also called affinity analysis. Association rules or affinity analysis is used in predictive data analytics to find patterns of association between items in large databases, such as associations among items purchased from a retail store, or “what goes with what.”

explanations.A: Affinity analysis is not another name for data analysis. Affinity analysis is used in predictive data analytics to find patterns of association between items in large databases, such as associations among items purchased from a retail store, or “what goes with what.” “Data analysis” is not one of the basic concepts used in predictive analysis.
explanations.C: Affinity analysis is not another name for data reduction. Affinity analysis is used in predictive data analytics to find patterns of association between items in large databases, such as associations among items purchased from a retail store, or “what goes with what.” Data reduction is a process in predictive data analytics that involves consolidating a large number of records into a smaller set by grouping the records into homogeneous groups.
explanations.D: Affinity analysis is not another name for data exploration. Affinity analysis is used in predictive data analytics to find patterns of association between items in large databases, such as associations among items purchased from a retail store, or “what goes with what.” Data exploration is used in predictive data analytics to understand the data and detect unusual values. Analytic Tools-Sensitivity and Simulation Analysis(7)

studyUnit: Study Unit 15: F.4. Data Mining

question: Which of the following statements is not correct with respect to sensitivity analysis and/or simulation analysis?

options.A: The variables used in sensitivity analysis are likely to be interrelated, and changing just one variable at a time may fail to take into consideration the effect that one variable’s change will have on other variables.
options.B: When the inputs used are themselves predictions, any prediction resulting from sensitivity analysis or simulation analysis can be ambiguous.
options.C: The accuracy of the assumptions used should be tested prior to being used in the model.
options.D: Simulation is flexible and can be used for a wide variety of problems.

correctExplanation: This is not correct. There is no way to test the accuracy of assumptions used in a sensitivity or simulation model until a certain amount of time has passed, and this is a limitation of sensitivity analysis and simulation analysis.

explanations.A: This is a correct statement. Only one variable at a time is changed in sensitivity analysis. Since variables may be interrelated and changing one may cause other variables to change, sensitivity analysis may fail to take into consideration the effect that one variable's change may have on other variables. This is a limitation of sensitivity analysis.
explanations.B: This is a correct statement, and it is a limitation of both sensitivity analysis and simulation analysis.
explanations.D: This is a correct statement, and it is a benefit of simulation analysis.

studyUnit: Study Unit 17: F.4. Analytic Tools-Sensitivity and Simulation Analysis

question: Which of the following statements regarding sensitivity analysis and Monte Carlo simulation analysis is true?

options.A: Changing one of the variables in sensitivity analysis is reflective of real-world changes because real-world variables are never interrelated.
options.B: Sensitivity analysis involves running a prediction model multiple times changing exactly one variable between each run.
options.C: The accuracy of the assumptions and relationships used in the model for sensitivity analysis are quickly and easily confirmed.
options.D: Monte Carlo simulation analysis is a subset of sensitivity analysis that involves changing only one input variable at a time.

correctExplanation: This is a true statement. Sensitivity analysis can be used to determine how much the prediction of a model will change if one input to the model is changed. It can be used to determine which input parameter is most important for achieving accurate predictions. Sensitivity analysis is known as “what-if” analysis.

explanations.A: The variables used in a sensitivity analysis are likely to be interrelated. Changing just one variable at a time may fail to take into consideration the effect that variable’s change will have on other variables.
explanations.C: There is no way to test the accuracy of assumptions and relationships used in the model until a certain amount of time has passed.
explanations.D: A Monte Carlo simulation analysis can be used to find solutions to mathematical problems that involve changes to multiple variables at the same time. Monte Carlo simulation can be used to develop an expected value when the situation is complex and the values cannot be expected to behave predictably.

studyUnit: Study Unit 17: F.4. Analytic Tools-Sensitivity and Simulation Analysis

question: Sensitivity analysis can be used to

options.A: estimate fixed and variable costs.
options.B: determine how much the prediction of a model will change if one input to the model is changed.
options.C: estimate the firm’s cost of capital.
options.D: determine how sensitive an independent variable is to a change in the dependent variable.

correctExplanation: Sensitivity analysis can be used to determine how much the prediction of a model will change if one input to the model is changed. It can be used to determine which input parameter is most important for achieving accurate predictions. Sensitivity analysis is known as “what-if” analysis.

explanations.A: Estimates of fixed and variable costs can be determined with simple linear regression analysis using the activity level of the cost driver as the independent variable (for example, production in units) and the associated cost as the dependent variable (for example, total production costs). But sensitivity analysis is not used to estimate fixed and variable costs.
explanations.C: Sensitivity analysis is not used to estimate a firm’s cost of capital. A company’s overall cost of capital is the return expected by investors on a portfolio consisting of all the company’s outstanding long-term debt and its equity securities. The overall cost of a firm’s capital depends upon the return that is demanded by each of the suppliers of its capital—its creditors and its shareholders. (Cost of capital is tested on the CMA Part 2 exam and is covered in the study materials for that exam.)

question: Which of the following can be used to find solutions to mathematical problems that involve changes to multiple input variables at the same time?

question: A company has analyzed the income distribution of its customer base. Management evaluates different presentation approaches. Which one of the following is the best data visualization option?

Each bar on a histogram represents an interval, and the size of each bar depicts the number of observations in that interval; whereas the bars on a bar chart represent the statistic being visualized across groups, such as the mean number of sales on each day of the week with a bar for each day. Therefore, a histogram would be the best data visualization option to use to present an income distribution of a company's customer base.

A bar chart would not be used to depict a frequency distribution such as the income distribution of a company's customer base. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.B: A line chart is used to visualize several observations for one or more different categories, with each category such as maximum, minimum, and mean represented by a line. A line chart would not be used to depict a frequency distribution such as the income distribution of a company's customer base. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.D: A scatter plot is used to show all the values for a dataset when there are two variables. It can reveal whether there is a correlation between them. question: A hospital has observed an increase in the number of cases of a disease and has asked an analyst to collect data on the cases over the last three years. explanations.B: A scatter plot can be used to show all the values for a dataset, typically when there are two variables. A scatter plot can reveal correlations between variables or alternatively, a lack of correlation. The independent variable is generally plotted on the horizontal (x) axis and the dependent variable is plotted on the vertical (y) axis. Since in this situation the independent variable is time and the dependent variable is the medical cases, a scatter plot would reveal the higher number of cases in the third and fourth quarters of each year. However, a scatter plot is not the best way to present the findings.
explanations.C: While a table would present the information, it would not be in a form that could easily be interpreted by the hospital management. A visual presentation would be a better way to show that the number of cases have been higher in the third and fourth quarters of each year.

question: “Goodness of fit” of a statistical model refers to

options.A: how well the predictor variable is predicted by the independent variable.
options.B: how close the actual, observed values are to the predicted values in the model.
options.C: how close the predicted future value is to the actual future value.
options.D: the average distances between the upper and lower bands of the confidence interval and the regression line.

correctExplanation: The term "goodness of fit" describes how close the values predicted by a statistical model match the observed values. Measures of goodness of fit summarize the difference between the observed values and the predicted values. When a model is trained on training data, the goal is to develop a model that is able to explain the relationship between the features of the training dataset and then generalize that to new data. The better the model explains the relationship between the variables of the new data, the better the fit of the model is.

explanations.A: “Goodness of fit” does not refer to how well the predictor variable is predicted by the independent variable. The independent variable in a regression is also known as the predictor variable, so the independent variable and the predictor variable are one and the same.
explanations.C: “Goodness of fit” does not refer to how close the predicted future value is to the actual future value. No statistical measure can measure that, since by definition, the actual future value has not happened yet.
explanations.D: “Goodness of fit” does not refer to the average distances between the upper and lower bands of the confidence interval and the regression line. The confidence interval is used to describe the amount of uncertainty caused by the sampling method used when drawing conclusions about a population based on a sample.

studyUnit: Study Unit 16: F.4. Types of Data Analytics

question: Which of the following statements with respect to regression analysis is not true?

options.A: If there is a change in conditions surrounding historical data, the use of historical data is questionable.
options.B: Regression analysis cannot be performed without historical data.
options.C: The statistical relationships may be valid for only the range of historical data in the sample.
options.D: Use of an inappropriate dependent variable may lead to misleading results.

correctExplanation: It is not correct to say that “an inappropriate dependent variable may lead to misleading results.” Regression analysis measures the extent to which an effect has historically been the result of a specific cause or causes. The usefulness of the data generated by regression analysis depends on the choice of independent variable(s), not on the choice of the dependent variable, and that is a limitation of regression analysis. If the choice of independent variable(s) is inappropriate, the results can be misleading. Even if the independent and dependent variable appear to be well correlated, correlation does not prove causation. The fact that two variables are correlated does not necessarily mean that one variable caused the other. Both variables could have been affected by a third, unidentified, factor. If a causal relationship between the independent and dependent variables used is assumed where none exists, decisions made on the basis of the data will be flawed. In addition to a strong correlation between each independent variable and the dependent variable, there must be a logical cause-and-effect relationship between them before the independent variable can be used effectively to predict the dependent variable.

explanations.A: This is a true statement, and this is a limitation of regression analysis. When historical data is used to develop a forecast, the conditions surrounding the historical data should continue into the forecast period in order for the historical data to be valid for use in forecasting.
explanations.B: This is a true statement, and this is a limitation of regression analysis. Regression analysis measures the extent to which an effect has historically been the result of a specific cause, and a forecast of that cause can then be used to forecast the future effect. Without historical data, regression analysis cannot be performed.
explanations.C: This is a true statement, and this is a limitation of regression analysis. The statistical relationships between the variables that can be developed using regression analysis may be valid for only the range of historical data in the sample. If that is the case, use of those relationships to forecast an effect when the independent variable is outside the range or to make assumptions about the population may cause misleading results.

question: Which of the following is a common cause of underfitting in a statistical model?

options.A: The model captures both the underlying trend and noise within the data, making it overly specific to the training data.
options.B: The model is too simple and does not capture the complexity of the underlying data patterns.
options.C: The model includes too many predictor variables, leading to an overly complex model.
options.D: The model performs exceptionally well on the training data but fails to generalize to new, unseen data.

correctExplanation: Underfitting occurs when a model is too simplistic to capture the underlying trends in the data. This can happen when the model lacks sufficient complexity, such as using a linear model for data with a non-linear relationship or having too few predictor variables.

question: When the relationship between the independent and dependent variables in a regression analysis is such that when x increases, y decreases by the same proportion and when x decreases, y increases by the same proportion, the correlation is said to be perfectly ______________, the correlation coefficient, r, is ____, and the regression line is _____________ sloping. Correlation R Regression line I. negative −1 downward II. negative −1 upward III. positive +1 upward IV. positive +1 downward

options.A: II.
options.B: IV.
options.C: III.
options.D: I.

correctExplanation: When the relationship between the independent variable and the dependent variable in a simple regression analysis is such that when x increases, y decreases by the same proportion and when x decreases, y increases by the same proportion, the correlation is said to be perfectly negative, the correlation coefficient, r, is −1, and the regression line is downward sloping. The correlation coefficient measures the strength of the relationship between the independent variable and the dependent variable. The coefficient of correlation expresses how closely related, or correlated, the two variables are and the extent to which a variation in the independent variable has historically resulted in a variation in the dependent variable. A correlation coefficient (r) of −1 means the linear relationship between each value for x and its corresponding value for y is perfectly negative (downsloping). When x increases, y decreases by the same proportion; when x decreases, y increases by the same proportion. In a time series, the x variable (time) can only increase, so if the correlation coefficient is negative and the regression line is downsloping, the value of y decreases with the passage of time.

explanations.A: When the relationship between the independent variable and the dependent variable in a simple regression analysis is such that when x increases, y decreases by the same proportion and when x decreases, y increases by the same proportion, the regression line is downward sloping.
explanations.B: When the relationship between the independent variable and the dependent variable in a simple regression analysis is such that when x increases, y decreases by the same proportion and when x decreases, y increases by the same proportion, the correlation is said to be perfectly negative and the correlation coefficient, r, is −1.
explanations.C: When the relationship between the independent and dependent variables in a regression analysis is such that when x increases, y decreases by the same proportion and when x decreases, y increases by the same proportion, the correlation is said to be perfectly negative, the correlation coefficient, R, is −1, and the regression line is downward sloping.

question: Which one of the following statements in regard to r-squared is not correct?

question: In a regression analysis, a residual is

options.B: A confidence interval.
options.C: A variance between the dependent and independent variables.
options.D: The standard error of the estimate.

correctExplanation: The difference between an actual, observed value of y at a given value of x and its predicted value on the calculated regression line at that value of x is called a deviation or a residual. On a graph, it is the distance between an actual value of y and its predicted value at that value of x.

explanations.B: A residual is not a confidence interval. The confidence interval is used in regression analysis to describe the amount of uncertainty caused by the sampling method used when drawing conclusions about a population based on a sample.
explanations.C: A residual is not a variance between the dependent and independent variables. Regression analysis does not involve calculation of a variance between the dependent and independent variables.
explanations.D: A residual is not the standard error of the estimate. The standard error of the estimate is the average distance that all the actual values of the dependent variable y fall from the predicted values of y on the regression line. In other words, the standard error of the estimate is the average of the residuals, not a single residual.

question: An example of a supervised learning algorithm is

correctExplanation: Simple linear regression is an example of a basic supervised learning algorithm. The x variable (the independent variable) serves as the predictor variable. The y variable (the dependent variable) is the outcome variable in the training and test data where the y value for each x value is known. explanations.B: Structured Query Language (SQL) is not an example of a supervised learning algorithm. Structured Query Language is used to allow users to query a database directly using SQL commands. explanations.C: Clustering is not an example of a supervised learning algorithm. In data mining, clustering is discovering groups in data sets that have similar characteristics without using known structures in the data or fixed groups. Clustering can be used in data reduction to reduce the number of groups to be included in the data mining algorithm. Data reduction is used in data mining to reduce the data dimension if needed by eliminating unneeded variables, transforming variables as necessary, and creating new variables. question: In the equation of a linear regression line, ŷ = a + bx, which of the following represents the slope of the line?

question: What is the error term in a regression analysis?

options.A: The standard error of each specific variable coefficient.
options.B: The T-statistic.
options.C: The standard error of the estimate.
options.D: The difference between the predicted value of y on the regression line for each value of x and the actual value of y for that value of x.

correctExplanation: The error term for each value of the independent variable x is the difference between the predicted value of y (ŷ) on the regression line for that value of x and the actual value of y for that value of x. If all of the historical data fell on the regression line, the error term for each value of x would be zero.

explanations.A: The error term in a regression analysis is not the standard error of each specific variable coefficient. The standard error of each specific variable coefficient is part of the output of a regression analysis performed on a computer. The standard error of each specific independent variable coefficient indicates the precision for the relationship between that specific independent x-variable and the dependent y-variable.
explanations.B: The error term in a regression analysis is not the T-statistic. The T-statistic, or T-value, of a given independent variable is its coefficient divided by the coefficient’s own standard error. The T-statistic indicates whether or not that independent variable has a measurable effect in explaining or predicting variations in the dependent variable.
explanations.C: The error term in a regression analysis is not the standard error of the estimate. The standard error of the estimate measures the variation in the full set of data from its mean, that is, the average distance of the residuals, or the average distance that the actual values of the dependent variable y fall from the predicted values of y (ŷ) on the regression line. It is computed as a standard deviation, with the deviations being the residuals, the distance of each actual value of y from its predicted value at that value of x. It describes how wrong the regression model is on average, using the units of the dependent variable, y.

question: In a regression analysis, what is the line of best fit?

options.A: The line of best fit is the confidence interval.
options.B: The line of best fit is the regression line.
options.C: The line of best fit connects all the points in the graph to show a trend.
options.D: The line of best fit is the line created when the independent variable or variables used in the regression are highly correlated with the observations of the dependent variable used in the regression.

correctExplanation: When the position of the regression line is calculated mathematically, the line will be in the position where the deviations, or residuals, between each actual, observed value on the graph and its predicted value on the regression line have been minimized. The resulting regression line is the line of best fit. That line may be able to be used to predict the value of y for any given value of x, if the independent variable being used (such as the passage of time for a time series) serves well as the predictor variable.

explanations.A: The line of best fit is not the confidence interval. The confidence interval is used in regression analysis to describe the amount of uncertainty caused by the sampling method used when drawing conclusions about a population based on a sample. If several samples are drawn from a population using the same sampling method and a confidence interval at a confidence level of 95% is used, 95% of the interval estimates in the samples can be expected to include the true parameter of the population. Thus, a confidence interval of 95% means that if several periods are sampled and analyzed using the same 95% confidence interval, the proportion of those sample intervals that would contain the true value of the dependent variable in the population would be equal to 95%. The line of best fit is a line that minimizes the deviations, or residuals, between each actual, observed value on the graph and its predicted value on the regression line.
explanations.C: The line of best fit does not connect all the points in the graph to show a trend. The line of best fit is a line that minimizes the deviations, or residuals, between each actual, observed value on the graph and its predicted value on the regression line.
explanations.D: The line of best fit is not the line created when the independent variable or variables used in the regression are highly correlated with the observations of the dependent variable used in the regression. The line of best fit is a line that minimizes the deviations, or residuals, between each actual, observed value on the graph and its predicted value on the regression line, and that is true regardless of how well correlated the variables are.

question: A regional bank wants to improve its loan approval process. If the predicted probability is greater than the threshold, the prediction is a "yes"; if below, a "no." The threshold can be 0.5 or any other probability the analyst decides on. In this context, it means a loan applicant will either default or not default on a loan.

explanations.A: Forecasting future loan balances involves predicting numerical values rather than binary outcomes. Logistic regression is not used to predict numerical values.
explanations.B: Grouping applicants into segments based on similar demographic characteristics is clustering. Cluster analysis does not estimate the probability that a future binary event will occur. In this scenario, management wants to predict whether a loan applicant will or will not default on the loan applied for, making logistic regression the appropriate technique.
explanations.D: Logistic regression predicts the probability of an event occurring, such as a customer’s defaulting on a loan; and that probability is then be used to classify the outcome and make a decision. However, logistic regression cannot determine the exact financial impact of an outcome such as a default.

question: A linear relationship between an independent and a dependent variable means that

options.A: the predicted values of the dependent variable corresponding to each value of the independent variable resulting from a regression analysis will graph as a straight line.
options.B: a forecast made using the historical data will be reasonably accurate.
options.C: the relationship between the two variables must be a direct one.
options.D: when the independent variable increases, the dependent variable increases by the same amount as the independent variable has increased.

correctExplanation: If the relationship between an independent variable and a dependent variable is linear, the predicted values of the dependent variable corresponding to each value of the independent variable that result from a regression analysis of the two variables will graph as a straight line on an x-y coordinate graph. For each unit that the x variable changes, a proportional change will take place in the y variable, and this proportional amount of change is a constant amount. A linear function will have the form ŷ = ax + b, where ŷ = the predicted value of y on the regression line corresponding to each value of x; a = the slope of the line (the amount by which y increases for each unit of increase in x); b = the y intercept, or the value of y when x is 0; x = the value of x on the x-axis that corresponds to the value of y on the regression line.

explanations.B: Just because a linear relationship exists between an independent variable and a dependent variable, that does not necessarily mean that a forecast made using the historical data will be reasonably accurate. In order for a forecast to be reasonably accurate, the historical changes in the two variables need to be correlated and there needs to be some reason for believing that changes in the independent variable are a cause of changes in the dependent variable. Data can be linear without much correlation and without causation being present. And even when the variables appear to be well correlated, there may be no logical causative relationship between them. For example, one might say "As electric bills increase, sales of ice cream increase. Therefore, an increase in electricity use causes an increase in sales of ice cream." Even though electricity usage and ice cream sales might increase and decrease in tandem, there is no support for the statement that an increase in electricity usage causes an increase in sales of ice cream. It is, however, very possible that both variables are being caused by a third factor, such as hot weather. A graph of temperatures on the x-axis and ice cream sales on the y-axis would likely indicate a strong correlation along with causation.
explanations.C: A direct relationship between two variables graphs as an upsloping line on an x-y coordinate graph. An upsloping line means that when the independent variable (x) increases, the dependent variable (y) also increases; and when the independent variable decreases, the dependent variable also decreases. A linear relationship may be a direct relationship, but it is not required to be a direct relationship. It may also be an inverse relationship, in which the dependent variable changes in the opposite direction from the direction of change in the independent variable.
explanations.D: It is not necessary for the dependent variable to increase by the same amount as the independent variable increases in order for a linear relationship to exist between the independent and the dependent variable. However, it is necessary for the dependent variable (y) to increase by the same amount for each unit of increase in the independent variable (x). If the amount of increase in the dependent variable varies, the line on the graph will not be a straight one and the relationship will not be a linear one.

explanations.B: Descriptive analytics report past performance. Descriptive analytics is the simplest type of data analytics. It is not the type of data analytics most likely to yield the most impact for an organization, nor is it the most complex type of data analytics.
explanations.C: Predictive analytics focus on the future using correlative analysis and historical and other data. Large quantities of data are processed to identify patterns and relationships between and among known random variables or data sets in order to make predictions about what is likely to occur in the future. A sales forecast made using past sales trends is a form of predictive analytics. Predictive data analytics is not the type of data analytics most likely to yield the most impact for an organization, nor is it the most complex type of data analytics.

studyUnit: Study Unit 16: F.4. Types of Data Analytics

question: A consumer products company is evaluating several proposed data analytics projects to improve its marketing efforts. Management wants to use customer demographic information, including age, gender, and household income, to determine which prospective customers should receive a promotional offer because they are most likely to respond favorably. Which of the following analytical techniques would best support management's objective?

options.A: Cluster analysis
options.B: Logistic regression
options.C: Linear regression
options.D: Time-series analysis

correctExplanation: Logistic regression is used to estimate the probability of a binary outcome based on identified factors. In this situation, it estimates the likelihood that a prospective customer will respond favorably to a promotional offer based on demographic information, allowing management to target customers most likely to respond.

explanations.A: Cluster analysis is used to group customers with similar characteristics but does not estimate the probability that a customer will respond to a promotional offer.
explanations.C: Linear regression analysis would not support management’s objective. Linear regression analysis is a statistical technique that is used to develop a mathematical equation that models the extent to which one variable (called the dependent or response variable) has historically been affected by one or more other variables (called the independent or predictor variables). If the historical relationship between the cause (or causes) and the effect has been sufficiently strong, regression analysis using the historical data can be used to make decisions and predictions about the dependent variable. Thus, linear regression predicts numerical outcomes rather than binary outcomes.
explanations.D: Time-series analysis is used to forecast future values based on historical trends rather than predict binary outcomes.

question: Which of the following scenarios illustrates a challenge related to overfitting when fitting an analytical model to data?

options.A: The model uses a small set of variables and therefore, it fails to capture the complex relationships in the data, resulting in poor predictions.
options.B: The model consistently underpredicts the total number of sales due to a simple linear regression approach.
options.C: The model accurately predicts the future sales revenue based on a large dataset spanning several years.
options.D: The model performs well on historical data but fails to predict future outcomes accurately because it has memorized noise in the training data.

correctExplanation: Overfitting occurs when a model learns not only the underlying patterns but also the random fluctuations, or noise, in the training data. This results in excellent performance on the training data but poor generalization to new, unseen data.

explanations.A: This scenario describes underfitting, where the model is not complex enough to capture the necessary relationships in the data, leading to inaccurate predictions.
explanations.B: This scenario describes underfitting, where the model is too simple to capture the complexity of the data, leading to poor predictions.
explanations.C: This scenario describes a well-fitted model that generalizes well to future data, which is the opposite of overfitting.

question: Which of the following is not a true statement?

options.B: A simple linear regression has only one independent variable.
options.C: A simple linear regression has only one dependent variable.
options.D: A multiple linear regression has more than one independent variable.

correctExplanation: This is not a true statement. The difference between simple linear regression and multiple linear regression is in the number of independent variables. A simple linear regression has only one independent variable and one dependent variable. A multiple linear regression has more than one independent variable and one dependent variable. Therefore, a multiple linear regression does not have more than one dependent variable.

explanations.B: This is a true statement. A simple linear regression has only one independent variable and only one dependent variable.

options.C: A time series may exhibit multiple patterns.

question: A company has accumulated data for the last 24 months in order to determine if there is an independent variable that could be used to estimate shipping costs. Three possible independent variables being considered are packages shipped, miles shipped, and pounds shipped. The quantitative technique that should be used to determine whether any of these independent variables might provide a good estimate for shipping costs is

options.A: flexible budgeting.
options.B: linear regression.
options.C: variable costing.
options.D: linear programming.

correctExplanation: Historical data on each of the independent variables being considered – packages shipped, miles shipped, and pounds shipped – should be regressed separately in a simple regression against the historical data on shipping costs, the dependent variable. From each separate regression, the resulting coefficient of correlation should be evaluated to determine whether there is a strong correlation between the independent variable and historical shipping costs. The coefficient of correlation is a numerical measure between +1 and −1 that results from the regression analysis and indicates the strength of the relationship between the independent and dependent variables. A coefficient of correlation that is close to +1 indicates a strong positive linear relationship between the independent and dependent variable, while a coefficient of correlation that is close to −1 indicates a strong inverse, or negative, linear relationship between the independent and dependent variable.

explanations.A: Flexible budgeting is not used to estimate or forecast a dependent variable using historical data on an independent variable.
explanations.C: Variable costing is not used to estimate or forecast a dependent variable using historical data on an independent variable.
explanations.D: Linear programming is not used to estimate or forecast a dependent variable using historical data on an independent variable.

question: Which of the following would not be a type of pattern of a time series analysis?

options.A: Basic.
options.B: Seasonal.
options.C: Cyclical.
options.D: Trend.

correctExplanation: “Basic” is not the name of a type of time series pattern. A time series—a sequence of measurements taken at equally-spaced, ordered points in time—may have one or more of four patterns (also called components) that influence its behavior over time: Trend pattern or component Cyclical pattern or component Seasonal pattern or component Irregular pattern or component

explanations.B: "Seasonal" is the name of a type of time series pattern. A seasonal pattern is a pattern in a time series that fluctuates within a period such as a year due to seasonality. The variability due to seasonal influences is called the seasonal component.
explanations.C: "Cyclical" is the name of a time series pattern. A cyclical pattern in a time series is one that fluctuates within a period lasting longer than a year, and it is attributable to the cyclical component in the time series. Usually in sales data, a cyclical component is due to the cyclical nature of the economy.
explanations.D: "Trend" is the name of a type of time series pattern. A trend pattern in a time series exhibits a gradual shifting to a higher or lower level. Short-term fluctuations may take place within the trend, but the long-term trend is apparent.
