topic: Just-In-Time Systems and MRP, MRPII, ERP
question: One of the benefits of implementing a just-in-time manufacturing system is

options.A: reduced costs for reworking defective outputs.
options.B: lower foreign exchange risk when working with international suppliers.
options.C: increased number of external suppliers gains better control.
options.D: faster response to customers because of higher inventory buffer stocks.

correctExplanation: A benefit of just-in-time production is greater emphasis on improving quality by eliminating the causes of rework, scrap, and waste, thereby reducing costs for reworking defective outputs. Just-in-time manufacturing requires manufacturing problems and defects to be solved as quickly as possible. Because of the close coordination needed between and among workstations and the minimum inventories held at each workstation, defects caused at one workstation very quickly affect other workstations. For JIT manufacturing to be successful, problems and defects must be solved by eliminating their root causes as quickly as possible. Because problems with quality are resolved quickly, the causes of rework, scrap, and waste are virtually eliminated, leading to improved quality and reduction of rework costs.

explanations.B: A just-in-time manufacturing system does not have any effect on a company's foreign exchange risk. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.C: A just-in-time manufacturing system does not rely on an increased number of external suppliers. The important thing is not the number of suppliers but the relationships between the company and its suppliers. Because inventory levels are kept low in a JIT system, the company must have very close relationships with its suppliers to make certain that the suppliers make frequent deliveries of smaller amounts of inventory. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.D: In a just-in-time system, the company does not have higher inventory buffer stocks. The levels of inventories held in the plant at all stages of production, including raw materials, work-in-process, and finished goods, are minimized. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

topic: Just-In-Time Systems and MRP, MRPII, ERP
question: Which one of the following is not an expected benefit of implementing a just-in-time (JIT) production system?

options.A: Lower total storage costs.
options.B: Lower total rework cost.
options.C: Lower total set-up costs.
options.D: Lower manufacturing lead time.

correctExplanation: A goal of JIT is to reduce batch setup time. However, reducing batch setup time does not mean that total setup costs are decreased. The savings comes from the fact that the reduction in batch setup time makes production of smaller batches more economical, enables inventory reductions, allows the company to respond quickly to changes in customer demand, and decreases manufacturing lead times.

explanations.A: Lower total storage costs is an expected benefit of implementing a just-in-time (JIT) production system. The primary advantage of a JIT inventory management system is reduction in the cost of carrying the inventory. In addition to reducing the amount invested in the inventory, the cost savings include reduction in the risk of damage, theft, loss, or a lack of ability to sell the finished goods.
explanations.B: Lower total rework cost is an expected benefit of implementing a just-in-time (JIT) production system. Part of the process of implementing JIT includes solving problems and defects by eliminating their root causes as quickly as possible. Therefore, expected benefits of JIT production include greater emphasis on improving quality by eliminating the causes of rework, scrap, and waste, which in turn reduces the cost of rework, scrap, and waste.
explanations.D: Lower manufacturing lead time is an expected benefit of implementing a just-in-time (JIT) production system. A goal of JIT is to reduce batch setup time because reduced setup time makes production of smaller batches more economical. The smaller batches enable inventory reductions and enable the company to respond quickly to changes in customer demand. The reduced setup time also leads to lower manufacturing lead times.

topic: Just-In-Time Systems and MRP, MRPII, ERP
question: An advantage of an enterprise resource planning system is that

options.A: its implementation improves business processes.
options.B: the system can be easily customized to suit the unique needs of the organization.
options.C: the comprehensiveness of the system reduces resistance to change.
options.D: it can usually be installed by organizations of all sizes.

correctExplanation: One of the advantages of an ERP system is that day-to-day operations are facilitated. All employees can easily gain access to real-time information that they need to do their jobs. Ready access by managers facilitates their decision-making and control over the factors of production. Other advantages of an ERP system are: Operational costs are reduced. Communication is improved across departments, leading to greater efficiencies in production, planning, and decision-making that can lead to lower production costs, lower marketing expenses, and other efficiencies. Inventory management is facilitated. Detailed inventory records are available, simplifying inventory transactions. Inventories can be managed more effectively to keep them at optimal levels. Resource planning as a part of strategic planning is simplified. Senior management has access to the information it needs in order to do strategic planning.

explanations.B: Some ERP software can be easily customized, and some cannot. Regardless of whether it is customizable or not, customization is not an advantage of an enterprise resource planning system.
explanations.C: There is nothing about an ERP system that can have any effect on employees' resistance to change.
explanations.D: It is true that a new generation of ERP systems have become available that are targeted to small and mid-sized businesses. They are easier to install, easier to manage, and require less implementation time and less startup cost than the first generation systems that were practical only for large businesses. This has made ERP systems more accessible to organizations of all sizes. However, that is not an advantage of an enterprise resource planning system.

topic: Just-In-Time Systems and MRP, MRPII, ERP
question: Successful implementation of a just-in-time (JIT) inventory system requires all of the following except

options.A: close coordination between and among work stations.
options.B: close relationships with suppliers.
options.C: each worker is able to operate all machinery and perform all supporting tasks.
options.D: use of Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) software.

correctExplanation: Enterprise Resource Planning software integrates all departments and functions across a company onto a single computer system with a single database so that the information needed by all areas of the company will be available to the people who need it for planning, manufacturing, order fulfillment, and other purposes. Use of Enterprise Resource Planning software is not required in order to implement a Just-In-Time (JIT) inventory system.

explanations.A: The company must be reorganized along lean manufacturing lines, to permit close coordination between and among work stations. The plant layout is arranged by manufacturing cells or work cells that each produce a product, or product type.
explanations.B: Close relationships with suppliers are required because inventory levels are kept low. The suppliers must make frequent deliveries of smaller amounts of inventory.
explanations.C: The company must be reorganized to permit lean manufacturing, where the plant layout is arranged by manufacturing cells or work cells that produce a product, or product type. Each worker in a manufacturing cell knows how to operate all machines in that cell and can perform supporting tasks within that cell, which lessens downtime resulting from breakdowns or employee absences.

topic: Just-In-Time Systems and MRP, MRPII, ERP
question: A production system in which a unit is produced only when needed in the next step in the production line is called a

options.A: just-in-time system.
options.B: back-flush system.
options.C: Pareto system.
options.D: material requirements planning system.

correctExplanation: The main idea of JIT is that nothing is produced until the next process in the assembly line needs it. In other words, nothing is produced until a customer orders it, and then it is produced very quickly. In a JIT system, inventory is purchased so that it will be delivered just as needed for production. The goal of a JIT system is to minimize the level of inventories held in the plant at all stages of production, including raw materials, work-in-process, and finished goods inventories while meeting customer demand in a timely manner with high-quality products at the lowest possible cost.

explanations.B: This is not a back-flush system. There is no such thing as a back-flush production system. However, backflush costing is a costing method that is usually used with a just-in-time production system. In backflush costing, the total costs of a production run are recorded in the accounting system only at the end of the process, either when the finished goods are transferred to finished goods inventory, or when they are sold and the expense is recognized as cost of goods sold expense. No work-in-process inventories are carried. Back-flush costing is outside the scope of the CMA exams. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.C: There is no such system as a Pareto system. The Pareto principle is the 80:20 principle that can be applied to various situations. The Pareto principle states that 80% of consequences come from 20% of the causes. For example, if there is a problem with production, after management pinpoints which 20% of the causes are accounting for 80% of the problems, it can focus its efforts on improving the areas that are likely to have the greatest overall impact. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.D: A Material Requirements Planning (MRP) system is not a production system in which a unit is produced only when needed in the next step in the production line. Material Requirements Planning systems are used to help determine what raw materials to order for production, when to order them, and how much to order. An MRP system can be used with various types of production systems. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

question: A company is planning to implement a just-in-time (JIT) inventory management system. All of the following are benefits expected from implementing JIT inventory management except

options.A: higher inventory turnover.
options.B: lower investment in inventory.
options.C: lower obsolescence and other carrying costs.

Therefore, fewer defects and less rework are not a benefit of a JIT inventory management system, though they are required on the production side of a JIT system and so are a benefit of JIT production.

explanations.B: Reduction in the amount of inventory carried and thus a reduction in the amount of investment in inventory is an advantage of a JIT inventory management system.
explanations.C: Reduction in the amount of inventory carried and thus reductions in inventory obsolescence and minimization of other carrying costs are advantages of a JIT inventory management system.

options.D: Master-budget capacity as the denominator level will result in a lower net income amount than if theoretical capacity is chosen.

correctExplanation: The most important fact given here is that variances are adjustments to cost of goods sold. If variances are prorated among cost of goods sold, finished goods inventory and work in process inventory, the choice of a denominator level will make no difference in net income, because net income will be the same no matter which denominator level is chosen. However, when all variances are adjustments to cost of goods sold, the choice of the denominator level will make a difference in net income. By using the practical level, a smaller amount of overhead will go to each unit than if the master-budget level is used. Therefore, less overhead will be included in ending inventory at the end of the period. Since there is less overhead on the balance sheet, there will be more overhead on the income statement since variances go to cost of goods sold. More overhead on the income statement will lead to a lower net income.

explanations.A: Because the normal capacity has the highest overhead rate, more overhead will be included in inventory using this capacity than any other. Therefore, using normal capacity will lead to a higher income than any of the other methods.
explanations.B: Because the practical capacity is higher than the normal capacity, the normal capacity level will lead to higher overhead costs per unit. Therefore, the normal capacity level will lead to more overhead being included in inventory and a higher income than the practical capacity would give.
explanations.D: Because the master-budget capacity is less than theoretical, the master-budget capacity will allocate more overhead to each unit. This means that there will be more overhead costs in inventory using the master-budget capacity and therefore a higher net income.

question: Which one of the following lists of functions is in proper value chain order?

correctExplanation: Research and development, marketing, and customer service is the correct order of those functions in the value chain. The primary activities in the value chain, in order of their completion, are: research & development, production, marketing & sales, and customer services. Research provides a company with needed knowledge for creating new or improving existing products, services or processes. Development uses those research findings to develop and improve the company’s products, processes, or services. The next step is design, which is the detailed planning and engineering for these efforts. Design is followed by production, which is the acquisition, coordination and assembly required to produce a product or deliver a service. Once the product is available for sale, marketing and sales, including advertising, promotion and sales activities, create the sales. Distribution involves delivery of products or services to customers after the sales are made. Customer service includes customer support and warranty services after a sale takes place.

explanations.A: Production design would logically have to come before production.
explanations.C: Distribution involves delivery of products or services to customers after the sales are made, and customer service cannot be provided until the goods or services are in the hands of the purchasers.
explanations.D: Distribution involves delivery of products or services to customers after the sales are made. Marketing efforts are required to make the sales. So marketing would logically have to come before distribution.

question: From the perspective of the management accountant, which one of the following represents a major disadvantage of business process reengineering?

options.D: The focus is, to a large extent, on short-term results.

correctExplanation: Business process reengineering involves analyzing and radically redesigning the work flow. Radical redesign means throwing out the old procedures and inventing new ways of getting the work done. As a business process is disassembled in order to be restructured, the internal controls that have been developed for the process will need to be revised or completely rewritten in order to effectively control the restructured process. If that step is overlooked, management will have no internal controls over the new process, leaving the company vulnerable to failure to achieve its objectives.

explanations.A: One of the basic premises of business process reengineering is that information should be captured only once, and it should appear simultaneously every place it is needed. If someone is taking information from one system and inputting it into another, that is a process that is broken and needs to be reengineered. Therefore, business process reengineering is likely to result in an increased use of centralized databases.
explanations.B: A legacy system is defined as a computer system that has been in operation for a long time, and whose functions are too essential to be disrupted by upgrading or integration with another system. Business process reengineering involves analyzing and radically redesigning the work flow. Radical redesign means throwing out the old procedures and inventing new ways of getting the work done. A reengineered process would not use a legacy system but instead would require a new system.
explanations.D: The focus of business process reengineering is on long-term results.

question: To achieve total quality management (TQM), the company must identify the relevant quality problems when and/or where they occur, and then use methods to analyze them. Which of the following is not one of these methods?

explanations.A: A Pareto diagram is used in analyzing qualify problems in a TQM environment. A Pareto diagram is a specific type of histogram. Utilizing the Pareto 80-20 principle (20% of the population causes 80% of the problems), it helps management to pinpoint which 20% of the causes are accounting for 80% of the problems. In this way, it helps management to focus efforts on improving the areas that are likely to have the greatest overall positive impact.
explanations.B: A histogram is a method for analyzing quality problems in a TQM environment. A histogram is a bar graph that shows the frequency of events in a set of data. Patterns that may not be apparent when just looking at a set of numbers become clear in a histogram, and problem areas can be pinpointed. For instance, if a particular production line is experiencing most of the difficulty, a histogram can help determine what types of problems are occurring most frequently.
explanations.D: A control chart is a method used in analyzing quality problems in a TQM environment. A control chart records observations of an operation taken at regular intervals. If there are trends, clusters, or many measurements outside or nearly outside the specified range, the process may be out of control.

question: Of these statements, which is not relevant to the overall benchmarking process?

options.A: Management uses target costing to set standard costs in order to put the focus on the market as well as on what target price to charge because the company must attain the target cost to realize its desired profit margin for the product.
options.B: Target costing utilizes kaizen to reduce costs in order to attain a desired profit margin.
options.C: Management determines what processes the company uses to convert materials, capital and labor into value-adding products.
options.D: Management puts into place a program to measure the organization against the products, practices and services of the most efficient competitors in its marketplace.

correctExplanation: Benchmarking involves measuring the company’s products, practices, and services against successful competitors, using the competitors’ standards as goals for its own operations. This “best practices” process helps the company to cut costs, boost output and achieve competitive advantage. The first step in benchmarking is to identify the critical success factors for the business and the processes it needs to benchmark. However, that is not the same thing as determining what the processes are that the company uses to convert materials, capital, and labor into value-adding products. Determining what processes the company uses to convert materials, capital and labor into value-adding products is not part of benchmarking because those processes should already be known. In order to do benchmarking, the company needs to identify the critical success factors involved in those processes. The critical success factors that need to be identified are the aspects of the company’s performance that are essential to its competitive advantage and therefore to its success.

explanations.A: This is relevant to the overall benchmarking process. Benchmarking involves measuring the company’s products, practices and services against successful competitors, using the competitors’ standards as goals for its own operations. This “best practices” analysis is then used to make improvements in the company's processes to match or beat the benchmark, such as cutting costs, boosting output, and achieving competitive advantage. Target costing is a means of making those improvements, because target costing is a way to find methods of cutting costs. Target costing starts with a target price based on the market price, and the company must attain the target cost if it is going to realize its desired gross profit margin for the product. The target cost is achieved through development of new manufacturing methods and techniques that entail continuous improvement or the ongoing search for new ways to reduce costs. Companies use target costing to set standard costs that will create the desired gross profit margin for their products sold at the target price.
explanations.B: This is relevant to the overall benchmarking process. Benchmarking involves measuring the company’s products, practices and services against successful competitors, using the competitors’ standards as goals for its own operations. This “best practices” analysis is then used to make improvements in the company's processes to match or beat the benchmark, such as cutting costs, boosting output, and achieving competitive advantage. Target costing is a means of making those improvements, because target costing is a way to find methods of cutting costs. Target costing starts with a target price based on the market price, and the company must attain the target cost if it is going to realize its desired gross profit margin for the product. Using kaizen principles, the company figures out how it can manufacture the product at the target cost. The target cost is achieved through development of new manufacturing methods and techniques that entail continuous improvement or the ongoing search for new ways to reduce costs.
explanations.D: This is relevant to the overall benchmarking process. Putting into place a program to measure the organization against the products, practices, and services of the most efficient competitors in its marketplace is the definition of benchmarking. Benchmarking continuously strives to imitate the performance of the best companies in the world or the best units in the company, and through meeting these higher standards, the organization may be able to create a competitive advantage over its marketplace competitors.

question: A principle of good corporate governance is the independence of its directors. Of the following, which director(s) would not be considered independent? I. The director is the brother-in-law of the CEO. II. The director's brother is the CEO of the company's major supplier. III. The director retired as CEO from the company six months ago. IV. The director owns a thousand shares of a mutual fund that has an investment in the company.

options.A: II and III only.
options.B: I and II only.
options.C: I, II, and III only.
options.D: None of the directors would be considered independent.

correctExplanation: An independent director is one who has no professional or personal ties (either current or former) to the company or its management. The directors in situations I, II and III would not be considered independent because of their current personal or former professional ties with the company. However, the director who owns shares in a mutual fund that has an investment in the company would be independent. Mutual funds invest in many different types of companies. The fact that the director has a mutual fund that has investment in the company would not impair the director's independence because the director would not control the specific investments of the mutual fund.

explanations.A: An independent director is one who has no professional or personal ties (either current or former) to the company or its management. In both II and III, the director has a personal relationship with someone connected to the company and is therefore not independent. However, these are not the only directors who are not independent.
explanations.B: An independent director is one who has no professional or personal ties (either current or former) to the company or its management. In both I and II, the director has a personal relationship with someone connected to the company and is therefore not independent. However, these are not the only directors who are not independent.
explanations.D: The director in one of the situations would be considered independent.

question: Which of the following would be of greatest concern to an auditor reviewing a policy regarding the sale of a company’s used PCs to outside parties?

options.A: Whether there is terminal emulation software on the computer.
options.B: Whether deleted files on the hard disk drive have been completely erased.
options.C: Whether the computer has viruses.
options.D: Whether all software on the computer is properly licensed.

correctExplanation: While most delete programs erase file pointers, they do not remove the underlying data. The company must use special utilities that fully erase the data. This is important because of the potential for confidential data on the PCs.

explanations.A: Terminal emulation software is widely available.
explanations.C: This could create a liability for the company if a virus destroyed the purchasing party’s data or programs. However, the purchasing party should use anti-virus software to detect and eliminate any viruses. This concern, while important, is not as serious as the correct response.
explanations.D: The purchasing party has a responsibility to ensure that all their software is properly licensed. If the company represented that all the software was properly licensed, this could create a liability. However, this liability is not as serious as the implication from the correct response.

question: Corporate governance is best described as

options.A: the process of implementing strategic plans.
options.B: the system of planning and allocating resources.
options.C: a system that maximizes shareholder wealth.
options.D: the means by which businesses are directed and controlled.

correctExplanation: Corporate governance includes all the means by which businesses are directed and controlled, including the rules, regulations, processes, customs, policies, procedures, institutions, and laws that affect the way the business is administered. It is a system by which an organization makes and implements decisions in pursuit of its objectives. Corporate governance spells out the rules and procedures to be followed in making decisions for the corporation for the purpose of meeting its various stakeholders’ objectives. A corporation’s stakeholders include all those who are affected by its actions: its board of directors, its shareholders, its management, its employees, its customers, its suppliers, its creditors, the community, and the government.

explanations.A: Corporate governance is not the process of implementing strategic plans. The process of implementing strategic plans involves developing tactical plans, which are designed to implement specific parts of the strategic plan. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.B: Corporate governance is not the system of planning and allocating resources. Planning and allocation of resources take place during the strategic planning and budgeting processes. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.C: Corporate governance is not a system that maximizes shareholder wealth. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

question: Good governance states that boards of directors should consist of independent, non-executive directors. Some of the ways to ensure independence would be all of the following except

question: Which of the following is not an appropriate member of an audit committee?

options.A: A retired executive of a firm that had been associated with the organization.
options.B: The organization's vice president of operations.
options.C: An academic specializing in business administration.
options.D: The vice president of the local bank used by the organization.

correctExplanation: Requirements for audit committee members are: They must be independent. That is, they must not be employed by the company in any capacity other than as a member of the audit committee, the board of directors, or any other board committee. One member of the audit committee must have accounting or financial management expertise. All members of the audit committee must be financially literate. The organization's vice president of operations is a member of management and thus would not be independent.

explanations.A: Requirements for audit committee members are: They must be independent. That is, they must not be employed by the company in any capacity other than as a member of the audit committee, the board of directors, or any other board committee. One member of the audit committee must have accounting or financial management expertise. All members of the audit committee must be financially literate. A retired executive of a firm that had been associated with the organization would be an independent director and as an executive, would be financially literate. Thus, this person would be an appropriate member of the audit committee.
explanations.C: Requirements for audit committee members are: They must be independent. That is, they must not be employed by the company in any capacity other than as a member of the audit committee, the board of directors, or any other board committee. One member of the audit committee must have accounting or financial management expertise. All members of the audit committee must be financially literate. An academic specializing in business administration would be an independent director and with knowledge of business administration would be financially literate. Thus, this person would be an appropriate member of the audit committee.
explanations.D: Requirements for audit committee members are: They must be independent. That is, they must not be employed by the company in any capacity other than as a member of the audit committee, the board of directors, or any other board committee. One member of the audit committee must have accounting or financial management expertise. All members of the audit committee must be financially literate. The vice president of the local bank would be an independent director and, as the vice president of a bank, would be financially literate. Thus, this person would be an appropriate member of the audit committee.

question: Which one of the following statements is correct?

options.A: Residual risks can only be assessed but not protected against.
options.B: Fraud can be eliminated by internal controls.
options.C: Inherent risk can only be addressed by top management.
options.D: Residual risk remains after management has implemented internal controls.

correctExplanation: The definition of residual risk is "the level of risk that remains after management has taken action to mitigate a risk" according to Enterprise Risk Management: Frameworks, Elements and Integration, published by the Institute of Management Accountants (IMA) as part of their Statements on Management Accounting series. Internal control cannot provide a guarantee that an organization will achieve its financial reporting, operational, and compliance objectives. No matter how well designed and operated it is, internal control can provide only reasonable assurance to management and the board of directors that the organization’s objectives will be achieved. Controls may fail because of human error, they may be circumvented by collusion, or management may override internal control procedures. Therefore, the level of risk that remains after management has implemented internal controls is the residual risk.

explanations.A: Residual risk is "the level of risk that remains after management has taken action to mitigate a risk," according to Enterprise Risk Management: Frameworks, Elements and Integration, published by the Institute of Management Accountants (IMA) as part of their Statements on Management Accounting series. An example of a residual risk is the annual deductible amount on an insurance policy that the insured must pay before the insurance will reimburse a loss. Although the insured must pay it each year if a loss occurs, the insured can set up an allowance for the deductible amount it expects to owe each year and/or set aside funds to cover it. Therefore, although residual risk is risk that remains, it can be protected against.
explanations.B: Fraud cannot be eliminated by internal controls. No internal control can provide a guarantee that fraud will not occur. For example, despite segregation of duties, two or more employees could collude with one another (work together to conspire) to commit fraud, covering for one another and, presumably, sharing the proceeds. Or a manager could override an internal control and take advantage of the opportunity to commit fraud.
explanations.C: Inherent risk is the susceptibility to a material mistake that exists “just because.” It is risk that is natural, assuming no controls are in place. Action to address inherent risk is not limited to top management.

studyUnit: Study Unit 3: E.1. Introduction to Internal Controls

question: When management of the sales department has the opportunity to override the system of internal controls of the accounting department, a weakness exists in

options.A: information and communication.
options.B: monitoring.
options.C: risk management.
options.D: the control environment.

correctExplanation: The control environment is a component of internal control. The control environment involves the structures, authorities, and responsibilities of employees. The control environment should include commitments to integrity, ethical values, and competence, and it should include a system to hold people accountable for their internal control responsibilities. If a manager can override (disregard) the internal control system, that is a weakness of the control environment because a manager overriding the internal control system violates the manager’s internal control responsibilities.

explanations.A: Information and communication is a component of internal control. It is the process of identifying, capturing, and sharing relevant information to enable people to carry out their internal control responsibilities. A manager having the ability to override (disregard) the internal control system is not a weakness in the information and communication of internal controls.
explanations.B: Monitoring activities are a component of internal control. Monitoring is the overseeing by management of the internal control system's performance over time to determine whether the components of internal control are present and functioning. A manager having the ability to override (disregard) the internal control system is not a weakness in the monitoring of internal controls.
explanations.C: Risk management is forecasting and evaluating risks and identifying procedures to mitigate or avoid them. A manager having the ability to override (disregard) the internal control system is a risk, but it is not a weakness in risk management.

studyUnit: Study Unit 3: E.1. Introduction to Internal Controls

question: A company has established policies that emphasize hiring competent people and providing them with professional training. This aligns most closely with which one of the five major components of COSO’s internal control framework?

options.A: Information and communication.
options.B: Control environment.
options.C: Monitoring.
options.D: Risk assessment.

correctExplanation: Establishing policies that emphasize hiring competent people and providing them with professional training aligns most closely with the control environment component of COSO's internal control framework. Organizations with effective control environments have several characteristics, one of which is that they demonstrate a commitment to attract, develop, and retain competent individuals. The company needs to have competent personnel in order for tasks to be accomplished in accordance with the company’s objectives and plans for achievement of those objectives. In order to have competent personnel, management should specify the knowledge and skills required for each position. Formal or informal job descriptions should specify the competence level needed for each job, and the company should make every effort to hire and retain competent people and to train them when necessary.

explanations.A: Establishing policies that emphasize hiring competent people and providing them with professional training does not align with the information and communication component of COSO's internal control framework. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.C: Establishing policies that emphasize hiring competent people and providing them with professional training does not align with the monitoring activities component of COSO's internal control framework. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.D: Establishing policies that emphasize hiring competent people and providing them with professional training does not align with the risk assessment component of COSO's internal control framework. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

question: The procedure requiring preparation of a prelisting of incoming cash receipts, with copies of the prelist going to the cashier and to accounting, is an example of which type of control?

options.A: Corrective.
options.B: Detective.
options.C: Directive.
options.D: Preventive.

correctExplanation: Prelisting incoming cash receipts is a preventive control designed to prevent undesirable events from occurring. In this case, an undesirable event is the disappearance of cash payments. The prelist should be made at the earliest possible time, in order to establish accountability for the cash.

explanations.A: Prelisting incoming cash receipts is a preventive control which is designed to prevent undesirable events from occurring, not a corrective control designed to correct undesirable events after they occur.
explanations.B: Prelisting incoming cash receipts is a preventive control which is designed to prevent undesirable events from occurring, not a detective control, which is designed to expose an error or a fraud after it occurs.
explanations.C: Prelisting incoming cash receipts is a preventive control which is designed to prevent undesirable events from occurring, not a directive control, which is designed to ensure the occurrence of a desirable event.

question: When an organization has strong internal control, management can expect various benefits. The benefit least likely to occur is

explanations.C: Strong internal control will result in some assurance of compliance with the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002, and thus that is a benefit.

question: Which one of the following statements in regard to internal controls is not true?

options.A: Control activities are the policies and procedures that help ensure that management directives are carried out.
options.B: Control environment is the foundation for all other components of internal control, providing discipline and structure.
options.C: Monitoring is a process that penalizes managers for breakdowns in internal control.

correctExplanation: This statement is not true. Monitoring is the process of evaluating the controls over time to determine whether the components of the internal control system are present and functioning and revisiting previously identified problems to make sure they have been corrected.

explanations.B: This statement is true. The control environment includes the standards, processes, and structures that provide the foundation for all of the other components of internal control.
explanations.D: This statement is true. Risk assessment is the process of identifying, analyzing, and managing the risks that have the potential to prevent the entity from achieving its objectives.

question: Accounting controls are concerned with the safeguarding of assets and the reliability of financial records. Consequently, these controls are designed to provide reasonable assurance that all of the following take place except

options.A: Executing transactions in accordance with management's general or specific authorization.
options.B: Permitting access to assets in accordance with management's authorization.
options.C: Compliance with methods and procedures ensuring operational efficiency and adherence to managerial policies.
options.D: Comparing recorded assets with existing assets at periodic intervals and taking appropriate action with respect to differences.

correctExplanation: Compliance with methods and procedures ensuring operational efficiency and adherence to managerial policies is an objective of operational control, not accounting control.

explanations.A: The safeguarding of assets and reliability of financial records requires that transactions be executed in accordance with management's general or specific authorization.
explanations.B: The safeguarding of assets and reliability of financial records requires that management control who can have access to the assets to be safeguarded.
explanations.D: The safeguarding of assets and reliability of financial records requires that physical assets be compared with recorded assets at periodic intervals, and that action be taken to resolve any differences.

question: Which one of the following is an example of a preventive control?

options.A: Audits of payroll accounts and disbursements.
options.B: Reconciliation of petty cash accounts.
options.C: Supervisory review and approval of payroll information before disbursement.
options.D: Supervisory review of monthly bank reconciliations.

correctExplanation: Preventive controls are controls designed to avoid an unintended event such as an error or fraud before it occurs. Supervisory review and approval of payroll information before disbursement can prevent errors in the payroll before the payments are made, so it is a preventive control.

explanations.A: Preventive controls are controls designed to avoid an unintended event such as an error or fraud before it occurs. Audits of payroll accounts and disbursements are a detective control because they are designed to discover an unintended event after it has occurred but before the ultimate objective has occurred, for example before financial statements are issued.
explanations.B: Preventive controls are controls designed to avoid an unintended event such as an error or fraud before it occurs. Reconciliation of petty cash accounts is a detective control because it is designed to discover an unintended event after it has occurred but before the ultimate objective has occurred, for example before financial statements are issued.
explanations.D: Preventive controls are controls designed to avoid an unintended event such as an error or fraud before it occurs. Supervisory review of monthly bank reconciliations is a detective control because it is designed to discover an unintended event after it has occurred but before the ultimate objective has occurred, for example before financial statements are issued.

question: Which of the following hiring procedures provides the most control over the accuracy of information submitted on an employment application?

options.A: The hiring organization calls the last place of employment for each finalist to verify the employment length and position held.
options.B: Letters of recommendation that attest to the applicant’s character must be mailed directly to the hiring organization rather than being submitted by the applicant.
options.C: Applicants are required to sign that the information on the application is true and correct as a confirmation of the truth of the information in the application.
options.D: Applicants are required to submit unofficial copies of their transcripts along with the application as verification of their educational credentials.

correctExplanation: This represents an independent verification of employment because the hiring organization is performing the verification process.

explanations.B: There is nothing to prevent the applicants from writing the letters themselves, putting fraudulent return address information on the letters, and mailing them.

question: A restaurant food chain has over 680 restaurants. All food orders for each restaurant are required to be input into an electronic device which records all food orders by food servers and transmits the order to the kitchen for preparation. All food servers are responsible for collecting cash for all their orders and must turn in cash at the end of their shift equal to the sales value of food ordered for their I.D. number. The manager then reconciles the cash received for the day with the computerized record of food orders generated. All differences are investigated immediately by the restaurant. Corporate headquarters has established monitoring controls to determine when an individual restaurant might not be recording all its revenue and transmitting the applicable cash to the corporate headquarters. Which one of the following would be the best example of a monitoring activity?

options.A: Management prepares a detailed analysis of gross margin per store and investigates any store that shows a significantly lower gross margin.
options.B: The restaurant manager reconciles the cash received with the food orders recorded on the computer.
options.C: Cash is transmitted to corporate headquarters on a daily basis.
options.D: All food orders must be entered on the computer, and segregation of duties is maintained between the food servers and the cooks.

correctExplanation: There are five interrelated components that comprise internal control. They are: (1) control environment, (2) risk assessment, (3) control activities, (4) information and communication, and (5) monitoring. Monitoring is an activity of management. Monitoring assesses the quality of the internal control system's performance over time. Monitoring can be done in two ways: (1) through ongoing monitoring during normal operations, and (2) separate evaluations by management with the assistance of the internal audit activity. If monitoring is done regularly during normal operations, it lessens the need for separate evaluations. When management prepares a detailed analysis of gross margin per store and investigates any store that shows a significantly lower gross margin, it is performing a monitoring activity.

explanations.B: There are five interrelated components that comprise internal control. They are: (1) control environment, (2) risk assessment, (3) control activities, (4) information and communication, and (5) monitoring. Monitoring is an activity of management. Monitoring assesses the quality of the internal control system's performance over time. Monitoring can be done in two ways: (1) through ongoing monitoring during normal operations, and (2) separate evaluations by management with the assistance of the internal audit activity. If monitoring is done regularly during normal operations, it lessens the need for separate evaluations. The manager's reconciliation of cash received with food orders entered is a control activity. A reconciliation is a detective control activity, because it is intended to detect the occurrence of an unwanted event. However, it does not represent a monitoring activity of management.
explanations.C: There are five interrelated components that comprise internal control. They are: (1) control environment, (2) risk assessment, (3) control activities, (4) information and communication, and (5) monitoring. Monitoring is an activity of management. Monitoring assesses the quality of the internal control system's performance over time. Monitoring can be done in two ways: (1) through ongoing monitoring during normal operations, and (2) separate evaluations by management with the assistance of the internal audit activity. If monitoring is done regularly during normal operations, it lessens the need for separate evaluations. Daily transmission of cash to corporate headquarters is a control activity which serves as an operational control.
explanations.D: There are five interrelated components that comprise internal control. They are: (1) control environment, (2) risk assessment, (3) control activities, (4) information and communication, and (5) monitoring. Monitoring is an activity of management. Monitoring assesses the quality of the internal control system's performance over time. Monitoring can be done in two ways: (1) through ongoing monitoring during normal operations, and (2) separate evaluations by management with the assistance of the internal audit activity. If monitoring is done regularly during normal operations, it lessens the need for separate evaluations. Segregation of duties is a control activity which serves as a preventive control, because it is intended to prevent the occurrence of an unwanted event. Therefore, it does not represent a monitoring activity of management.

question: All of the following would be part of a factory’s control system to prevent release of wastewater that does not meet discharge standards except:

options.A: Specifying (by policy, training, and advisory signs) which substances may be disposed of via sinks and floor drains within the factory.
options.B: Performing chemical analysis of the water before discharge for components specified in the permit.
options.C: Periodically flushing sinks and floor drains with a large volume of clean water to ensure pollutants prohibited to be disposed of down the drain are sufficiently diluted.
options.D: Establishing a preventive maintenance program for the factory’s pretreatment system.

correctExplanation: This question is concerned with complying with pollutant discharge regulations. It relates to the definition of internal control as providing reasonable assurance that the company’s objectives relating to compliance will be achieved. If discharge standards do not permit the disposal of a pollutant down the drain, dilution of it after it has been poured down the drain does not correct the violation.

explanations.A: Each of these individual controls, and probably others as well, help management achieve its objective of preventing the release of wastewater that does not meet permit limits or other conditions. These three controls each approach the risk in different ways. Analytical results are the criteria for the decision to discharge; keeping pollutants out of the wastewater will help reduce concentrations and the degree of pretreatment needed; and breakdown of pretreatment equipment is less likely to occur if a preventive maintenance program is in place.
explanations.B: Each of these individual controls, and probably others as well, help management achieve its objective of preventing the release of wastewater that does not meet permit limits or other conditions. These three controls each approach the risk in different ways. Analytical results are the criteria for the decision to discharge; keeping pollutants out of the wastewater will help reduce concentrations and the degree of pretreatment needed; and breakdown of pretreatment equipment is less likely to occur if a preventive maintenance program is in place.
explanations.D: Each of these individual controls, and probably others as well, help management achieve its objective of preventing the release of wastewater that does not meet permit limits or other conditions. question: To minimize the risk that agents in the purchasing department will use their positions for personal gain, the organization should

options.A: Specify that all items purchased must pass value-per-unit-of-cost reviews.

studyUnit: Study Unit 3: E.1. Introduction to Internal Controls

question: An internal audit of the payroll function revealed several instances in which a payroll clerk had added fictitious employees to the payroll and deposited the checks in accounts of close relatives. What control should have prevented such actions?

options.A: Having the treasurer's office sign payroll checks.
options.B: Allowing changes to the payroll to be authorized only by the personnel department.
options.C: Establishing a policy to deal with close relatives working in the same department.
options.D: Using time cards and attendance records in the computation of employee gross earnings.

correctExplanation: Only the personnel department should be authorized to make changes to the payroll, while only the payroll department should process payroll checks. Furthermore, to prevent an unauthorized person from adding a name of a fictitious employee to the payroll, payroll records should be reconciled with the active employee list from the personnel department each payday.

explanations.A: Having the treasurer's office sign payroll checks would not prevent a payroll clerk from adding fictitious employees to the payroll and keeping and depositing their paychecks.
explanations.C: Establishing a policy for the hiring of close relatives would not prevent a payroll clerk from adding fictitious employees to the payroll and keeping and depositing their paychecks.
explanations.D: Using time cards and attendance records would not prevent a payroll clerk from adding fictitious employees to the payroll and keeping and depositing their paychecks.

studyUnit: Study Unit 3: E.1. Introduction to Internal Controls

question: The basic concepts implicit in internal accounting controls include the following. The cost of the system should not exceed benefits expected to be attained. The overall impact of the control procedure should not hinder operating efficiency. Which one of the following internal accounting controls recognizes these two factors?

options.A: Methods of data processing.
options.B: Reasonable assurance.
options.C: Management responsibility.
options.D: Limitations.

correctExplanation: The goal of internal control is to provide reasonable assurance that the company's objectives will be achieved in the areas of (1) effectiveness and efficiency of operations, (2) reliability of financial reporting, and (3) compliance with applicable laws and regulations. It is not the goal of internal control to provide a guarantee that the company's objectives will be achieved in these areas. The idea of reasonable assurance recognizes that it is not possible for an internal control system to guarantee that it will detect every error or prevent every error. This limitation exists because of cost/benefit issues and because controls should not be so cumbersome that they prevent the business from operating. As a result, not every possible control will be implemented. Some may not be implemented because management has decided that the cost to do them would be greater than any potential loss that could result from not doing them. Some may not be implemented because management has decided that to do them would hinder operating efficiency too much. Because internal control is not expected to provide a guarantee but only to provide reasonable assurance, it is reasonable to omit some control procedures for those reasons.

explanations.A: This answer is not correct. See the correct answer for a complete explanation.
explanations.C: This answer is not correct. See the correct answer for a complete explanation.
explanations.D: This answer is not correct. See the correct answer for a complete explanation.

question: Which of the following best describes the concept of control?

options.A: Control procedures should be designed from the "bottom up" to ensure attention to detail.
options.B: Control represents specific procedures that accountants and auditors design to ensure the correctness of processing.
options.C: Management takes action to enhance the likelihood that established goals and objectives will be achieved.
options.D: Management regularly discharges personnel who do not perform up to expectations.

correctExplanation: A control is any action taken by management to enhance the likelihood that established goals and objectives will be achieved.

explanations.A: While control procedures may be designed from the bottom up, the concept of control flows from the top down.
explanations.B: Control encompasses much more than controls designed to ensure the correctness of processing. Furthermore, control is designed and instituted by management, not by accountants or auditors.
explanations.D: This is not the definition of a control.

studyUnit: Study Unit 3: E.1. Introduction to Internal Controls

question: Internal control can provide only reasonable assurance of achieving entity control objectives because

options.A: management monitors internal control.
options.B: the auditor’s primary responsibility is the detection of fraud.
options.C: the cost of internal control should not exceed its benefits.
options.D: the board of directors is active and independent.

correctExplanation: Internal control procedures can provide reasonable assurance only—not absolute assurance and not a guarantee—to the entity’s board of directors and senior management that the company’s objectives will be achieved. This statement reflects the fundamental concepts that (1) the cost of an internal control system should not exceed the expected benefits, and (2) the overall impact of a control procedure should not hinder operating efficiency.

explanations.A: Management certainly should monitor internal control. However, that is not the reason that internal control can provide only reasonable assurance of achieving entity control objectives. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.B: The auditor's primary responsibility is not the detection of fraud. The purpose of an external audit is for the auditor to provide an opinion as to whether the financial statements of the organization have been prepared correctly, according to the accounting standards under which they have been prepared. Furthermore, nothing that an external auditor does causes internal control to be able to provide only reasonable assurance of achieving entity control objectives. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.D: The board of directors certainly should be active and independent. However, that is not the reason that internal control can provide only reasonable assurance of achieving entity control objectives. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

studyUnit: Study Unit 3: E.1. Introduction to Internal Controls

question: Preventive controls are an integral part of virtually all accounting information systems. All of the following are essential elements of a preventive control system except

options.A: documentation of policies and procedures.
options.B: separation of responsibilities.
options.C: sound personnel practices.
options.D: implementation of state-of-the-art systems.

correctExplanation: Preventive controls prevent errors and fraud before they occur. Examples of preventive controls are segregation of duties, job rotation, training and competence of personnel, documentation of policies and procedures, dual access controls, authorization, approval, endorsement and cancellation, and preformatted input. A preventive control system does not need to have state-of-the-art systems.

explanations.A: The documentation of policies and procedures is part of a preventive control system. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.B: The separation of responsibilities is part of a preventive control system. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.C: Sound personnel practices are part of a preventive control system. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

studyUnit: Study Unit 3: E.1. Introduction to Internal Controls

question: The reporting of accounting information plays a central role in the regulation of business operations. The importance of sound internal control practices is underscored by the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act of 1977 which requires publicly owned U.S. corporations to maintain systems of internal control that meet certain minimum standards. Preventive controls are an integral part of virtually all accounting processing systems, and much of the information generated by the accounting system is used for preventive control purposes. Which one of the following is not an essential element of a sound preventive control system?

options.A: Separation of responsibilities for the recording, custodial, and authorization functions.
options.B: Sound personnel practices.
options.C: Documentation of policies and procedures.
options.D: Implementation of state-of-the-art software and hardware.

correctExplanation: Implementation of state-of-the-art software and hardware is not necessary for an organization to have a sound control system.

explanations.A: Separation of responsibilities for the recording, custodial, and authorization functions is an essential element of a sound preventive control system, because without such separation of responsibilities, a person could commit a fraud and conceal it.
explanations.B: Sound personnel practices contribute to sound control systems. Organizations with effective control environments transmit guidance to their employees both verbally and by example, communicating the entity's values, standards and code of conduct; and they follow up on violations. There are mechanisms to encourage employee reporting of suspected violations, and disciplinary actions are taken when employees fail to report them. Formal and clearly communicated policies and procedures that result in shared values and teamwork are followed at all times, without exception. The competence level needed for particular jobs is specified, competent people are hired and retained, and authority and responsibility are appropriately assigned. Internal control is an explicit or implicit part of everyone's job description, and all individuals in the organization realize that they will be held accountable.
explanations.C: Documented policies and procedures are an important part of a sound control system. Formal and clearly communicated policies and procedures that result in shared values and teamwork should be followed at all times, without exception.

question: Effective internal control

options.A: Eliminates risk and potential loss to the organization.
options.B: Cannot be circumvented by management.
options.C: Reduces the need for management to review exception reports on a day-to-day basis.
options.D: Is unaffected by changing circumstances and conditions encountered by the organization.

explanations.B: Internal controls can be overridden by managers.

question: Control risk is the risk that a material misstatement in an account will not be prevented or detected on a timely basis by the client's internal control structure policies or procedures. The best control procedure to prevent or detect fictitious payroll transactions is

options.A: Personnel department authorization for hiring, pay rate, job status, and termination.
options.B: To use and account for prenumbered payroll checks.
options.C: Periodic independent bank reconciliations of the payroll bank account.
options.D: Internal verification of authorized pay rates, computations, and agreement with the payroll register.

correctExplanation: The personnel department should authorize all hiring, pay rates, job status changes, and terminations. This is the authorization function, and it should be separate from the recording function, which is performed by the payroll department.

explanations.B: The use of pre-numbered payroll checks is a control procedure that ensures that all checks are accounted for in the accounting records. However, it would not prevent or detect fictitious payroll transactions.
explanations.C: Reconciliations of the payroll bank account would not prevent or detect fictitious payroll transactions.
explanations.D: Although these are important controls, they would not prevent or detect fictitious payroll transactions.

studyUnit: Study Unit 4: E.1. Transaction Controls

question: In order to control purchasing and accounts payable, an information system must include certain source documents. For a manufacturing organization, these documents should include

options.A: Purchase requisitions, purchase orders, inventory reports of goods needed, and vendor invoices.
options.B: Receiving reports and vendor invoices.
options.C: Purchase requisitions, purchase orders, receiving reports, and vendor invoices.
options.D: Purchase orders, receiving reports, and vendor invoices.

correctExplanation: A purchase requisition, authorized by the user department, gives purchasing personnel authority to place an order. The purchase order, along with the purchase requisition and the receiving report, should be checked before the vendor's invoice is paid. The purchase order is necessary so that the accounts payable department can see that the items were ordered; and the receiving report is needed so they can be sure the items were received before they are paid for.

explanations.A: A receiving report is also required, in order to be certain that the items ordered were received; and an inventory report of goods needed is not a required document to control purchasing and accounts payable, although it may be useful as backup to a purchase requisition.
explanations.B: In addition, a purchase requisition and a purchase order are needed.
explanations.D: In addition, a purchase requisition is needed.

question: Which of the following controls would be the most appropriate means to ensure that terminated employees had been removed from the payroll?

options.A: Reconciling payroll and time-keeping records.
options.B: Establishing direct-deposit procedures with employees' banks.
options.C: Mailing checks to employees' residences.
options.D: Establishing computerized limit checks on payroll rates.

correctExplanation: If an employee has been terminated but the employee has not been removed from the payroll, a reconciliation of payroll records with time-keeping records should detect it.

explanations.B: Establishing direct-deposit procedures with employees' banks does nothing to verify whether all the paychecks are valid. Using this procedure, terminated employees who had not been removed from the payroll would continue to receive paychecks.
explanations.C: Mailing checks to employees' homes does nothing to verify whether all the paychecks are valid. Using this procedure, terminated employees who had not been removed from the payroll would continue to receive paychecks.
explanations.D: This procedure would detect excessive pay to current employees but not inappropriate pay to terminated employees.

studyUnit: Study Unit 4: E.1. Transaction Controls

question: Which one of the following situations represents a strength of internal control for purchasing and accounts payable?

options.A: Unmatched receiving reports are reviewed on an annual basis.
options.B: Vendors' invoices are matched against purchase orders and receiving reports before a liability is recorded.
options.C: Invoices are approved for payment by the purchasing department.
options.D: Prenumbered receiving reports are issued randomly.

correctExplanation: Vendor's invoices should be matched against purchase requisitions, purchase orders, and receiving reports before any liability is recorded. When the payment has been approved, the accounts payable department should prepare a voucher, which is an internal document that is the authorization for payment.

explanations.A: Unmatched receiving reports should be reviewed more frequently than annually.
explanations.C: The purchasing department should not approve invoices for payment. The accounts payable department should approve invoices for payment, based on a review of all the supporting documentation which includes the purchase requisition, the purchase order, and the receiving report/packing slip.
explanations.D: Receiving reports should be prenumbered and should be issued sequentially, not randomly, so that a missing report or a report out of sequence can be investigated.

studyUnit: Study Unit 4: E.1. Transaction Controls

question: The internal controls surrounding the revenue cycle should provide assurances of all of the following except the

options.A: proper authorization of all sales return and allowance transactions.
options.B: accurate recording of customer accounts and finished goods inventories.
options.C: accurate recording, shipping, and billing of all valid sales transactions.
options.D: approval of all credit sales transactions after they are processed.

correctExplanation: Credit sales transactions should be approved before they are processed. That is a transaction control objective in the revenue cycle. However, there is very little purpose to approving credit sales transactions after they have been processed. At that point, if the person approving the transaction determines that the customer is not creditworthy, it is too late because the sale has already been processed and the product shipped or delivered to the customer. And there will be a high probability of a loss.

explanations.A: Controls surrounding the revenue cycle should provide assurance of proper authorization of all sales return and allowance transactions. Authorization by someone with the authority to approve the specific transactions is a transaction control objective in the revenue cycle.
explanations.B: Controls surrounding the revenue cycle should provide assurance of accurate recording of customer accounts and finished goods inventories. Accuracy is a transaction control objective.
explanations.C: Controls surrounding the revenue cycle should provide assurance of accurate recording, shipping, and billing of all valid sales transactions. Accuracy is a transaction control objective.

studyUnit: Study Unit 4: E.1. Transaction Controls

question: Certain limitations are inherent in any internal control system. Which one of the following scenarios is the result of an inherent limitation of internal control?

options.A: An employee, who is unable to read, is assigned custody of the firm's computer tape library and run manuals that are used during the third shift.
options.B: The comptroller both makes and records cash deposits.
options.C: A security guard allows one of the warehouse employees to remove company assets from the premises without authorization.
options.D: The firm sells to customers on account, without credit approval.

correctExplanation: If two employees (the security guard and the warehouse employee) collude to defraud their employer, a control based on segregation of functions can be rendered ineffective. This is an inherent limitation of internal control.

explanations.A: Assignment of an employee who is unable to read to a job requiring reading is avoidable through adequate testing of potential employees. Therefore, it is not an inherent limitation of internal control.
explanations.B: This is not an inherent limitation of internal control, because it could and should be avoided through adequate segregation of duties.
explanations.D: This is not an inherent limitation of internal control, because it could and should be avoided through adequate credit approval of sales.

question: Auditors document their understanding of internal control with questionnaires, flowcharts, and narrative descriptions. A questionnaire consists of a series of questions concerning controls that auditors consider necessary to prevent or detect errors and irregularities. The most appropriate question designed to contribute to the auditors' understanding of the completeness of the expenditure cycle would concern the

options.A: Use and accountability of prenumbered checks.
options.B: Qualifications of accounting personnel.
options.C: Disposition of cash receipts.
options.D: Internal verification of quantities, prices, and mathematical accuracy of sales invoices.

correctExplanation: In understanding the completeness of the expenditure cycle, the auditor is interested in whether all the transactions have been recorded. If prenumbered checks are used sequentially, a gap in check numbers would be something for the auditor to investigate, because it may mean that there are unrecorded transactions.

explanations.B: Qualifications of accounting personnel are unrelated to the controls over the expenditure cycle.
explanations.C: Cash receipts are unrelated to the expenditure cycle and can contribute nothing to the auditors' understanding of the completeness of the expenditure cycle.
explanations.D: Verification of sales invoices will not contribute to an understanding of the completeness of the expenditure cycle, because sales invoices are part of the revenue cycle.

question: An internal auditor found that employee time cards in one department are not properly approved by the supervisor. Which of the following could result?

options.B: Payroll checks might not be distributed to the appropriate payees.
options.C: Duplicate paychecks might be issued.

explanations.B: Payroll checks would not be distributed to the wrong employees as a result of the supervisor failing to approve employee time cards.
explanations.C: Duplicate paychecks would not be issued as a result of the supervisor failing to approve employee time cards.

question: Which one of the following methods for the distribution of employees' paychecks would provide the best internal control for the organization?

options.A: Distribution of paychecks directly to each employee by a representative of the Human Resource department.
options.B: Direct deposit in each employee's personal bank account.
options.C: Distribution of paychecks directly to each employee by the payroll manager.
options.D: Delivery of the paychecks to each department supervisor, who in turn would distribute paychecks directly to the employees in his/her department.

correctExplanation: Direct deposit to each employee's personal bank account provides the best internal control over distribution of paychecks. It lessens the risk of damaged, lost or stolen payroll checks because no checks are distributed. The only thing distributed is a statement of earnings. If earnings are deposited electronically into employees' accounts, it is important that deposit records be reconciled to a list of active employees at every pay date so that persons whose employment has been terminated do not continue receiving payroll deposits. Cancellation of direct deposit processing should be part of employment termination procedures, and a terminated employee should receive his or her final paycheck in the form of a physical check instead of a direct deposit, as evidence of the direct deposit cancellation.

explanations.A: Representatives of the Human Resources department authorize transactions that add employees to the payroll, change pay and effect other key transactions. Therefore, human resource employees must not have access to paycheck distribution, nor to timekeeping or payroll functions. The Human Resource department must be organizationally separate from the payroll office and payroll functions. So having a representative of Human Resources distribute paychecks would be a violation of the principle of segregation of duties.
explanations.C: The payroll manager has oversight over the processing and production of the payroll. The function of payroll processing must be segregated from the function of paycheck distribution. Therefore, having the payroll manager distribute paychecks would be a violation of the principle of segregation of duties.
explanations.D: This would be an acceptable method of distributing paychecks, as long as controls are in place to minimize the potential for theft or fraudulent distribution of paychecks, such as payments made to fictitious or terminated employees. The person who distributes the checks should not also have authority to authorize payroll checks. However, this is not the method from among those given that provides for the best internal control for the organization. Safeguarding Controls (40)
