question: Which of the following is a malicious program, the purpose of which is to reproduce itself throughout the network, and can possibly produce a denial of service attack by excessively utilizing system resources?

options.A: Worm.
options.B: Trojan horse.
options.C: Logic bomb.
options.D: Virus.

correctExplanation: A worm is an independent program that replicates itself from system to system without the use of any host file. The difference between a worm and a virus is that the worm does not require the use of an infected host file, while the virus does require the spreading of an infected host file. Worms generally exist inside of other files, often Word or Excel documents. However, worms use the host file differently from viruses. Usually the worm releases a document that has the "worm" macro inside the document. The entire document spreads from computer to computer, so the entire document is, in essence, the worm.

explanations.B: A Trojan horse is an independent program that is disguised as legitimate software. They may look useful or interesting to an unsuspecting user, but are actually harmful when executed.
explanations.C: A logic bomb is a malicious program that is activated when some particular condition occurs (e.g., could be a date, or system operation).
explanations.D: A virus is a program that alters the way another computer operates, but it is not an independent program that can reproduce itself throughout the network. A virus spreads by inserting copies of itself into the executable code or documents.

studyUnit: Study Unit 9: E.2. Internet Security

question: A department purchased one copy of a word processing software program for internal use. The manager of the department installed the program on the manager’s office computer and then made two complete copies of the original diskettes. Copy number 1 was solely for backup purposes. Copy number 2 was for use by another member of the department. In terms of software licenses and copyright law, which of the following is correct?

options.A: Only copy number 2 is legal.
options.B: Both copies are legal.
options.C: Only copy number 1 is legal.
options.D: Neither copy is legal.

correctExplanation: A backup copy is legal under the copyright law. However, any copy other than a backup copy is illegal and is a license violation.

explanations.A: Any copy other than a backup copy is illegal and is a license violation.
explanations.B: Only copy number 1 is legal.
explanations.D: One of the copies is indeed legal.

studyUnit: Study Unit 9: E.2. Internet Security

question: A controller became aware that a competitor appeared to have access to the company's pricing information. An investigation determined that the "leak of information" was occurring during the electronic transmission of data from branch offices to the head office. Which of the following controls would be most effective in preventing the leak of information?

options.A: Encryption.
options.B: Use of passwords.
options.C: Asynchronous transmission.
options.D: Use of fiber optic transmission lines.

correctExplanation: Encryption is the conversion of data into a code. An intruder may be able be able to access the data by "tapping into" the transmission line. However, the intruder would need an encryption "key" in order to understand the data being sent. Encryption is a logical security control within the broader classification of general controls.

explanations.B: Use of passwords will control access at the sending location, and will limit access to the head office computer. Passwords, however, will not prevent someone from "tapping into" the transmission line.
explanations.C: Asynchronous transmission does not prevent theft of data, it speeds up the transmission process.
explanations.D: Fiber optic transmission lines will improve the quality of the transmission, but will not prevent theft of data.

studyUnit: Study Unit 9: E.2. Internet Security

question: Utility programs can be used to read files that contain all authorized access user codes for a server. A control to prevent this is:

options.A: Internally encrypted passwords.
options.B: A peer-to-peer network.
options.C: A password hierarchy.
options.D: Logon passwords.

correctExplanation: Internally encrypted passwords are controls designed to preclude users browsing the password file with a utility software application.

explanations.B: A peer-to-peer network is a system that relies on a series of equal microcomputers for processing.
explanations.C: A password hierarchy represents a set of interrelated authorization codes to distinguish between action privileges such as reading, adding, or deleting records.
explanations.D: Logon passwords represent the initial user authorization access codes to the typical system.

studyUnit: Study Unit 9: E.2. Internet Security

question: Which of the following statements regarding encryption is true?

options.A: It is impossible to intercept encrypted data sent over the Internet.
options.B: Secret key systems use two different keys, one for encryption and one for decryption.
options.C: A message encrypted with Company Q's public key can only be decrypted with Company Q's private key.
options.D: Encryption is a 100% guarantee that data being transmitted cannot be read by an unintended third party.

correctExplanation: This is a true statement. Only the matching private key can decrypt a message encrypted with the public key. This is an essential part of the SSL system used on the Internet for secure web sites.

explanations.A: Quite to the contrary, it is very easy to intercept encrypted data. Encryption makes it difficult for transmitted data to be read, but it does nothing to prevent interception. There is a better answer among the choices here.
explanations.B: A secret key system uses the same key for encryption and decryption. A public/private key system uses two different keys.
explanations.D: There are two problems with this answer. First and foremost, encryption is only as good as the secrecy of the encryption keys used in the encryption. If the encryption keys are lost, stolen or otherwise revealed to third parties, those third parties will be able to read the encrypted messages. Secondly, while encryption is mathematically very difficult to break, it is not impossible given enough time, skill and determination.

studyUnit: Study Unit 9: E.2. Internet Security

question: A firm uses a centralized computer system that allows its traveling sales personnel to directly enter new orders and to query the database on old orders. To maintain data integrity in this application, it would be important to have:

options.A: uninterruptible power supplies.
options.B: password protection.
options.C: backup.
options.D: encryption.

correctExplanation: Encryption should be used to make sure that data is not changed in transit over a network or the Internet.

explanations.A: An uninterruptible power supply is important, but it does not maintain data integrity. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.B: Password protection is important, but it does not maintain data integrity. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.C: A backup system is important, but it does not maintain data integrity. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

studyUnit: Study Unit 9: E.2. Internet Security

question: Encoding electronic data through the use of an algorithm to make information unreadable to unauthorized individuals is identified as

options.A: a worm.
options.B: a virus.
options.C: encryption.
options.D: a firewall.

correctExplanation: Encryption is the process of converting data into a code using an algorithm, and then a key is required to convert the code back to data. Unauthorized people can receive the coded information, but without the proper key they cannot read it.

explanations.A: This is not the definition of a worm. A worm is a program that replicates itself from system to system without the use of any host file. Unlike a virus, a worm does not require the use of an infected host file. Worms generally exist inside of other files, often Word or Excel documents. However, worms use the host file differently from viruses. Usually the worm releases a document that has the “worm” macro inside the document. The entire document spreads from computer to computer, so the entire document is, in essence, the worm.
explanations.B: This is not the definition of a virus. A computer virus is a program that alters the way another computer operates. Viruses can damage programs, delete files or reformat the hard disk. Other viruses may not do damage but they replicate themselves and present text, video, and audio messages. Although these other viruses may not cause damage directly, they create problems by taking up computer memory and causing erratic behavior or system crashes that can lead to data loss. A virus can be received from a downloaded file or an email attachment, among other places.
explanations.D: This is not the definition of a firewall. A firewall serves as a barrier between the internal and the external networks and prevents unauthorized access to the internal network. If it is properly configured, a firewall makes a computer’s ports invisible to port scans. In addition to protecting a computer from incoming probes, a firewall can also prevent backdoor applications, Trojan horses, and other unwanted applications from sending data from the computer. A firewall can be in the form of software directly installed on a computer, or it can be a piece of hardware installed between the computer and its connection to the Internet.

studyUnit: Study Unit 9: E.2. Internet Security

question: The chief information technology officer introduced a technology to prevent unauthorized external access to its client’s network. The technology described by the chief information officer is most likely

options.A: firewall.
options.B: public-key.
options.C: data encryption.
options.D: private-key.

correctExplanation: A firewall is a technology that prevents unauthorized external access to its client’s network. A firewall serves as a barrier between the internal and the external networks and prevents unauthorized access to the internal network. A properly configured firewall makes a computer’s ports invisible to hackers. In addition to protecting a computer from incoming probes, a firewall can also prevent backdoor applications, Trojan horses, and other unwanted applications from sending data from the computer.

explanations.B: Public-key is not a technology to prevent unauthorized external access to its client’s network. A public key is used in a public-key/private-key encryption system. In a public-key/private-key encryption system, each entity that needs to receive encrypted data publishes a public key for encrypting data while keeping a private key to itself as the only means for decrypting that data. Anyone can encrypt and send data to the company using its published public key, but only the company’s private key can be used to decrypt the data, and only the company that published the public key has the private key.
explanations.C: Data encryption is not a technology to prevent unauthorized external access to its client’s network. Data encryption converts data into a code and then a key is required to convert the code back to data. Unauthorized people can receive the coded information, but without the proper key, they cannot read it. An attacker may be able to see where the traffic came from and where it went but not the content.
explanations.D: Private-key is not a technology to prevent unauthorized external access to its client’s network. A private key is used in a public-key/private-key encryption system. In a public-key/private-key encryption system, each entity that needs to receive encrypted data publishes a public key for encrypting data while keeping a private key to itself as the only means for decrypting that data. Anyone can encrypt and send data to the company using its published public key, but only the company’s private key can be used to decrypt the data, and only the company that published the public key has the private key.

studyUnit: Study Unit 9: E.2. Internet Security

question: If Sarah Corp. wants to send an order over the Internet to Lee Inc. for raw materials, which of the following would be the correct methodology for encrypting the order so that only Lee Inc. will be able to decrypt and read the contents of the order?

options.A: Sarah Corp. would request that Lee Inc. email their secret key so that Sarah Corp. could use it to encrypt the order for transmission.
options.B: Sarah Corp. would encrypt the message using Sarah Corp's private key, and Lee Inc. would decrypt the message using Sarah Corp's public key.
options.C: Sarah Corp. would encrypt the message using Lee Inc's public key, and Lee Inc. would decrypt the message using their own private key.
options.D: Sarah Corp. would encrypt the message using Lee Inc's private key, and Lee Inc. would decrypt the message using their own public key.

correctExplanation: This is correct. Lee Inc's public key would be publicly available, and only Lee Inc., using their private key, would be able to decrypt any message encrypted with their public key.

explanations.A: Email cannot be trusted to be secure when sending via the Internet, and therefore the secret key could be intercepted and used by a third party to decrypt Sarah Corp's order details.
explanations.B: Because Sarah Corp's public key is available publicly, any message encrypted with Sarah Corp's private key could be decrypted by anyone. Sarah Corp. may as well send the order without encryption.
explanations.D: No one but Lee Inc. should have possession of their private key, so neither Sarah Corp. nor any other company would ever use Lee Inc's. private key.

studyUnit: Study Unit 9: E.2. Internet Security

question: Which of the following is a technical computer crime that requires sophisticated knowledge of computers and/or networks?

options.A: Denial of service.
options.B: Dumpster diving.
options.C: Phishing.
options.D: Social engineering.

correctExplanation: A denial of service (DOS) attack involves overwhelming a server or cluster of servers to the point that they are unable to respond to legitimate requests, thereby making them unavailable for normal usage. A DOS attack certainly requires a reasonable amount of technical and network skills to successfully execute.

explanations.B: Dumpster diving requires no computer knowledge whatsoever, only the willingness to get a little bit dirty.
explanations.C: Phishing refers to deceiving others into revealing personal and/or sensitive information such as credit card numbers, social security numbers, passwords, etc., usually through an email message. This requires no sophisticated technical knowledge beyond being able to send an email.
explanations.D: Social engineering refers to using social tactics to gain information. For example, an employee from one company may call a competitor and pretend to be a coworker who forgot how to access certain files, hoping that the person who they are talking to will reveal that information. No technical skills are required; in fact, social skills would be the most essential when attempting to gain information through social engineering.

studyUnit: Study Unit 9: E.2. Internet Security

question: A company's IT manager has been asked to ensure that the company’s data is protected in the event it was intercepted during transmission. Which one of the following is the best control to implement from the selection below?

options.A: Encryption.
options.B: Sequencing of messages.
options.C: Self-checking algorithms.
options.D: Dedicated lines.

correctExplanation: Encryption is the best protection against data leaks caused by traffic interception. Data encryption is the process of converting data into a code, and then a key is required to convert the code back to data. Encryption prevents data from being read by unauthorized persons. Unauthorized people can intercept the coded information, but without the proper key, they cannot read it. Thus, an attacker may be able to see where the traffic came from and where it went but not the content.

explanations.B: Message sequencing is used to ensure that messages are delivered to the receiving application in a particular order. Sequencing of messages would not protect against data leaks caused by traffic interception. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.C: An algorithm is a sequence of instructions that a computer must perform to solve a well-defined problem. It defines what the computer needs to do and how to do it. Algorithms can instruct a computer how to perform a calculation, process data, or make a decision. Self-checking algorithms are used in error detection, for example a check digit used in an account number to check that the account number is a valid number, which could identify a typographical error made in input. Self-checking algorithms would not protect against data leaks caused by traffic interception. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.D: Dedicated lines would not be a practical way of protecting against data leaks caused by traffic interception because communications would be limited to moving only across the dedicated lines. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

studyUnit: Study Unit 9: E.2. Internet Security

question: Encryption

options.A: serves as a barrier between the internal and external networks and prevents unauthorized access to the internal network.
options.B: allows for the quick retrieval of data.
options.C: records every keystroke and then sends this information back to the computer operator.
options.D: converts data into code and then a key is required to convert the code back to data.

correctExplanation: Encryption converts data into a code and then a key is required to convert the code back to data. Unauthorized people may be able to intercept the coded information, but without the proper key they cannot read it. Encryption is the best protection against traffic interception resulting in data leaks.

explanations.A: This is the description of a firewall. A properly configured firewall makes a computer’s ports invisible to port scans. In addition to protecting a computer from incoming probes, a firewall can also prevent backdoor applications, Trojan horses, and other unwanted applications from sending data from the computer.
explanations.B: This is not a description of encryption. A database management system allows for the retrieval of data.
explanations.C: This is a description of a keylogger, which is a type of malware that records every keystroke and sends it back to the hacker who installed the keylogger on the user's computer without the user's knowledge. Keylogging software can be used by hackers to gather bank information, credit card information, and passwords.

studyUnit: Study Unit 9: E.2. Internet Security

question: Which of the following would not be a cybercrime?

options.A: Use of a network to obtain information illegally.
options.B: Theft of emails.
options.C: Unauthorized copying of software.
options.D: Dismantling of a proxy server.

correctExplanation: A proxy server is a computer and software that creates a gateway to and from the Internet. The proxy server contains an access control list of approved web sites and handles all web access requests, limiting access to only those sites contained in the access control list, so it can enable an employer to deny its employees access to sites that are unlikely to have any productive benefits. The proxy server can limit the information stored on it to information the company can afford to lose, and if the proxy server is broken into, the organization’s main servers remain functional. The proxy server also examines all incoming requests for information and tests them for authenticity, so it can function as a firewall. Dismantling a proxy server would make the computer system more vulnerable, but it is not a cybercrime.

explanations.A: The use of a network to obtain information illegally is a cybercrime.
explanations.B: Theft of emails is a cybercrime.
explanations.C: Unauthorized copying of software is copyright infringement and is a cybercrime.

studyUnit: Study Unit 9: E.2. Internet Security

question: Friendly Skies Airline is about to create an internet site to capture the flight reservations and ticket payments. Which one of the following best demonstrates the inherent risks of the internet?

options.A: The limited controls available to mitigate risks.
options.B: Data formats are not typically standardized.
options.C: Dependency on internet service provider.
options.D: Confidential information can be intercepted.

correctExplanation: Electronic eavesdropping can occur if computer users are able to observe transmissions intended for someone else. Therefore, organizations must ensure that information sent over a network is properly protected to maintain the confidentiality of company information. Furthermore, the company must ensure that company files cannot be accessed or changed without authorization.

explanations.A: This is not the best demonstration of the inherent risks of the internet. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.B: This is not the best demonstration of the inherent risks of the internet. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.C: Dependency on an internet service provider is not the best demonstration of the inherent risks of the internet. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

studyUnit: Study Unit 9: E.2. Internet Security

question: All of the following are examples of potential Internet security risks except

options.A: a swiffer.
options.B: A port scanner.
options.C: A backdoor.
options.D: Electronic eavesdropping.

correctExplanation: A swiffer is not an example of a potential Internet security risk. (A sniffer is a piece of software that grabs all of the traffic flowing into and out of a computer attached to a network, and it can be used to gather information illegally, which is a potential security risk. But a swiffer is not a potential Internet security risk.)

explanations.B: A port scanner is software that can probe a server or a computer for ports that are open. Although port scanners have legitimate uses, they are also used by hackers to locate and exploit vulnerabilities. Using port scans, hackers can look for a particular make of computer or a particular software program, because they know of weaknesses in those computers or programs that they can exploit. Once a hacker has identified a vulnerable computer or software application, the hacker can leave a backdoor open in the computer in order to re-enter it at any time. If the original entry point is detected and closed, the backdoor functions as a hidden, undetected way back in. A port scanner is a potential security risk.
explanations.C: A “backdoor” is an undocumented means to gain access to a program, online service or an entire computer system by bypassing the normal authentication process. A backdoor is a potential security risk.
explanations.D: Electronic eavesdropping occurs if computer users are able to observe transmissions intended for someone else. Electronic eavesdropping is a potential security risk.

studyUnit: Study Unit 9: E.2. Internet Security

question: Which of the following is an indication that a computer virus is present?

options.A: Inadequate backup, recovery, and contingency plans.
options.B: Numerous copyright violations due to unauthorized use of purchased software.
options.C: Unexplainable losses of or changes to data.
options.D: Frequent power surges that harm computer equipment.

correctExplanation: Unexplainable losses of, or changes to data are an indication of computer viruses.

explanations.A: Inadequate backup, recovery, and contingency plans are weaknesses of operational planning.
explanations.B: Numerous copyright violations are compliance problems.
explanations.D: Power surges are primarily caused by power supply problems.

studyUnit: Study Unit 9: E.2. Internet Security

question: Six months after a disgruntled systems programmer was fired and passwords disabled, the company's mainframe was brought to a halt when it suddenly erased all of its own files and software. The most likely way the programmer accomplished this was by

options.A: Returning to the computer center after 6 months.
options.B: Planting a computer virus through the use of telephone access.
options.C: Having an accomplice in the computer center.
options.D: Implanting a virus in the operating system and executing it via a backdoor.

correctExplanation: This is probably the best explanation of how the files and software were suddenly erased. A virus is a program that alters the way another computer operates. Viruses can damage programs, delete files or reformat the hard disk. A backdoor in a computer system is a method of bypassing normal authentication or securing remote access to a computer, while attempting to remain hidden from casual inspection.

explanations.A: The programmer was more than likely denied access to the computer center.
explanations.B: The passwords were disabled, so the programmer would not know the new passwords.
explanations.C: In these circumstances, it is not likely that there was collusion.

studyUnit: Study Unit 9: E.2. Internet Security

question: A computer virus is different from a "Trojan Horse" because the virus can

options.A: replicate itself.
options.B: corrupt data.
options.C: alter programming instructions.
options.D: erase executable files.

correctExplanation: To be considered a virus, a virus must meet two criteria: 1) It must execute itself. A virus often places its own code in the path of the execution of another program. And 2) it must replicate itself. A virus can replace other executable files with a copy of the virus-infected file. A Trojan Horse does not replicate itself.

explanations.B: Both viruses and Trojan horses can corrupt data. A virus is a program that alters the way another computer operates. Viruses can damage programs, delete files or reformat the hard disk. A Trojan horse is any program that does something besides what a person believes it will do. A Trojan horse can appear to be something desirable, but in fact it contains malicious code that, when triggered, will cause loss or even theft of data.
explanations.C: Both viruses and Trojan horses can alter programming instructions. A virus is a program that alters the way another computer operates. Viruses can damage programs, delete files or reformat the hard disk. A Trojan horse is any program that does something besides what a person believes it will do. A Trojan horse can appear to be something desirable, but in fact it contains malicious code that, when triggered, will cause loss or even theft of data.
explanations.D: Both viruses and Trojan horses can erase executable files. A virus is a program that alters the way another computer operates. Viruses can damage programs, delete files or reformat the hard disk. A Trojan horse is any program that does something besides what a person believes it will do. A Trojan horse can appear to be something desirable, but in fact it contains malicious code that, when triggered, will cause loss or even theft of data.

studyUnit: Study Unit 9: E.2. Internet Security

question: Confidential data can be securely transmitted over the Internet by using

options.A: single-use passwords.
options.B: encryption.
options.C: firewalls.
options.D: digital signatures.

correctExplanation: Encryption is the best protection against internet traffic being intercepted, resulting in data leaks. Encryption converts data into a code, and then a key is required to convert the code back to data. Unauthorized people can receive the coded information, but without the proper key, they cannot read it. Thus, an attacker may be able to see where the traffic came from and where it went but not the content.

explanations.A: A single-use password is a password that is valid for only one login session or transaction. If an intruder manages to intercept a single-use password that has already been used to log into a service or to conduct a transaction, he or she will not be able to use it again, because it will no longer be usable. Single-use passwords do not enable confidential data to be securely transmitted over the internet, however, because they do not prevent the data from being intercepted while being transmitted.
explanations.C: A firewall serves as a barrier between the internal and the external networks and prevents unauthorized access to the internal network. It does not enable confidential data to be securely transmitted over the internet, because it does not prevent the data from being intercepted while being transmitted.
explanations.D: A digital signature is an electronic signature that can be used to authenticate the identity of the sender of a message or the signer of a document. It can also be used to ensure that the original content of the message or document that was sent has not been changed. The ability to ensure that the original signed message arrived means that the sender cannot easily say later that he never sent it or that he sent something different. A digital signature can be used with any kind of message, whether it is encrypted or not, so that the receiver can be sure of the sender's identity and that the message arrived without being changed. However, a digital signature does not provide security for confidential data that is being sent over the internet, because it does not prevent the data from being intercepted while being transmitted. Business Continuity Planning(16)

studyUnit: Study Unit 9: E.2. Internet Security

question: A company is updating its backup control plan. Which one of the following should be included in this plan?

options.A: Limit access to data processing centers to authorized personnel.
options.B: A communication and service restoration plan.
options.C: Concurrency controls in multi-user systems.
options.D: An uninterruptible power system to avoid loss of data from power interruption.

correctExplanation: A communication restoration and service restoration plan is part of a backup control plan, which is an important part of a disaster recovery plan. It is essential that the company have plans for the backup and recovery of its data, including an alternative site for service restoration and data communications for tranmission of data and online processing in the event of a disaster.

explanations.A: Limiting access to data processing centers to authorized personnel is a physical access control that is used to secure equipment and premises. It is not a part of a backup control plan. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.C: Concurrency controls are not part of a backup control system. When multiple users try to access the same file or program at the same time, they can destroy each other's work. Concurrency controls in a software program allow the program to deal with multiple users trying to access the same file or program at the same time so work is not destroyed. With concurrency controls in a software application, multiple users can access the same file at the same time without having to worry about data loss; or concurrency controls can also be used to prevent file compromise by restricting access to one user at a time. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.D: An uninterruptible power system is an important part of a disaster recovery plan, as is a backup control plan. However, an uninterruptible power system is not a part of the backup control plan. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

studyUnit: Study Unit 10: E.2. Business Continuity Planning

question: The IT team of a company created a disaster recovery plan for their employer. The plan includes several versions of backups of data and systems, including at least one copy kept off site. The plan also includes an off-site location selected for its reduced chance of natural disasters like floods and hurricanes. This location is guarded by a security service. The IT manager has a copy of the plan at home, and the plan is regularly tested. Select the statement below that best describes the plan.

options.A: The disaster plan needs to ensure that there are copies of the disaster recovery plan accessible on the computer system.
options.B: The disaster recovery plan needs to include a disaster recovery site that is a hot or cold site with necessary capabilities.
options.C: The disaster recovery plan has everything required because the company can access the data backups and continue processing.
options.D: The disaster recovery plan needs to include information on which employees will participate in disaster recovery and their responsibilities.

correctExplanation: In addition to other weaknesses in the plan, the plan should include information on which employees will participate in disaster recovery and their responsibilities. One person should oversee disaster recovery, and another should be second in command.

explanations.A: There would be very little point in putting copies of the disaster recovery plan on the computer system, because in the event of a disaster the computer system would probably not be immediately accessible.
explanations.B: A disaster recovery site is needed and it has been arranged for. The recovery site does not need to be only a hot or a cold site. A disaster recovery site may be a hot site, a cold site, a warm site, or a mobile site. However, more information relative to the type of site is needed in the recovery plan. A hot site, or a mirrored data center, is a backup facility with a computer system similar to the one used regularly that is fully operational and immediately available, with all necessary telecommunications hookups for online processing. A hot site also has current, live data being replicated to it in real time from the live site by automated data communications. A hot site would be able to take over processing at a moment’s notice. If the site is a cold site—a facility where space, electric power, and heating and air conditioning are available and processing equipment can be installed—the disaster recovery plan must include arrangements to quickly get computer equipment installed and operational If the site is a warm site—a facility with all the computer equipment and necessary data and communications links installed but with no current data on the computers—current data will need to be restored to it in the event of a disaster, and the recovery plan must include processes to do that. A mobile site may be a hot site, a warm site, or a cold site. It may be company owned, or it may be contracted.
explanations.C: The disaster recovery plan does not have everything required. If the off-site location is a cold site, the disaster recovery plan must include arrangements to quickly get computer equipment installed and operational; and if it is a warm site, current data will need to be restored to it in the event of a disaster, and the recovery plan must include processes to do that. The disaster recovery plan does not include information on which employees will participate in disaster recovery and their responsibilities. One person should oversee the disaster recovery, and another should be second in command. Furthermore, all the backups, not just one, should be stored off-site; and all the disaster recovery team members should have current copies of the recovery plan at their homes, not just the IT manager.

studyUnit: Study Unit 10: E.2. Business Continuity Planning

question: A large property insurance company has regional centers that customers call to report claims. Although the regional centers are not located in areas known to be prone to natural disasters, the company needs a disaster recovery plan that would restore call answering capacity in the event of a disaster or other extended loss of service. The best plan for restoring capacity in the event of a disaster would be to reroute call traffic to

options.A: A hot site that duplicates regional facilities.
options.B: A cold site that duplicates regional facilities.
options.C: Non-affected regional centers.
options.D: A third-party service center.

correctExplanation: Rerouting call traffic to non-affected regional centers is the best approach because it minimizes cost, maximizes the company's control over the reconfiguration, and permits calls to be answered by the company's skilled personnel.

explanations.A: A hot site is a backup facility that has a computer system similar to the one used regularly. The hot site must be fully operational and immediately available, with all necessary telecommunications hookups for online processing. A hot site also has current, live data that is replicated to it from the live site, either by data communications or by on-site storage of backup media. Duplicating regional facilities in a hot site would provide space, equipment, and some software but would not provide personnel.
explanations.B: A cold site is a facility where space, electric power, and heating and air conditioning are available and processing equipment can be installed, though the equipment and the necessary telecommunications are not immediately available. Duplicating regional facilities in a cold site would not immediately provide equipment, software, or personnel.
explanations.D: Rerouting call traffic to a third-party service center would be overly expensive because of personnel cost, and service center personnel would not be trained for the company's calls.

studyUnit: Study Unit 10: E.2. Business Continuity Planning

question: A company has in its disaster recovery plan a process to store in a secure, offsite warehouse building a back-up of its current financial operating systems. What type of back-up location is the company most likely using?

options.A: A hot site.
options.B: A mirrored data center.
options.C: A recovery operations center.
options.D: A cold site.

correctExplanation: This is most likely to be a cold site. A cold site is a facility where space, electric power, and heating and air conditioning are available and processing equipment can be installed, though the equipment and the necessary telecommunications are not immediately available. If an organization uses a cold site, its disaster recovery plan must include arrangements to quickly get computer equipment installed and operational.

explanations.A: This is not the description of a hot site. A hot site is a backup facility that has a computer system similar to the one used regularly. The hot site must be fully operational and immediately available, with all necessary telecommunications hookups for online processing. A hot site also has current, live data that is replicated to it in real-time from the live site by automated data communications.
explanations.B: This is not the description of a mirrored data center. A mirrored data center is another term for a hot site. It is a fully operational secondary data center where data is backed up in real-time by automated data communications. It has a computer system similar to the one used regularly. The hot site must be fully operational and immediately available, with all necessary telecommunications hookups for online processing.
explanations.C: This is not a description of a recovery operations center. "Recovery operations center" is another term for a hot site. A hot site is a backup facility that has a computer system similar to the one used regularly. The hot site must be fully operational and immediately available, with all necessary telecommunications hookups for online processing. A hot site also has current, live data that is replicated to it in real-time from the live site by automated data communications.

studyUnit: Study Unit 10: E.2. Business Continuity Planning

question: A company’s management is aware that it cannot foresee every contingency even with the best planning. Management believes, however, that a more thorough recovery plan increases the ability to resume operations quickly after an interruption and thus to:

options.A: Receive the maximum benefit from planning.
options.B: Fulfill its obligations to customers.
options.C: Minimize the cost of facility repair.
options.D: Maintain the same level of employment.

correctExplanation: The better the recovery plans, the more likely the company would be to resume operations quickly and fulfill its obligations to customers.

explanations.A: The maximum benefit from planning is that it prompts action to avoid the most likely or most devastating events with the potential to interrupt business. Management would be delighted if planning ensured that business was never interrupted and thus that the recovery plan was never invoked.
explanations.C: Thorough planning may or may not minimize the cost of facility repair. That is, the best approach may be to undergo more expensive repair sooner in order to resume operations sooner.
explanations.D: The company may or may not maintain the same level of employment after a disaster. For example, a disaster that destroys productive capacity in one plant may lead to layoffs.

studyUnit: Study Unit 10: E.2. Business Continuity Planning

question: Which one of the following statements on the contingency planning for disasters is not true?

options.A: A very important part of a disaster recovery plan is the specification of the backup site.
options.B: The design of the disaster recovery plan should include an evaluation of the company's needs, a list of priorities for recovery, and a set of recovery strategies and procedures.
options.C: The disaster recovery plan should be thoroughly documented and approved.
options.D: A disaster recovery plan must be implemented at the lowest levels in the company.

correctExplanation: This is not a true statement. Developing and implementing a disaster recovery plan is a management responsibility. In the event of a disaster, leadership by management is critical.

explanations.A: This is a true statement. Arrangements for alternative facilities as a disaster recovery site and offsite storage of the company’s databases are a very important part of the disaster recovery plan. An alternative facility might be a different facility owned by the company, or it might be a facility contracted for by the company. The different locations should be a significant distance away from the original processing site.
explanations.B: This is a true statement. The following should be included in the disaster recover y plan: Which employees will participate in disaster recovery and their responsibilities. One person should oversee disaster recovery, and another should be second in command. What hardware, software, and facilities will be used. The priority of applications that should be processed.
explanations.C: This is a true statement. An organization should have a formal disaster recovery plan that is thoroughly documented and approved to fall back on in the event of a hurricane, fire, earthquake, flood, or criminal or terrorist act. A disaster recovery plan specifies: Which employees will participate in disaster recovery and their responsibilities. One person should oversee disaster recovery, and another should be second in command. What hardware, software, and facilities will be used. The priority of applications that should be processed. Personnel should be trained in emergency procedures and re-training should be done regularly to keep their knowledge fresh. The disaster recovery plan should be tested periodically by simulating a disaster to reveal any weaknesses in the plan. This test should be conducted using typical volumes, and processing times should be recorded. The disaster recovery plan should be reviewed regularly and revised when necessary because organizational and operational changes made that have not been incorporated into the recovery plan could make the recovery plan unusable.

question: Grocery Co. has had to pull their backup files from an off-site location and restore them due to a flood that destroyed their on-site data. They pulled the file with an external label for the most recent backup. Instead, they find that the backup is a blank tape and they are unable to locate the proper tape. Which controls can Grocery Co. implement so that they will be able to find the correct data in the future?

options.A: File structure that includes duplication of critical fields.
options.B: Tape management systems such as the grandparent/parent/child concept.
options.C: Storage of the file and its backup together in a secure place.
options.D: Additional external labeling containing further file details.

correctExplanation: In grandparent-parent-child processing, data files from previous periods are retained and if a file is damaged during updating, or if the current backup file is unusable, the previous data files can be used to reconstruct a new backup or current file. Like backup media, these files should also be stored off-premises.

explanations.A: A file structure that includes duplication of critical fields would not compensate for a blank backup file. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.C: A file and its backup should be stored in separate locations. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.D: Additional external labeling containing further file details would not compensate for a blank backup file. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

studyUnit: Study Unit 10: E.2. Business Continuity Planning

question: Contingency plans for information systems should include appropriate backup agreements. Which of the following arrangements would be considered too vendor-dependent when vital operations require almost immediate availability of computer resources?

options.A: A "hot site" arrangement.
options.B: Using excess capacity at another data center within the organization.
options.C: A "cold and hot site" combination arrangement.
options.D: A "cold site" arrangement.

correctExplanation: A "cold site" is a facility where power and space are available to install processing equipment, but it is not immediately available. If an organization uses a cold site, its disaster recovery plan must include arrangements to get computer equipment installed there quickly. Thus, a "cold site" arrangement is too vendor-dependent because the company has to rely on vendors for timely delivery of the equipment.

explanations.A: A "hot site" arrangement must be fully operational and immediately available. A "hot site" arrangement cannot be too vendor-dependent.
explanations.B: Using excess capacity at another data center within the organization ensures that assets needed for backup are available. Thus, it is not too vendor-dependent.
explanations.C: A "cold and hot site" combination arrangement is where the hot site is first used until the cold site is prepared. Thus, it is not too vendor-dependent.

studyUnit: Study Unit 10: E.2. Business Continuity Planning

question: A company is following a plan to continue operations if a place of business is affected by disasters. The plan is most likely called

options.A: crisis communication planning.
options.B: business continuity planning.
options.C: strategic planning.
options.D: continuous availability planning.

correctExplanation: This is a definition of a business continuity plan. Business continuity planning involves defining the risks facing a company in the event of a disaster, assessing those risks, creating procedures to mitigate those risks, regularly testing those procedures to ensure that they work as expected, and periodically reviewing the procedures to make sure that they are up to date.

explanations.A: This is not a crisis communication plan. A crisis communication plan is the policies and procedures for the coordination of communications both internally and externally in the event of an emergency or a negative situation that requires a public response, such as the accessing of confidential company data by a hacker.
explanations.C: This is not a description of strategic planning. Strategic planning is the formulation of strategies, or actions, to take to increase the company's performance.
explanations.D: This is not a description of continuous availability planning. Continuous availability describes the information technology methods used to ensure business continuity in the event of a disaster. While continuous availability is an important part of a plan to continue operations if a place of business is affected by a disaster, it is not the full plan.

studyUnit: Study Unit 10: E.2. Business Continuity Planning

question: When attempting to restore computing facilities at an alternate site following a disaster, which one of the following should be restored first?

options.A: Batch system.
options.B: Operating system.
options.C: Online system.
options.D: Decision support system.

correctExplanation: The operating system should be restored first, because without the operating system, none of the other applications can be run. The operating system serves the following functions: It provides the user interface that allows the user to communicate with the computer in order to load programs, access files, and accomplish other tasks. It provides resource management to manage the hardware and networking resources of the system. It contains file management programs that control the creation, deletion and access of files and also keep track of the physical locations of files on secondary storage devices. It includes task management programs to manage the accomplishment of the computing tasks. This enables multitasking capability, so that several computing tasks, for example keyboarding and printing, can take place at the same time. It provides utilities and support service to perform housekeeping tasks and file conversion functions such as data backup, data recovery, virus protection, data compression and file defragmentation.

explanations.A: A batch system is not a system to be restored at all. The term "batch system" describes a type of transaction processing system. In a batch system, transactions of a similar type (i.e., accounts receivable receipts) are accumulated over a period of time such as a day, and then the whole batch is processed to update the master files.
explanations.C: An online system is not the system to restore first. An online system would not be usable if it were restored first.
explanations.D: A decision support system is not the system to restore first. A decision support system would not be usable if it were restored first.

question: Which one of the following would most compromise the use of backups as protection against loss or damage of master files?

options.A: Storing of all files in one location.
options.B: Use of magnetic tape.
options.C: Failure to encrypt data.
options.D: Inadequate ventilation.

correctExplanation: Storing all files in one location undermines the concept of multiple backups inherent in the grandparent-parent-child principle.

explanations.B: The use of magnetic tape is not the greatest risk to using backups as protection against loss or damage of master files.
explanations.C: The failure to encrypt data is not the greatest risk to using backups as protection against loss or damage of master files.
explanations.D: Inadequate ventilation is not the greatest risk to using backups as protection against loss or damage of master files.

To reveal any weaknesses in the plan, the testing should simulate a disaster. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

question: The primary objective of a disaster recovery plan is to

options.A: set up and be able to operate a cold site if disaster damages important assets.
options.B: ensure employees and assets are safe when a disaster affects the business.
options.C: minimize the effects of a disaster on business operations and productivity.
options.D: plan for a disaster that may destroy the building with an alternative office space.

correctExplanation: This is the primary objective of a disaster recovery plan. Without the ability to recover from a disaster, a company could be out of business.

explanations.A: This is not the primary objective of a disaster recovery plan. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.
explanations.B: This is the objective of business continuity planning. A disaster recovery plan is a part of business continuity planning. However, business continuity planning is more than just disaster planning. The purpose of a disaster recovery plan is to minimize the effects of the disaster on business operations and productivity.
explanations.D: This is not the primary objective of a disaster recovery plan. Please see the correct answer explanation for more information.

question: Many organizations are critically dependent on information systems to support daily business operations. Consequently, an organization may incur significant loss of revenues or incur significant expenses if a disaster such as a hurricane or power outage causes information systems processing to be delayed or interrupted. A bank, for example, may incur significant penalties as a result of missed payments. Which of the following management activities is essential to ensure continuity of operations in the event a disaster or catastrophe impairs information systems processing?

options.A: Review of insurance coverage.
options.B: Change control procedures.
options.C: Contingency planning.
options.D: Electronic vaulting.

correctExplanation: Contingency planning is a management activity which is essential to ensure continuity of operations in the event a disaster impairs information systems processing.

explanations.A: Review of insurance coverage is an aspect of risk analysis, and a much narrower concept than contingency planning.
explanations.B: Change control procedures do not ensure continuity of operations.
explanations.D: Electronic vaulting is a technology that may be used to address contingency planning issues.

question: A critical aspect of a disaster recovery plan is to be able to regain operational capability as soon as possible. In order to accomplish this, an organization can have an arrangement with its computer hardware vendor to have a fully operational facility available that is configured to the user's specific needs. This is best known as a(n)

options.A: Parallel system.
options.B: Hot site.
options.C: Cold site.
options.D: Uninterruptible power system.

correctExplanation: A hot site is a backup facility that has a computer system that is similar to the one used regularly and is fully operational and thus immediately available.

explanations.A: A parallel system is a system that is identical to the main system.
explanations.C: A cold site is a facility that can be used to install computer equipment if needed, but it is not fully operational.
explanations.D: An uninterruptible power system (UPS) is a backup power source that kicks in automatically in the event of a power outage to prevent loss of data.

question: An owner of a company has entered into a contract with a hardware vendor ensuring that in the event of a disaster, the vendor would provide the company with computer equipment. options.A: Hot site.

It is fully operational and immediately available, with all necessary telecommunications hookups for online processing. It also has current, live data being replicated to it in real time from the live site by automated data communications.
explanations.C: This situation does not describe a mirrored data center.
